title.raw: 卷48 高允 Volume 48: Gao Yun

sentences.zh: 高允，字伯恭，勃海人也。

translations.literal: Gao Yun, styled Bogong, was a man of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yun, whose courtesy name was Bogong, came from Bohai.

sentences.zh: 祖泰，在叔父湖傳。

translations.literal: His grandfather Tai is treated in the biography of his uncle Hu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Tai is discussed in the biography of his uncle Hu.

sentences.zh: 父韜，少以英朗知名，同郡封懿雅相敬慕。

translations.literal: His father Tao was in youth renowned for brilliance and clarity; Feng Yi of the same commandery admired and respected each other in refined friendship.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tao won early fame for his keen intelligence and open manner; he and Feng Yi of the same commandery held each other in deep mutual esteem.

sentences.zh: 為慕容垂太尉從事中郎。

translations.literal: He served as Attendant Gentleman in the office of the Grand Commandant under Murong Chui.
translations.idiomatic: He served Murong Chui as an attendant gentleman in the office of the grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 太祖平中山，以韜為丞相參軍。

translations.literal: When the Taizu Emperor pacified Zhongshan, Tao was made Army Advisor to the Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Daowu conquered Zhongshan, Tao was appointed an army adviser on the chancellor's staff.

sentences.zh: 早卒。

translations.literal: He died young.
translations.idiomatic: He died at an early age.

sentences.zh: 允少孤夙成，有奇度，清河崔玄伯見而異之，歎曰：「高子黃中內潤，文明外照，必為一代偉器，但恐吾不見耳。」

translations.literal: Yun lost his parents early yet matured quickly and possessed unusual capacity. Cui Xuanbo of Qinghe saw him and marveled, exclaiming: "Master Gao is yellow at the center and lustrous within, civil brilliance shining without—he is sure to become a monumental vessel of his age, though I fear I may not live to see it."
translations.idiomatic: Yun was orphaned young yet precocious, with an uncommon breadth of mind. When Cui Xuanbo of Qinghe met him he was struck with wonder and sighed: "Young Gao is golden at the core and radiant within, his civil brilliance shining outward—he is bound to be a pillar of his generation, though I fear I shall not live to see it."

sentences.zh: 年十餘，奉祖父喪還本郡，推財與二弟而為沙門，名法淨。

translations.literal: At just over ten years of age, he escorted his grandfather's coffin back to his home commandery, turned over his share of the family property to his two younger brothers, and became a Buddhist monk under the name Fajing.
translations.idiomatic: When he was barely into his teens, he brought his grandfather's coffin home to their commandery, gave his inheritance to his two younger brothers, and entered the clergy under the name Fajing.

sentences.zh: 未久而罷。

translations.literal: Before long he quit.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he left the monastic life.

sentences.zh: 性好文學，擔笈負書，千里就業。

translations.literal: By nature he loved literary study; carrying books on his back in a satchel, he traveled a thousand li to pursue learning.
translations.idiomatic: He loved scholarship by nature, shouldered his book-box, and traveled a thousand li to study under masters.

sentences.zh: 博通經史天文術數，尤好春秋公羊。

translations.literal: He mastered the classics, histories, astronomy, and numerology, especially favoring the Gongyang Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: He gained a thorough command of the classics and histories, astronomy and numerology, and was especially devoted to the Gongyang tradition of the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 郡召功曹。

translations.literal: The commandery summoned him as Merit Officer.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery recruited him as merit officer.

sentences.zh: 神䴥三年，世祖舅陽平王杜超行征南大將軍，鎮鄴，以允為從事中郎，年四十餘矣。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shenqi, the Emperor's maternal uncle, the Prince of Yangping, Du Chao, served as Acting Grand General Who Pacifies the South and garrisoned Ye; he appointed Yun as Attendant Gentleman when Yun was already over forty.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Shenqi reign, the emperor's uncle by marriage, Du Chao, Prince of Yangping, held the post of acting grand general who pacifies the south and garrisoned Ye; he made Yun his attendant gentleman when Yun was already past forty.

sentences.zh: 超以方春而諸州囚多不決，乃表允與中郎呂熙等分詣諸州，共評獄事。

translations.literal: Since it was spring and many prisoners throughout the provinces remained unresolved, Chao memorialized that Yun, together with the Gentleman Lü Xi and others, should go separately to the various provinces to review criminal cases jointly.
translations.idiomatic: Because it was spring and prisoners in many provinces still awaited judgment, Chao memorialized that Yun, together with the gentleman Lü Xi and others, should each go to different provinces and jointly review criminal cases.

sentences.zh: 熙等皆以貪穢得罪，唯允以清平獲賞。

translations.literal: Xi and the rest were all punished for greed and corruption, while Yun alone received reward for his impartiality and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Xi and the others were all punished for corruption, while Yun alone was rewarded for his fair and upright conduct.

sentences.zh: 府解，還家教授，受業者千餘人。

translations.literal: When his post in the office ended, he returned home to teach; more than a thousand students received instruction from him.
translations.idiomatic: When his term in the office ended, he went home to teach, and more than a thousand students studied under him.

sentences.zh: 四年，與盧玄等俱被徵，拜中書博士。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was summoned together with Lu Xuan and others and appointed Doctor of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was summoned to court together with Lu Xuan and others and appointed a doctor of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 遷侍郎，與太原張偉並以本官領衞大將軍、樂安王範從事中郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Gentleman Attendant and, together with Zhang Wei of Taiyuan in their original offices, served as Attendant Gentleman to the General-in-Chief Who Guards the Army, the Prince of Le'an, Fan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to gentleman attendant and, together with Zhang Wei of Taiyuan, retained his original rank while serving as attendant gentleman on the staff of Fan, Prince of Le'an, general-in-chief who guards the army.

sentences.zh: 範，世祖之寵弟，西鎮長安，允甚有匡益，秦人稱之。

translations.literal: Fan, a favored younger brother of the Shizu Emperor, held Chang'an as western garrison; Yun was of great help in setting matters right, and the people of Qin praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Fan, a favored younger brother of Emperor Taiwu, held Chang'an in the west; Yun gave him strong counsel and the people of Qin praised him.

sentences.zh: 尋被徵還。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 允曾作塞上翁詩，有混欣戚，遺得喪之致。

translations.literal: Yun had once composed a poem on the Old Man of the Frontier, blending joy and sorrow and conveying the spirit of forgetting gain and loss.
translations.idiomatic: Yun had once written a poem on the old man by the frontier pass, blending joy and grief and capturing the spirit of letting go of gain and loss.

sentences.zh: 驃騎大將軍、樂平王丕西討上邽，復以本官參丕軍事。

translations.literal: The General of Agile Cavalry, the Prince of Leiping, Pi, campaigned west against Shanggui; Yun again served in his army staff in his original office.
translations.idiomatic: When Pi, Prince of Leiping and general of agile cavalry, marched west against Shanggui, Yun again joined his staff in his former capacity.

sentences.zh: 語在丕傳。

translations.literal: The account is given in Pi's biography.
translations.idiomatic: The full account appears in Pi's biography.

sentences.zh: 涼州平，以參謀之勳，賜爵汶陽子，加建武將軍。

translations.literal: When Liang province was pacified, for his merit as staff planner he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wenyangzi and given the additional title General Who Establishes Martiality.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang province was pacified, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wenyangzi and given the additional title general who establishes martiality for his service as a staff planner.

sentences.zh: 後詔允與司徒崔浩述成國記，以本官領著作郎。

translations.literal: Later an edict ordered Yun, together with the Minister of Education Cui Hao, to compile the National History; he held his original office while serving as Editorial Director.
translations.idiomatic: Later an edict directed Yun and Minister of Education Cui Hao to compile the national history; Yun retained his original post while serving as editorial director.

sentences.zh: 時浩集諸術士，考校漢元以來，日月薄蝕、五星行度，并識前史之失，別為魏曆，以示允。

translations.literal: At that time Hao gathered various specialists to examine solar and lunar eclipses and the motions of the five planets from the Yuan period of Han onward, to identify errors in earlier histories, and to devise a separate Wei calendar, which he showed to Yun.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Hao assembled various experts to verify solar and lunar eclipses and the courses of the five planets from the Han Yuan period onward, to note errors in earlier histories, and to draft a separate Wei calendar, which he showed Yun.

sentences.zh: 允曰：「天文曆數不可空論。

translations.literal: Yun said: "Astronomical chronology cannot be discussed in empty words.
translations.idiomatic: Yun said, "Astronomy and calendrical reckoning cannot be argued in the abstract.

sentences.zh: 夫善言遠者必先驗於近。

translations.literal: One who speaks well of distant matters must first verify them in what is near.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever speaks well of distant things must first test them against what is near at hand.

sentences.zh: 且漢元年冬十月，五星聚於東井，此乃曆術之淺。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the tenth month of the first year of Han, the five planets gathered in the Well Mansion—this is a shallow point in calendrical astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the record that in the tenth month of the first year of Han the five planets gathered in the Well Mansion shows a shallow grasp of calendrical science.

sentences.zh: 今譏漢史，而不覺此謬，恐後人譏今猶今之譏古。」

translations.literal: Now you criticize the Han histories yet do not notice this error; I fear later men will criticize the present just as we criticize antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: You now fault the Han histories yet miss this error yourself; I fear posterity will fault our age just as we fault antiquity.

sentences.zh: 浩曰：「所謬云何？」

translations.literal: Hao said: "In what does the error consist?"
translations.idiomatic: Hao asked, "What is the error?"

sentences.zh: 允曰：「案星傳，金水二星常附日而行。

translations.literal: Yun said: "According to the star canon, Mercury and Venus constantly follow the sun in their course.
translations.idiomatic: Yun replied, "According to the star canon, Mercury and Venus normally travel with the sun.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，日在尾箕，[1]昏沒於申南，而東井方出於寅北。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, the sun is in the Tail and Winnowing Basket; at dusk it sets south of Shen, while the Well Mansion is just rising north of Yin.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the sun stands in the Tail and Winnowing Basket; at dusk it sets south of Shen, while the Well Mansion is just rising north of Yin.

sentences.zh: 二星何因背日而行？

translations.literal: How could the two planets turn their backs on the sun and move?
translations.idiomatic: How could those two planets turn away from the sun and travel on their own?

sentences.zh: 是史官欲神其事，不復推之於理。」

translations.literal: The historians wished to magnify the event and did not reason it through.
translations.idiomatic: The historians wished to make the event miraculous and never reasoned it through.

sentences.zh: 浩曰：「欲為變者何所不可，君獨不疑三星之聚，而怪二星之來？」

translations.literal: Hao said: "When one wishes to make an omen, what may not be done? You alone do not doubt the gathering of three stars yet find two stars' arrival strange?"
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "When one wishes to fashion an omen, what may not be done? You alone do not doubt the gathering of three stars, yet you find two stars' arrival strange?"

sentences.zh: 允曰：「此不可以空言爭，宜更審之。」

translations.literal: Yun said: "This cannot be argued in mere words; it should be examined more carefully."
translations.idiomatic: Yun said, "This cannot be settled by words alone; it should be examined again with care."

sentences.zh: 時坐者咸怪，唯東宮少傅游雅曰：「高君長於曆數，當不虛也。」

translations.literal: Those present were all astonished; only You Ya, Junior Tutor of the Eastern Palace, said: "Master Gao excels in chronology and astronomy; he surely will not speak vainly."
translations.idiomatic: Those present were all astonished; only You Ya, junior tutor of the eastern palace, said, "Master Gao excels in calendrical reckoning—he surely does not speak idly."

sentences.zh: 後歲餘，浩謂允曰：「先所論者，本不注心，及更考究，果如君語，以前三月聚於東井，非十月也。」

translations.literal: More than a year later Hao told Yun: "What we discussed before—I had not truly applied my mind; on further investigation it was indeed as you said: the gathering in the Well Mansion occurred in the third month, not the tenth."
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later Hao told Yun, "What we discussed before—I had not really attended to it; on further study it was indeed as you said: the gathering in the Well Mansion was in the third month, not the tenth."

sentences.zh: 又謂雅曰：「高允之術，陽元之射也。」

translations.literal: He also told Ya: "Gao Yun's art is Yang Xiong's archery."
translations.idiomatic: He also told Ya, "Gao Yun's skill is like Yang Xiong's archery."

sentences.zh: 眾乃歎服。

translations.literal: The assembly then sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: The company then sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 允雖明於曆數，初不推步，有所論說。

translations.literal: Though Yun understood chronology and astronomy, at first he did not perform step-by-step calculations for what he discussed.
translations.idiomatic: Though Yun understood calendrical reckoning, he did not at first perform step-by-step calculations for what he discussed.

sentences.zh: 唯游雅數以災異問允。

translations.literal: Only You Ya repeatedly asked Yun about portents and anomalies.
translations.idiomatic: Only You Ya repeatedly questioned Yun about omens and anomalies.

sentences.zh: 允曰：「昔人有言，知之甚難，既知復恐漏泄，不如不知也。

translations.literal: Yun said: "Men of old have said: to know such things is very hard; once known, one fears disclosure—better not to know.
translations.idiomatic: Yun said, "Men of old said that to know such things is very hard, and once known one fears disclosure—better not to know at all.

sentences.zh: 天下妙理至多，何遽問此。」

translations.literal: Subtle principles in the world are exceedingly many; why press this question alone?"
translations.idiomatic: Subtle principles in the world are beyond number—why press this question alone?"

sentences.zh: 雅乃止。

translations.literal: Ya then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: You Ya then ceased asking.

sentences.zh: 尋以本官為秦王翰傅。

translations.literal: Before long, in his original office he became Tutor to the Prince of Qin, Han.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed, in his existing rank, tutor to Han, Prince of Qin.

sentences.zh: 後敕以經授恭宗，甚見禮待。

translations.literal: Later an edict had him teach the Classics to Crown Prince Chongzong; he was greatly honored and treated with ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Later an edict had him instruct Crown Prince Huang in the classics, and he was treated with great respect.

sentences.zh: 又詔允與侍郎公孫質、李虛、[2]胡方回共定律令。

translations.literal: Another edict ordered Yun, together with Gentlemen Attendant Gongsun Zhi, Li Xu, and Hu Fanghui, jointly to codify laws and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict directed Yun, together with the gentlemen attendant Gongsun Zhi, Li Xu, and Hu Fanghui, to draft laws and ordinances jointly.

sentences.zh: 世祖引允與論刑政，言甚稱旨。

translations.literal: The Shizu Emperor drew Yun in to discuss criminal administration; his words were highly pleasing.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu drew Yun into discussion of criminal policy, and his words greatly pleased the emperor.

sentences.zh: 因問允曰：「萬機之務，何者為先？」

translations.literal: He then asked Yun: "Among the myriad affairs of state, which should come first?"
translations.idiomatic: He then asked Yun, "Among the myriad affairs of state, which should come first?"

sentences.zh: 是時多禁封良田，又京師遊食者眾。

translations.literal: At that time many prohibitions sealed off fertile fields, and in the capital there were many who lived idly without labor.
translations.idiomatic: At that time fertile land was widely sealed off by prohibition, and in the capital many lived idly without working the fields.

sentences.zh: 允因言曰：「臣少也賤，所知唯田，請言農事。

translations.literal: Yun therefore said: "In my youth I was lowly; what I know is only farming—allow me to speak of agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Yun therefore said, "In my youth I was of humble station; what I know is farming alone—allow me to speak of agriculture.

sentences.zh: 古人云：方一里則為田三頃七十畝，百里則田三萬七千頃。

translations.literal: The ancients said: within one square li there are seventy-three acres per three qing of fields; for a hundred li there are thirty-seven thousand qing of fields.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said that within one square li there are three qing and seventy mu of fields, and within a hundred li there are thirty-seven thousand qing of fields.

sentences.zh: 若勤之，則畝益三斗，不勤則畝損三斗。

translations.literal: If cultivated diligently, each mu gains three dou; if not cultivated diligently, each mu loses three dou.
translations.idiomatic: If worked diligently, each mu yields three dou more; if neglected, each mu loses three dou.

sentences.zh: [3]方百里損益之率，為粟二百二十二萬斛，況以天下之廣乎？

translations.literal: For a region a hundred li square, the gain or loss amounts to 2,220,000 hu of grain—how much more for the breadth of the empire?
translations.idiomatic: For a region a hundred li on a side, the difference in gain or loss amounts to 2,220,000 hu of grain—how much more for the breadth of the realm?

sentences.zh: 若公私有儲，雖遇飢年，復何憂哉？」

translations.literal: If public and private stores are filled, even in years of famine what worry remains?"
translations.idiomatic: If public and private granaries are full, what worry remains even in years of famine?"

sentences.zh: 世祖善之。

translations.literal: The Shizu Emperor approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his counsel.

sentences.zh: 遂除田禁，悉以授民。

translations.literal: Thereupon field prohibitions were lifted and all land was granted to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the prohibitions on farmland were lifted and all such land was granted to the people.

sentences.zh: 初，崔浩薦冀、定、相、幽、并五州之士數十人，各起家郡守。

translations.literal: Earlier, Cui Hao had recommended several tens of scholars from the five provinces Ji, Ding, Xiang, You, and Bing, each to begin their careers as commandery governors.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Cui Hao had recommended several dozen scholars from Ji, Ding, Xiang, You, and Bing provinces, each to begin his career as a commandery governor.

sentences.zh: 恭宗謂浩曰：「先召之人，亦州郡選也，在職已久，勤勞未答。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Chongzong said to Hao: "Those summoned before were also provincial selections; they have long held office without reward for their toil.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Huang said to Hao, "Those summoned earlier were also chosen by the provinces; they have long served without reward for their labor.

sentences.zh: 今可先補前召外任郡縣，以新召者代為郎吏。

translations.literal: Now we may first assign those previously summoned to external posts in commanderies and counties, and let the newly summoned replace them as court clerks.
translations.idiomatic: We may now first assign those previously summoned to posts in commanderies and counties outside the capital, and let the newly summoned take their places as court clerks.

sentences.zh: 又守令宰民，宜使更事者。」

translations.literal: Moreover, for commandery governors and magistrates who oversee the people, men with governing experience should be sent."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, for prefects and magistrates who govern the people, men with prior administrative experience should be appointed."

sentences.zh: 浩固爭而遣之。

translations.literal: Hao stubbornly argued and sent them off anyway.
translations.idiomatic: Hao stubbornly opposed the plan and sent them off anyway.

sentences.zh: 允聞之，謂東宮博士管恬曰：「崔公其不免乎！

translations.literal: When Yun heard of it he said to the Eastern Palace Doctor Guan Tian: "Will not Lord Cui avoid disaster!
translations.idiomatic: When Yun heard of this he said to Guan Tian, doctor of the eastern palace, "Lord Cui will surely not escape disaster!

sentences.zh: 苟逞其非，而校勝於上，何以勝濟。」

translations.literal: If he indulges what is wrong and contests victory with his sovereign above, how can victory sustain him?"
translations.idiomatic: If he indulges his error and contests victory with his sovereign above, how can such victory save him?"

sentences.zh: 遼東公翟黑子有寵於世祖，奉使并州，受布千匹，事尋發覺。

translations.literal: At that time the Duke of Liaodong, Zhai Heizi, was favored by the Shizu Emperor; on mission to Bing province he accepted a thousand bolts of cloth, and the matter was soon discovered.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhai Heizi, Duke of Liaodong, enjoyed the emperor's favor; on a mission to Bing province he accepted a thousand bolts of cloth, and the affair was soon exposed.

sentences.zh: 黑子請計於允曰：「主上問我，為首為諱乎？」

translations.literal: Heizi asked Yun's counsel: "When the sovereign questions me, should I confess first or conceal first?"
translations.idiomatic: Heizi asked Yun's advice: "When the sovereign questions me, should I confess first or conceal the matter?"

sentences.zh: 允曰：「公帷幄寵臣，答詔宜實。

translations.literal: Yun said: "You are a cherished minister within the imperial curtains; in answering the edict you should speak truthfully.
translations.idiomatic: Yun said, "You are a cherished minister at the emperor's side; in answering the edict you should speak truthfully.

sentences.zh: 又自告忠誠，罪必無慮。」

translations.literal: Moreover, by confessing of your own accord you show loyalty; punishment is sure to be no concern."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, by confessing of your own accord you show loyalty, and you need not fear punishment."

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎崔覽、公孫質等咸言首實罪不可測，宜諱之。

translations.literal: The Gentleman Attendant Cui Lan, Gongsun Zhi, and others all said that for a voluntary confession the penalty could not be foreseen and concealment was better.
translations.idiomatic: The gentleman attendant Cui Lan, Gongsun Zhi, and others all said that voluntary confession made the penalty unpredictable and that he should conceal the matter.

sentences.zh: 黑子以覽等為親己，而反怒允曰：「如君言，誘我死，何其不直！」

translations.literal: Heizi took Lan and the others as siding with him, yet turned in anger on Yun: "As you advise, you lure me to death—how lacking in straight dealing!"
translations.idiomatic: Heizi took Lan and the others as favoring him, yet turned on Yun in anger and said, "As you counsel, you would lure me to my death—how lacking in honesty!"

sentences.zh: 遂與允絕。

translations.literal: He thereupon broke with Yun.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon broke off relations with Yun.

sentences.zh: 黑子以不實對，竟為世祖所疏，終獲罪戮。

translations.literal: Heizi answered untruthfully and was eventually estranged by the Shizu Emperor; in the end he suffered execution.
translations.idiomatic: Heizi answered untruthfully, was eventually estranged by the emperor, and in the end was put to death.

sentences.zh: 是時，著作令史閔湛、郄𢷋性巧佞，為浩信待。

translations.literal: At that time the Editorial Clerk Min Zhan and Qie were clever flatterers trusted by Hao.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the editorial clerks Min Zhan and Qie were clever flatterers in whom Hao placed his trust.

sentences.zh: 見浩所注詩、論語、尚書、易，遂上疏，言馬、鄭、王、賈雖注述六經，並多疏謬，不如浩之精微。

translations.literal: Seeing Hao's commentaries on the Odes, Analects, Documents, and Changes, they submitted a memorial stating that Ma, Zheng, Wang, and Jia, though they commented on the Six Classics, were largely in error and coarse—not as subtle as Hao's work.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Hao's commentaries on the Odes, Analects, Documents, and Changes, they submitted a memorial saying that Ma, Zheng, Wang, and Jia, though they had commented on the Six Classics, were full of errors and lapses and were not as subtle as Hao's work.

sentences.zh: 乞收境內諸書，藏之祕府。

translations.literal: They begged to collect all books within the realm and store them in the secret archive.
translations.idiomatic: They asked that all books within the realm be collected and stored in the imperial archive.

sentences.zh: 班浩所注，命天下習業。

translations.literal: They ordered Hao's commentaries promulgated and commanded the empire to study them.
translations.idiomatic: They proposed that Hao's commentaries be promulgated and that the empire be ordered to study them.

sentences.zh: 并求敕浩注禮傳，令後生得觀正義。

translations.literal: They also asked that Hao be ordered to comment on the Rites transmission so that later students might behold correct meaning.
translations.idiomatic: They also asked that Hao be ordered to comment on the Rites so that later students might see correct doctrine.

sentences.zh: 浩亦表薦湛有著述之才。

translations.literal: Hao also memorialized recommending Zhan's talent for composition.
translations.idiomatic: Hao also memorialized recommending Zhan's talent for writing.

sentences.zh: 既而勸浩刊所撰國史于石，用垂不朽，欲以彰浩直筆之跡。

translations.literal: Before long they urged Hao to inscribe the compiled National History on stone for lasting immortality, wishing to manifest Hao's record of straight writing.
translations.idiomatic: Before long they urged Hao to carve the national history he had compiled on stone so that it would endure forever, wishing to display Hao's record of the straight brush.

sentences.zh: 允聞之，謂著作郎宗欽曰：「閔湛所營，分寸之間，恐為崔門萬世之禍。

translations.literal: When Yun heard of it he said to the Editorial Gentleman Zong Qin: "What Min Zhan is doing—in a hair's breadth—may become calamity for ten thousand generations of the Cui house.
translations.idiomatic: When Yun heard of this he said to Zong Qin, editorial gentleman, "What Min Zhan is undertaking, in the space of a hair's breadth, may become calamity for ten thousand generations of the Cui clan.

sentences.zh: 吾徒無類矣。」

translations.literal: Our sort are done for."
translations.idiomatic: Our sort are finished."

sentences.zh: 未幾而難作。

translations.literal: Before long disaster broke out.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the catastrophe broke out.

sentences.zh: 初，浩之被收也，允直中書省。

translations.literal: When Hao was first arrested, Yun was on duty in the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao was first arrested, Yun was on duty at the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 恭宗使東宮侍郎吳延召允，仍留宿宮內。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Chongzong sent the Eastern Palace Gentleman Attendant Wu Yan to summon Yun and detained him overnight in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Huang sent Wu Yan, gentleman attendant of the eastern palace, to summon Yun and kept him overnight in the palace.

sentences.zh: 翌日，恭宗入奏世祖，命允驂乘。

translations.literal: The next day Chongzong entered to report to the Shizu Emperor and ordered Yun to ride in the equerry's carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the crown prince entered to report to the emperor and ordered Yun to ride beside him in the carriage.

sentences.zh: 至宮門，謂曰：「入當見至尊，吾自導卿。

translations.literal: At the palace gate he said: "When you enter you will see His Majesty; I myself will guide you.
translations.idiomatic: At the palace gate he said, "When you enter you will see His Majesty; I myself will guide you.

sentences.zh: 脫至尊有問，但依吾語。」

translations.literal: If the Emperor questions you, only follow my words."
translations.idiomatic: If His Majesty questions you, speak only as I have told you."

sentences.zh: 允請曰：「為何等事也？」

translations.literal: Yun asked: "What sort of affair is this?"
translations.idiomatic: Yun asked, "What sort of affair is this?"

sentences.zh: 恭宗曰：「入自知之。」

translations.literal: Chongzong said: "You will know when you enter."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince said, "You will know when you enter."

sentences.zh: 既入見帝。

translations.literal: When he had entered to see the Emperor—
translations.idiomatic: When he had entered to see the emperor—

sentences.zh: 恭宗曰：「中書侍郎高允自在臣宮，同處累年，小心密慎，臣所委悉。

translations.literal: Chongzong said: "Gentleman Attendant of the Palace Library Gao Yun has long been in my household these many years, careful and discreet; I know well what I entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince said, "Gentleman attendant Gao Yun has long been in my household these many years, careful and discreet in all things—I know him well.

sentences.zh: 雖與浩同事，然允微賤，制由於浩。

translations.literal: Though he worked with Hao, Yun was of humble rank and was constrained by Hao's authority.
translations.idiomatic: Though he worked with Hao, Yun was of humble rank and acted under Hao's direction.

sentences.zh: 請赦其命。」

translations.literal: I beg that his life be spared."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that his life be spared."

sentences.zh: 世祖召允，謂曰：「國書皆崔浩作不？」

translations.literal: The Shizu Emperor summoned Yun and asked: "Was the National History entirely the work of Cui Hao?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Yun and asked, "Was the national history entirely the work of Cui Hao?"

sentences.zh: 允對曰：「太祖記，前著作郎鄧淵所撰。

translations.literal: Yun answered: "The Annals of the Taizu Emperor were composed by the former Editorial Gentleman Deng Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yun answered, "The annals of Emperor Daowu were composed by the former editorial gentleman Deng Yuan.

sentences.zh: 先帝記及今記，臣與浩同作。

translations.literal: The Annals of the late Emperor and the present record I composed together with Hao.
translations.idiomatic: The annals of the late emperor and the present record I composed together with Hao.

sentences.zh: 然浩綜務處多，總裁而已。

translations.literal: Yet Hao handled many comprehensive duties and only supervised as chief coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Hao handled many other duties and served chiefly as general editor.

sentences.zh: 至於注疏，臣多於浩。」

translations.literal: As for annotations and commentaries, I contributed more than Hao.
translations.idiomatic: As for annotations and commentaries, I contributed more than Hao.

sentences.zh: 世祖大怒曰：「此甚於浩，安有生路！」

translations.literal: The Shizu Emperor said in great anger: "This is even worse than Hao—how can there be a way to live!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor burst out in fury: "This is even worse than Hao—how could he be allowed to live!"

sentences.zh: 恭宗曰：「天威嚴重，允是小臣，迷亂失次耳。

translations.literal: Chongzong said: "Heaven's majesty is severe; Yun is a petty official who was confused and lost composure.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince said, "Heaven's majesty is overwhelming; Yun is a minor official who lost his composure in confusion.

sentences.zh: 臣向備問，皆云浩作。」

translations.literal: When I questioned him earlier, he all said Hao wrote it."
translations.idiomatic: When I questioned him earlier, he said it was all Hao's work."

sentences.zh: 世祖問：「如東宮言不？」

translations.literal: The Shizu Emperor asked: "Is it as the Eastern Palace says?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Is it as the eastern palace says?"

sentences.zh: 允曰：「臣以下才，謬參著作，犯逆天威，罪應滅族，今已分死，不敢虛妄。

translations.literal: Yun said: "With my low talent I wrongly joined the editorial work, offending heaven's majesty; the crime deserves extermination of the clan. I am already as good as dead and dare not speak falsely.
translations.idiomatic: Yun said, "With my meager talent I wrongly took part in the compilation, offending your majesty; the crime deserves the extinction of my clan. I am already as good as dead and dare not speak falsely.

sentences.zh: 殿下以臣侍講日久，哀臣乞命耳。

translations.literal: Your Highness, because I long served as lecturer, pitied me and begged for my life.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness pitied me and begged for my life only because I had long served as your lecturer.

sentences.zh: 實不問臣，臣無此言。

translations.literal: In truth he did not ask me, and I never said such words.
translations.idiomatic: In truth he never questioned me, and I never spoke those words.

sentences.zh: 臣以實對，不敢迷亂。」

translations.literal: I answer with facts and dare not be confused.
translations.idiomatic: I answer with the facts and dare not speak in confusion.

sentences.zh: 世祖謂恭宗曰：「直哉！

translations.literal: The Shizu Emperor said to Chongzong: "How upright!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to the crown prince, "How upright!

sentences.zh: 此亦人情所難，而能臨死不移，不亦難乎！

translations.literal: This is also what human feeling finds hard, yet able at impending death not to shift—is it not also hard!
translations.idiomatic: This is also what human nature finds hardest, yet he could face death without wavering—is that not also hard!

sentences.zh: 且對君以實，貞臣也。

translations.literal: Moreover, to answer the ruler with truth—he is a loyal minister.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, to answer one's ruler with truth—such a man is a loyal minister.

sentences.zh: 如此言，寧失一有罪，宜宥之。」

translations.literal: With such words, better to lose one guilty man—he should be pardoned."
translations.idiomatic: With such words as his, better to let one guilty man go free—he should be pardoned."

sentences.zh: 允竟得免。

translations.literal: Yun ultimately escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was spared after all.

sentences.zh: 於是召浩前，使人詰浩。

translations.literal: Thereupon Hao was summoned forward and men were sent to interrogate him.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Hao was summoned forward and interrogators were sent to question him.

sentences.zh: 浩惶惑不能對。

translations.literal: Hao was fearful and confused and could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was frightened and confused and could not answer.

sentences.zh: 允事事申明，皆有條理。

translations.literal: Yun explained each matter clearly, all with orderly reasoning.
translations.idiomatic: Yun clarified each matter in turn, all with clear and orderly reasoning.

sentences.zh: 時世祖怒甚，敕允為詔，自浩已下、僮吏已上百二十八人皆夷五族。

translations.literal: At that time the Shizu Emperor was very angry and ordered Yun to draft an edict: from Hao down, servants and clerks numbering one hundred twenty-eight in all were to have their five clans exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and ordered Yun to draft an edict exterminating the five clans of all one hundred twenty-eight persons from Hao down through his servants and clerks.

sentences.zh: 允持疑不為，頻詔催切。

translations.literal: Yun hesitated and would not write; edicts repeatedly urged him urgently.
translations.idiomatic: Yun hesitated and refused to write; edicts repeatedly pressed him with urgency.

sentences.zh: 允乞更一見，然後為詔。

translations.literal: Yun begged for one more audience, then he would draft the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Yun begged for one more audience with the emperor, after which he would draft the edict.

sentences.zh: 詔引前，允曰：「浩之所坐，若更有餘釁，非臣敢知。

translations.literal: Summoned forward by edict, Yun said: "Hao's crime—if there is further guilt beyond this, it is not what I dare know.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned before the emperor, Yun said, "As for Hao's crime, if there is further guilt beyond this, it is not for me to know.

sentences.zh: 直以犯觸，罪不至死。」

translations.literal: Simply for the offense of giving offense, the crime does not reach death."
translations.idiomatic: For the offense of giving offense alone, the crime does not warrant death."

sentences.zh: 世祖怒，命介士執允。

translations.literal: The Shizu Emperor was angry and ordered armored guards to seize Yun.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged and ordered armored guards to seize Yun.

sentences.zh: 恭宗拜請。

translations.literal: Chongzong bowed and pleaded.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince bowed and pleaded on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 世祖曰：「無此人忿朕，當有數千口死矣。」

translations.literal: The Shizu Emperor said: "Without this man resenting me, there would have been several thousand dead."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Without this man's resentment of me, several thousand people would have died."

sentences.zh: 浩竟族滅，餘皆身死。

translations.literal: Hao's clan was ultimately exterminated; the rest all died in person.
translations.idiomatic: Hao's entire clan was exterminated; the rest were put to death.

sentences.zh: 宗欽臨刑，歎曰：「高允其殆聖乎！」

translations.literal: Zong Qin at execution sighed: "Gao Yun is almost a sage!"
translations.idiomatic: At his execution Zong Qin sighed, "Gao Yun is nearly a sage!"

sentences.zh: 恭宗後讓允曰：「人當知機，不知機，學復何益？

translations.literal: Later Chongzong reproached Yun: "A man should know the moment; without knowing the moment, what use is learning?
translations.idiomatic: Later the crown prince reproached Yun: "A man must know when to adapt; without knowing the moment, what good is learning?

sentences.zh: 當爾之時，吾導卿端緒，何故不從人言，怒帝如此。

translations.literal: At that time I guided you to the proper thread—why did you not follow my words and anger the Emperor so?
translations.idiomatic: At that moment I guided you to the right course—why did you not follow my words and provoke the emperor's wrath as you did?

sentences.zh: 每一念之，使人心悸。」

translations.literal: Each time I think of it, it makes the heart tremble.
translations.idiomatic: Each time I think of it, my heart still trembles.

sentences.zh: 允曰：「臣東野凡生，本無宦意。

translations.literal: Yun said: "I am a rustic commoner of the eastern wilds and originally had no wish for office.
translations.idiomatic: Yun said, "I am a rustic commoner from the eastern wilds and never aspired to office.

sentences.zh: 屬休延之會，應旌弓之舉，釋褐鳳池，仍參麟閣，尸素官榮，妨賢已久。

translations.literal: It happened to be a time of peace and extension; I answered the summons of the signal bow, put off my plain cloth at the Phoenix Pool, and still served in the Unicorn Pavilion—holding office in vain, hindering the worthy for long.
translations.idiomatic: By chance it was a time of peace; I answered the imperial summons, entered office at the Secretariat, and still served in the imperial archives—occupying rank without merit and blocking the worthy for long.

sentences.zh: 夫史籍者，帝王之實錄，將來之烱戒，今之所以觀往，後之所以知今。

translations.literal: Historical records are the true record of emperors and kings, bright warnings for the future—by them the present observes the past, and the future knows the present.
translations.idiomatic: Historical records are the true chronicle of emperors and kings, bright warnings for generations to come—by them the present views the past, and the future understands the present.

sentences.zh: 是以言行舉動，莫不備載，故人君慎焉。

translations.literal: Therefore words, deeds, and conduct are all fully recorded, and so rulers are cautious therein.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore words, deeds, and conduct are all fully recorded, and rulers must be cautious in them.

sentences.zh: 然浩世受殊遇，榮曜當時，孤負聖恩，自貽灰滅。

translations.literal: Yet Hao received exceptional favor generation after generation, glory shining in his time; he betrayed the sage grace and brought destruction on himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Hao received exceptional favor in his generation, glory shining in his day; he betrayed the emperor's grace and brought ruin upon himself.

sentences.zh: 即浩之跡，時有可論。

translations.literal: As for Hao's conduct, there are points that may be discussed.
translations.idiomatic: As for Hao's conduct, there are points that may still be debated.

sentences.zh: 浩以蓬蒿之才，荷棟梁之重，在朝無謇諤之節，退私無委蛇之稱，私欲沒其公廉，愛憎蔽其直理，此浩之責也。

translations.literal: Hao with talent fit for wild weeds bore the weight of pillar and beam; in court he had no forthright remonstrance, in private no reputation for flexible courtesy; private desire drowned his public integrity, love and hate blinded his straight judgment—this is Hao's responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Hao, with talent fit only for the wilds, bore the weight of the state's pillars; in court he lacked forthright remonstrance, in private he lacked a reputation for tact; private desire drowned his public integrity, and love and hate blinded his judgment—this was Hao's fault.

sentences.zh: 至於書朝廷起居之跡，言國家得失之事，此亦為史之大體，未為多違。

translations.literal: As for recording the court's daily conduct and speaking of the state's gains and losses, this too is the great substance of history and was not greatly at fault.
translations.idiomatic: As for recording the court's daily conduct and discussing the state's gains and losses, that too is the great substance of history and was not greatly at fault.

sentences.zh: 然臣與浩實同其事，死生榮辱，義無獨殊。

translations.literal: Yet I and Hao truly shared the same task; in life and death, honor and disgrace, by right there is no separate exception.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Hao and I truly shared the same task; in life and death, honor and shame, by right there should be no separate exception for me.

sentences.zh: 誠荷殿下大造之慈，違心苟免，非臣之意。」

translations.literal: I truly bear Your Highness's great grace of creating life anew, but to go against my heart and seek escape by pretense is not my intent.
translations.idiomatic: I am truly grateful for Your Highness's great grace in sparing my life, but to go against my heart and seek escape by pretense is not my intent.

sentences.zh: 恭宗動容稱歎。

translations.literal: Chongzong was moved in countenance and praised him with sighs.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince was moved and sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 允後與人言，我不奉東宮導旨者，恐負翟黑子。

translations.literal: Yun later said to people: "The reason I did not follow the Eastern Palace's guidance was that I feared failing Zhai Heizi."
translations.idiomatic: Yun later told others, "The reason I did not follow the eastern palace's guidance was that I feared betraying Zhai Heizi."

sentences.zh: 恭宗季年，頗親近左右，營立田園，以取其利。

translations.literal: In Chongzong's later years he drew rather close to those at his side and established private estates to take profit.
translations.idiomatic: In the crown prince's later years he grew close to those at his side and established private estates to turn a profit.

sentences.zh: 允諫曰：「天地無私，故能覆載；

translations.literal: Yun remonstrated: "Heaven and earth are without selfishness, and therefore can cover and bear all things;
translations.idiomatic: Yun remonstrated, "Heaven and earth are without selfishness, and therefore can shelter and sustain all things;

sentences.zh: 王者無私，故能包養。

translations.literal: a king without selfishness therefore can embrace and nourish.
translations.idiomatic: a ruler without selfishness therefore can embrace and nourish his people.

sentences.zh: 昔之明王，以至公宰物，故藏金於山，藏珠於淵，示天下以無私，訓天下以至儉。

translations.literal: The enlightened kings of old, with utmost fairness governing all things, therefore hid gold in mountains and pearls in deep pools, showing the world their lack of selfishness and instructing the world in utmost frugality.
translations.idiomatic: The enlightened kings of old governed all things with utmost fairness; they hid gold in mountains and pearls in deep waters, showing the world their selflessness and teaching the world utmost frugality.

sentences.zh: 故美聲盈溢，千載不衰。

translations.literal: Therefore their fine reputation overflowed and did not fade for a thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore their fine reputation overflowed and has not faded for a thousand years.

sentences.zh: 今殿下國之儲貳，四海屬心，言行舉動，萬方所則，而營立私田，畜養鷄犬，乃至販酤市鄽，與民爭利，議聲流布，不可追掩。

translations.literal: Now Your Highness is the state's heir apparent; the four seas turn their hearts to you; words, deeds, and conduct are the model for all regions—yet you establish private fields, raise chickens and dogs, and even sell wine and trade in market stalls, competing with the people for profit; talk spreads and cannot be covered after the fact.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Highness is the heir to the realm; the four seas look to you; your words and deeds are the model for all lands—yet you establish private fields, raise chickens and dogs, and even sell wine and trade in market stalls, competing with the people for profit; rumor spreads and cannot be undone.

sentences.zh: 夫天下者，殿下之天下，富有四海，何求而不獲，何欲而弗從，而與販夫販婦競此尺寸。

translations.literal: The realm is Your Highness's realm; possessing the four seas, what seek you and not obtain, what desire and not have granted—yet you compete with peddling men and women for these inches?
translations.idiomatic: The realm is Your Highness's realm; possessing the four seas, what could you seek and not obtain, what desire and not have granted—yet you compete with peddlers for these trifling gains.

sentences.zh: 昔虢之將亡，神乃下降，賜之土田，卒喪其國。

translations.literal: When Guo was about to perish, a spirit descended and bestowed land and fields; in the end it lost its state.
translations.idiomatic: When the state of Guo was about to perish, a spirit descended and bestowed land and fields upon it; in the end it lost its kingdom.

sentences.zh: 漢之靈帝，不修人君之重，好與宮人列肆販賣，私立府藏，以營小利，卒有顛覆傾亂之禍。

translations.literal: Emperor Ling of Han did not uphold the weight of a ruler; he delighted in setting up stalls with palace women to buy and sell, established private treasuries to seek small profit, and in the end suffered the calamity of overthrow and turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ling of Han did not uphold the dignity of a ruler; he delighted in setting up stalls with palace women to buy and sell, kept private treasuries to seek small profit, and in the end brought on the calamity of overthrow and chaos.

sentences.zh: 前鑒若此，甚可畏懼。

translations.literal: Former mirrors are like this—very much to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: Such precedents from the past are deeply to be feared.

sentences.zh: 夫為人君者，必審於擇人。

translations.literal: One who is ruler must be careful in choosing men.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler must be careful in choosing his men.

sentences.zh: 故稱知人則哲，惟帝難之。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: to know men is to be wise—only the emperor finds it hard.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore it is said that to know men is wisdom—and only the emperor finds it hard.

sentences.zh: 商書云『無邇小人』，孔父有云，小人近之則不遜，遠之則怨矣。

translations.literal: The Book of Shang says, 'Do not keep petty men near'; Confucius's father said that if petty men are kept near they are insolent, and if kept far they resent.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Shang says, 'Do not keep petty men near'; Confucius said that if petty men are kept near they grow insolent, and if kept at a distance they resent you.

sentences.zh: 武王愛周、邵、齊、畢，所以王天下。

translations.literal: King Wu cherished the Zhou, Shao, Qi, and Bi, and therefore ruled the realm.
translations.idiomatic: King Wu cherished the Duke of Zhou, the Duke of Shao, Jiang Ziya, and the Duke of Bi, and therefore ruled the realm.

sentences.zh: 殷紂愛飛廉、惡來，所以喪其國。

translations.literal: King Zhou of Yin cherished Fei Lian and E Lai, and therefore lost his state.
translations.idiomatic: King Zhou of Yin cherished Fei Lian and E Lai, and therefore lost his kingdom.

sentences.zh: 歷觀古今存亡之際，莫不由之。

translations.literal: Reviewing past and present at the turning points of survival and ruin, none fail to follow this pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Surveying past and present at the turning points of survival and ruin, none fail to follow this pattern.

sentences.zh: 今東宮誠曰乏人，儁乂不少。

translations.literal: Now the Eastern Palace truly says it lacks men, yet outstanding talent is not few.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern palace may say it lacks men, yet outstanding talent is not scarce.

sentences.zh: 頃來侍御左右者，恐非在朝之選。

translations.literal: Those who recently attend and serve at your side—I fear they are not choices fit for court.
translations.idiomatic: Those who recently attend you at your side—I fear they are not the sort chosen for court service.

sentences.zh: 故願殿下少察愚言，斥出佞邪，親近忠良，所在田園，分給貧下，畜產販賣，以時收散。

translations.literal: Therefore I wish Your Highness would slightly consider my foolish words, drive out flatterers and the wicked, draw near the loyal and good, distribute existing estates to the poor, and gather in livestock and trading at the proper time.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I beg Your Highness to consider my humble words, drive out flatterers and the wicked, draw near the loyal and good, distribute your estates to the poor, and wind up your livestock and trading in good time.

sentences.zh: 如此則休聲日至，謗議可除。」

translations.literal: If so, fine reputation will come day by day and slander can be removed.
translations.idiomatic: If you do so, your good reputation will grow day by day and slander can be dispelled.

sentences.zh: 恭宗不納。

translations.literal: Chongzong did not accept this.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince did not accept his advice.

sentences.zh: 恭宗之崩也，允久不進見。

translations.literal: When Chongzong died, Yun long did not enter audience.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince died, Yun long avoided appearing at court.

sentences.zh: 後世祖召，允昇階歔欷，悲不能止。

translations.literal: Later the Shizu Emperor summoned him; Yun ascended the steps sobbing and could not stop his grief.
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor summoned him; Yun ascended the steps sobbing and could not stop his grief.

sentences.zh: 世祖流淚，命允使出。

translations.literal: The Shizu Emperor shed tears and ordered Yun to go out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor shed tears and ordered Yun to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 左右莫知其故，相謂曰：「高允無何悲泣，令至尊哀傷，何也？」

translations.literal: Those at his side did not know the reason and said to one another: "For what reason does Gao Yun weep in grief and make the Emperor sorrowful?"
translations.idiomatic: Those at the emperor's side did not know why and said to one another, "Why does Gao Yun weep for no apparent reason and move His Majesty to grief?"

sentences.zh: 世祖聞之，召而謂曰：「汝不知高允悲乎？」

translations.literal: The Shizu Emperor heard this, summoned them, and said: "Do you not know why Gao Yun grieves?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard this, summoned them, and said, "Do you not know why Gao Yun grieves?"

sentences.zh: 左右曰：「臣等見允無言而泣，陛下為之悲傷，是以竊言耳。」

translations.literal: Those at his side said: "We saw Yun weep without speaking, and Your Majesty was moved to sorrow for him—therefore we spoke privately."
translations.idiomatic: They said, "We saw Yun weep without speaking, and Your Majesty was moved to sorrow for him—that is why we spoke privately."

sentences.zh: 世祖曰：「崔浩誅時，允亦應死，東宮苦諫，是以得免。

translations.literal: The Shizu Emperor said: "When Cui Hao was executed, Yun also should have died; the Eastern Palace pleaded bitterly, and therefore he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "When Cui Hao was executed, Yun should also have died; the crown prince pleaded bitterly, and therefore he was spared.

sentences.zh: 今無東宮，允見朕因悲耳。」

translations.literal: Now there is no Eastern Palace; when Yun sees me he grieves for that reason."
translations.idiomatic: Now there is no crown prince; when Yun sees me he grieves for that reason."

sentences.zh: 允表曰：「往年被敕，令臣集天文災異，使事類相從，約而可觀。

translations.literal: Yun submitted a memorial: "In former years I received an edict ordering me to gather astronomical portents and anomalies, arranging them by category so they would be concise and viewable.
translations.idiomatic: Yun submitted a memorial: "In former years I received an edict ordering me to gather astronomical portents and anomalies, arranging them by category so they would be concise and readable.

sentences.zh: 臣聞箕子陳謨而洪範作，宣尼述史而春秋著，皆所以章明列辟，景測皇天者也。

translations.literal: I have heard that when Jizi presented his counsel the Great Plan was composed, and when Confucius narrated history the Spring and Autumn was written—all to make clear the ranks of rulers and mirror and measure august Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that when Jizi presented his counsel the Great Plan was composed, and when Confucius narrated history the Spring and Autumn Annals were written—all to clarify the ranks of rulers and mirror the will of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 故先其善惡而驗以災異，隨其失得而效以禍福，天人誠遠，而報速如響，甚可懼也。

translations.literal: Therefore they first set forth good and evil and verified them by portents and anomalies, following gain and loss and testing them by fortune and calamity—Heaven and man are truly distant, yet retribution is swift as an echo; it is very much to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore they first set forth good and evil and verified them by portents, following gain and loss and testing them by fortune and calamity—Heaven and man are truly distant, yet retribution comes swift as an echo; it is deeply to be feared.

sentences.zh: 自古帝王莫不尊崇其道而稽其法數，以自修飭。

translations.literal: From antiquity emperors and kings have none who did not honor this way and examine its methods and numbers to discipline themselves.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity no emperor or king has failed to honor this way and examine its methods and numbers to discipline himself.

sentences.zh: 厥後史官並載其事，以為鑒誡。

translations.literal: Afterward historians all recorded these matters as mirrors and warnings.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward historians recorded these matters as mirrors and warnings.

sentences.zh: 漢成帝時，光祿大夫劉向見漢祚將危，權歸外戚，屢陳妖眚而不見納。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Cheng of Han, the Household Minister Liu Xiang saw the Han mandate about to be endangered and power return to maternal relatives; he repeatedly presented omens and calamities but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: In the reign of Emperor Cheng of Han, Liu Xiang, household minister of the left, saw the Han mandate endangered and power falling to the empress's kin; he repeatedly presented omens and calamities but was not heeded.

sentences.zh: 遂因洪範、春秋災異報應者而為其傳，覬以感悟人主，而終不聽察，卒以危亡。

translations.literal: Thereupon, drawing on the Great Plan and Spring and Autumn accounts of portents and responses, he made his commentary, hoping to move the ruler to awareness—yet in the end he was not heard or examined, and the dynasty ended in danger and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon, drawing on the Great Plan and the Spring and Autumn accounts of portents and responses, he compiled his commentary, hoping to move the ruler to awareness—yet in the end he was not heeded, and the dynasty fell into ruin.

sentences.zh: 豈不哀哉！

translations.literal: Is it not lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: Is it not lamentable!

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下神武則天，叡鑒自遠，欽若稽古，率由舊章，前言往行，靡不究鑒，前皇所不逮也。

translations.literal: I bow and consider that Your Majesty's divine martiality matches Heaven, sagely discernment reaches far, reverently following antiquity and proceeding by old statutes—words of former sages and deeds of the past, none not thoroughly examined and mirrored; what former emperors did not attain.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly consider that Your Majesty's divine martial prowess matches Heaven, your sagely discernment reaches far, you reverently follow antiquity and proceed by established statutes—words of former sages and deeds of the past, all thoroughly examined; what former emperors did not attain.

sentences.zh: 臣學不洽聞，識見寡薄，懼無以裨廣聖聽，仰酬明旨。

translations.literal: My learning is not broadly heard, my knowledge and views few and thin; I fear I have nothing to add to broaden the sage hearing and repay the bright intent.
translations.idiomatic: My learning is not broad, my insight shallow; I fear I have nothing to add to broaden your sage hearing and repay your clear intent.

sentences.zh: 今謹依洪範傳、天文志撮其事要，略其文辭，凡為八篇。」

translations.literal: Now I respectfully follow the Great Plan commentary and Astronomical Treatise, extracting essentials and abbreviating the wording—in all eight chapters."
translations.idiomatic: Now I respectfully follow the Great Plan commentary and the Astronomical Treatise, extracting the essentials and abbreviating the wording—in all eight chapters."

sentences.zh: 世祖覽而善之，曰：「高允之明災異，亦豈減崔浩乎？」

translations.literal: The Shizu Emperor read it and approved, saying: "Gao Yun's clarity on portents and anomalies—how could it be less than Cui Hao's?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read it and approved, saying, "Gao Yun's understanding of portents and anomalies—how could it be less than Cui Hao's?"

sentences.zh: 及高宗即位，允頗有謀焉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong took the throne, Yun had considerable part in the planning.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wencheng took the throne, Yun had played a considerable part in the planning.

sentences.zh: 司徒陸麗等皆受重賞，允既不蒙褒異，又終身不言。

translations.literal: Minister of Education Lu Li and others all received heavy rewards; Yun neither received special praise nor spoke of it for his whole life.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Education Lu Li and others all received rich rewards; Yun received no special praise and never spoke of it for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 其忠而不伐，皆此類也。

translations.literal: His loyalty without boasting—all were of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His loyalty without boasting—all were of this kind.

sentences.zh: 給事中郭善明，性多機巧，欲逞其能，勸高宗大起宮室。

translations.literal: Guo Shanming, Supervising Censor, was by nature full of clever contrivance and wished to display his ability; he urged Emperor Gaozong to undertake great palace construction.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Shanming, supervising censor, was by nature full of clever contrivance and wished to display his talent; he urged Emperor Wencheng to undertake great palace construction.

sentences.zh: 允諫曰：「臣聞太祖道武皇帝既定天下，始建都邑。

translations.literal: Yun remonstrated: "I have heard that when the Taizu Emperor Daowu had settled the realm, he first established the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yun remonstrated, "I have heard that when Emperor Daowu had settled the realm, he first established the capital.

sentences.zh: 其所營立，非因農隙，不有所興。

translations.literal: What he built and established—unless it was during gaps in farming, he undertook nothing.
translations.idiomatic: What he built he undertook only during gaps in the farming season, and otherwise raised nothing.

sentences.zh: 今建國已久，宮室已備，永安前殿足以朝會萬國，西堂溫室足以安御聖躬，紫樓臨望可以觀望遠近。

translations.literal: Now the state has long been founded and palaces are complete; the Yong'an front hall suffices for audiences with the myriad states, the Western Hall and warm chamber suffice to settle the sage person, and the Purple Tower overlooking can survey far and near.
translations.idiomatic: Now the state has long been founded and the palaces are complete; the front hall of Yong'an suffices for audiences with all nations, the western hall and warm chamber suffice for the emperor's residence, and the Purple Tower suffices to survey far and near.

sentences.zh: 若廣修壯麗為異觀者，宜漸致之，不可倉卒。

translations.literal: If one broadly builds magnificent structures as marvels to behold, it should be done gradually and cannot be rushed.
translations.idiomatic: If magnificent structures are to be built as marvels, they should be undertaken gradually and cannot be rushed.

sentences.zh: 計斫材運土及諸雜役須二萬人，丁夫充作，老小供餉，合四萬人，半年可訖。

translations.literal: It is calculated that felling timber, moving earth, and various miscellaneous labor require twenty thousand men; with corvée laborers filling the work and old and young supplying provisions, forty thousand in all—half a year could finish it.
translations.idiomatic: It is estimated that felling timber, moving earth, and various labor would require twenty thousand men; with corvée laborers at work and old and young supplying provisions, forty thousand in all—half a year could complete it.

sentences.zh: 古人有言：一夫不耕，或受其飢；

translations.literal: The ancients have a saying: if one man does not plow, someone may suffer hunger;
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said that if one man does not plow, someone may go hungry;

sentences.zh: 一婦不織，或受其寒。

translations.literal: if one woman does not weave, someone may suffer cold.
translations.idiomatic: if one woman does not weave, someone may suffer cold.

sentences.zh: 況數萬之眾，其所損廢，亦以多矣。

translations.literal: How much more for a multitude of tens of thousands—the waste and loss would also be great.
translations.idiomatic: How much more for a multitude of tens of thousands—the waste and loss would be enormous.

sentences.zh: 推之於古，驗之於今，必然之效也。

translations.literal: Pushing it back to antiquity and testing it in the present—this is an effect that must follow.
translations.idiomatic: Reasoning from antiquity and testing against the present, this is an effect that must follow.

sentences.zh: 誠聖主所宜思量。」

translations.literal: Truly this is what a sage ruler should consider.
translations.idiomatic: Truly this is what a sage ruler should consider.

sentences.zh: 高宗納之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wencheng accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 允以高宗纂承平之業，而風俗仍舊，婚娶喪葬，不依古式，允乃諫曰：

translations.literal: Yun, because Emperor Gaozong succeeded to a legacy of peace yet customs remained as before—marriage, burial, and mourning not following ancient forms—thereupon remonstrated:
translations.idiomatic: Because Emperor Wencheng had succeeded to a legacy of peace yet customs remained unchanged—marriage and funeral rites not following ancient forms—Yun remonstrated:

sentences.zh: 前朝之世，屢發明詔，禁諸婚娶不得作樂，及葬送之日歌謠、鼓舞、殺牲、燒葬，一切禁斷。

translations.literal: In the former dynasty's time, bright edicts were repeatedly issued forbidding music at weddings, and on the day of burial and escort songs, drumming, dancing, killing beasts, and cremation—all strictly forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: In the previous reign, bright edicts were repeatedly issued forbidding music at weddings, and on burial days songs, drumming, dancing, animal sacrifice, and cremation—all strictly forbidden.

sentences.zh: 雖條旨久頒，而俗不革變。

translations.literal: Though the articles and intent were long promulgated, custom did not change.
translations.idiomatic: Though these regulations were long in force, custom did not change.

sentences.zh: 將由居上者未能悛改，為下者習以成俗，教化陵遲，一至於斯。

translations.literal: Perhaps it is because those above could not repent and reform, while those below practiced until it became custom; instruction and transformation declined, reaching to this point.
translations.idiomatic: The reason must be that those in authority failed to reform themselves, while those below took their ways as custom until they set. Moral instruction decayed until things came to this pass.

sentences.zh: 昔周文以百里之地，修德布政，先於寡妻，及於兄弟，以至家邦，三分天下而有其二。

translations.literal: Formerly King Wen of Zhou, with a territory of a hundred li, cultivated virtue and spread governance—first toward his widowed wife, then his brothers, reaching family and state—and held two-thirds of the realm under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago King Wen of Zhou, ruling only a hundred-li domain, cultivated virtue and spread good governance—first toward his widowed wife, then his brothers, and finally his household and state—until he held two-thirds of All Under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 明為政者先自近始。

translations.literal: He who clearly governs begins from what is near himself.
translations.idiomatic: One who truly governs well begins with those nearest to him.

sentences.zh: 詩云：「爾之教矣，民胥効矣。」

translations.literal: The Classic of Poetry says: "Your teaching—the people all imitate it."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Songs says, "In your teaching, the people all take their pattern."

sentences.zh: 人君舉動，不可不慎。

translations.literal: A ruler's every act must not be uncareful.
translations.idiomatic: A sovereign's every act demands the utmost care.

sentences.zh: 禮云：嫁女之家，三日不息燭；

translations.literal: The Rites say: In the house that marries out a daughter, for three days the candles are not extinguished;
translations.idiomatic: The Rites state that when a family marries out a daughter, candles burn unextinguished for three days;

sentences.zh: 娶婦之家，三日不舉樂。

translations.literal: in the house that takes a wife, for three days music is not raised.
translations.idiomatic: while the family receiving a bride goes three days without music.

sentences.zh: 今諸王納室，皆樂部給伎以為嬉戲，而獨禁細民，不得作樂，此一異也。

translations.literal: Now when the various princes take wives, all are supplied entertainers by the music office for amusement, yet common folk alone are forbidden to make music—this is the first anomaly.
translations.idiomatic: Today when princes wed, the music bureau supplies performers for their entertainment, yet ordinary people alone are barred from music—here is the first contradiction.

sentences.zh: 古之婚者，皆揀擇德義之門，妙選貞閑之女，先之以媒娉，繼之以禮物，集僚友以重其別，親御輪以崇其敬，婚姻之際，如此之難。

translations.literal: Those who married in antiquity all selected gates of virtue and righteousness, superbly chose chaste and modest women, first had matchmakers, then ritual gifts, gathered colleagues and friends to honor the parting, personally drove the carriage-wheel to exalt respect—at marriage's moment, such was the difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity marriage meant choosing families of virtue and integrity, carefully selecting modest and chaste brides, first engaging matchmakers, then presenting gifts, gathering colleagues to honor the farewell, and personally attending to the carriage to show reverence—marriage was treated with such solemn care.

sentences.zh: 今諸王十五，便賜妻別居。

translations.literal: Now at fifteen the various princes are bestowed wives and live apart.
translations.idiomatic: Today princes are given wives and separate households at the age of fifteen.

sentences.zh: 然所配者，或長少差舛，或罪入掖庭，而作合宗王，妃嬪藩懿。

translations.literal: Yet those matched to them may err in elder and younger, or have entered the rear palace through crime, yet are made to unite with imperial clan princes as consorts and fair ones of the domains.
translations.idiomatic: Yet their matches may be grievously mismatched in age, or drawn from palace women condemned for crime, yet are paired with princes of the imperial clan as consorts and ladies of the domain.

sentences.zh: 失禮之甚，無復此過。

translations.literal: The lapse from ritual is extreme; there is no lapse beyond this.
translations.idiomatic: No breach of ritual could be more extreme.

sentences.zh: 往年及今，頻有檢劾。

translations.literal: In past years until now, there have been frequent investigations and impeachments.
translations.idiomatic: In years past and now, there have been frequent investigations.

sentences.zh: 誠是諸王過酒致責，跡其元起，亦由色衰相棄，致此紛紜。

translations.literal: Truly it is that the princes' excess of wine brought reprimand; tracing their origins, it also arises from fading beauty and mutual abandonment, causing this turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: True, the princes were disciplined for drunken excess, but tracing the matter to its source, it often began when wives lost favor and were cast aside, provoking such strife.

sentences.zh: 今皇子娶妻，多出宮掖，令天下小民，必依禮限，此二異也。

translations.literal: Now princes take wives mostly from within the palace confines; common people of the realm must follow ritual limits—this is the second anomaly.
translations.idiomatic: Today imperial sons take wives chiefly from the palace women, while ordinary people must obey ritual limits—here is the second contradiction.

sentences.zh: 萬物之生，靡不有死，古先哲王，作為禮制，所以養生送死，折諸人情。

translations.literal: Of all things born, none lacks death; ancient sage-kings made ritual systems to nurture the living and send off the dead, tempering human sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: All that lives must die; the sage-kings of old fashioned ritual to nurture life and send off the dead, measuring human feeling by propriety.

sentences.zh: 若毀生以奉死，則聖人所禁也。

translations.literal: If one destroys the living to serve the dead, the sages forbade it.
translations.idiomatic: To ruin the living in serving the dead is what the sages forbid.

sentences.zh: 然葬者藏也，死者不可再見，故深藏之。

translations.literal: Yet burial is hiding; the dead cannot be seen again, hence deep concealment.
translations.idiomatic: Yet burial means concealment; the dead cannot return, and so they are laid deep in the earth.

sentences.zh: 昔堯葬穀林，農不易畝；

translations.literal: Formerly Yao was buried at Gu-Lin; farmers did not change their mu;
translations.idiomatic: Yao was buried at Grain Grove, and farmers did not shift their field boundaries;

sentences.zh: 舜葬蒼梧，市不改肆。

translations.literal: Shun was buried at Cangwu; markets did not change their stalls.
translations.idiomatic: Shun was buried at Dark Wu, and market stalls remained unmoved.

sentences.zh: 秦始皇作為地市，下固三泉，金玉寶貨不可計數，死不旋踵，尸焚墓掘。

translations.literal: The First Emperor of Qin made an underground palace; below he fixed the Three Springs; gold, jade, and precious goods were beyond counting; before death had turned, his corpse was burned and tomb excavated.
translations.idiomatic: The First Emperor built an underground palace, sealed it with the Three Springs beneath, and filled it with countless gold and jewels—yet hardly had he died before his corpse was burned and his tomb looted.

sentences.zh: 由此推之，堯舜之儉，始皇之奢，是非可見。

translations.literal: From this one may infer: Yao and Shun's frugality and the First Emperor's extravagance—the right and wrong can be seen.
translations.idiomatic: From this contrast, the frugality of Yao and Shun against the First Emperor's extravagance shows plainly which is right and which is wrong.

sentences.zh: 今國家營葬，費損巨億，一旦焚之，以為灰燼。

translations.literal: Now the state in preparing burial spends hundreds of millions; in one moment burns it to ash.
translations.idiomatic: Today the state spends vast sums on funerals, only to burn everything on the pyre until nothing remains but ash.

sentences.zh: 苟靡費有益於亡者，古之臣奚獨不然。

translations.literal: If extravagant waste benefited the departed, why alone did the ministers of old not do likewise?
translations.idiomatic: If such waste truly benefited the dead, why did the ministers of antiquity not do the same?

sentences.zh: 今上為之不輟，而禁下民之必止，此三異也。

translations.literal: Now the sovereign does not stop it, yet forbids commoners who must cease—this is the third anomaly.
translations.idiomatic: The throne will not cease this practice, yet commoners must stop—here is the third contradiction.

sentences.zh: 古者祭必立尸，序其昭穆，使亡者有憑，致食饗之禮。

translations.literal: In antiquity at sacrifice one established a corpse-representative, arranged the senior and junior lines, so the departed had something to rely on—presenting food and the rites of feasting.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity sacrifices required establishing a ritual representative, ordering the ancestral lines so the dead had a presence, and performing the rites of offering food.

sentences.zh: 今已葬之魂，人直求貌類者事之如父母，燕好如夫妻，損敗風化，瀆亂情禮，莫此之甚。

translations.literal: Now for souls already buried, people simply seek lookalikes and treat them as parents, intimate as husband and wife—damaging customs and profaning ritual sentiment; nothing surpasses this.
translations.idiomatic: Today people take look-alikes for the spirits of the dead and treat them as parents, even sharing a bed as husband and wife—corrupting morals and profaning ritual; nothing is worse.

sentences.zh: 上未禁之，下不改絕，此四異也。

translations.literal: Above they do not forbid it; below they do not change or end it—this is the fourth anomaly.
translations.idiomatic: The court has not banned this; the people have not abandoned it—here is the fourth contradiction.

sentences.zh: 夫饗者，所以定禮儀，訓萬國，故聖王重之。

translations.literal: Feasts are means to fix ritual observance and instruct the myriad states; hence sage-kings valued them.
translations.idiomatic: Feasts exist to establish ritual propriety and instruct the realm, which is why sage-kings held them in esteem.

sentences.zh: 至乃爵盈而不飲，肴乾而不食，樂非雅聲則不奏，物非正色則不列。

translations.literal: To the point that when the cup was full one did not drink, when delicacies dried one did not eat; if music was not elegant sound it was not played; if things were not proper color they were not arranged.
translations.idiomatic: At such feasts cups might stand full yet untasted, delicacies untouched, only refined music played, and only proper colors displayed.

sentences.zh: 今之大會，內外相混，酒醉喧譊，罔有儀式。

translations.literal: Today's great assemblies mix inner and outer; drunk with noise and clamor, without any ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Today's grand banquets mix ranks without distinction, dissolve into drunken uproar, and observe no ritual at all.

sentences.zh: 又俳優鄙藝，[4]汚辱視聽。

translations.literal: Moreover, actors' vulgar arts [4] defile sight and hearing.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, vulgar entertainments [4] degrade what eyes and ears behold.

sentences.zh: 朝庭積習以為美，而責風俗之清純，此五異也。

translations.literal: The court accumulates habit and calls it beautiful, yet demands pure and simple folkways—this is the fifth anomaly.
translations.idiomatic: The court has made such habits a standard of refinement, yet demands purity of custom from the people—here is the fifth contradiction.

sentences.zh: 今陛下當百王之末，踵晉亂之弊，而不矯然釐改，以厲頹俗，臣恐天下蒼生，永不聞見禮教矣。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty stands at the end of a hundred kings, following the Jin chaos's defects, yet does not vigorously reform and rectify to stimulate declining custom—I fear the myriad people will never again hear or see ritual instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty reigns at the end of an age of kings and inherits the disorder left by Jin, yet does not vigorously reform to rouse a failing age. I fear the common people may never again hear or witness the teachings of ritual.

sentences.zh: 允言如此非一，高宗從容聽之。

translations.literal: Yun spoke thus not once; Emperor Gaozong listened at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Yun spoke in this vein many times, and Emperor Wencheng listened calmly.

sentences.zh: 或有觸迕，帝所不忍聞者，命左右扶出。

translations.literal: When there was offense against taboo, what the Emperor could not bear to hear, he ordered attendants to support him out.
translations.idiomatic: When Yun touched on what the emperor could not bear to hear, he would order attendants to lead him out.

sentences.zh: 事有不便，允輒求見，高宗知允意，逆屏左右以待之。

translations.literal: When affairs were inconvenient, Yun would seek audience; Emperor Gaozong knowing Yun's intent would in advance dismiss attendants to await him.
translations.idiomatic: When matters troubled him, Yun would request an audience. Knowing his intent, Wencheng would dismiss his attendants beforehand and wait for him alone.

sentences.zh: 禮敬甚重，晨入暮出，或積日居中，朝臣莫知所論。

translations.literal: Ritual respect was very weighty; entering at dawn and leaving at dusk, sometimes staying within for accumulated days—the courtiers did not know what was discussed.
translations.idiomatic: The courtesies were profound. He might enter at dawn and leave at dusk, or remain inside for days on end, while courtiers never learned what was discussed.

sentences.zh: 或有上事陳得失者，高宗省而謂羣臣曰：「君父一也，父有是非，子何為不作書於人中諫之，使人知惡，而於家內隱處也。

translations.literal: When someone submitted a memorial stating gains and losses, Emperor Gaozong read it and told the assembled ministers: "Father and lord are one. When a father has right and wrong, why should a son not write a letter among people to remonstrate, making others know the evil, yet remonstrate only in secret at home?
translations.idiomatic: When someone submitted a memorial on policy, Emperor Wencheng read it and told his ministers, "A lord and a father are one. If a father errs, why should his son not remonstrate openly so others may know the fault, rather than hide his counsel at home?

sentences.zh: 豈不以父親，恐惡彰於外也。

translations.literal: Is it not because of father and kin, fearing that evil would be displayed outward?
translations.idiomatic: Is it not from affection for one's father, fearing to expose his shame before the world?

sentences.zh: 今國家善惡，不能面陳而上表顯諫，此豈不彰君之短，明己之美。

translations.literal: Now the state's good and evil cannot be stated face to face yet one memorializes with open remonstrance—is this not to display the lord's shortcomings and clarify one's own excellence?
translations.idiomatic: Today one cannot speak of the state's right and wrong to the emperor's face, yet submits a memorial of open remonstrance—is that not to expose the ruler's faults while displaying one's own virtue?

sentences.zh: 至如高允者，真忠臣矣。

translations.literal: As for Gao Yun, he is a true loyal minister.
translations.idiomatic: As for Gao Yun—he is a true loyal minister.

sentences.zh: 朕有是非，常正言面論，至朕所不樂聞者，皆侃侃言說，無所避就。

translations.literal: When I have right and wrong, he always speaks frankly face to face; even what I am displeased to hear, he all speaks forthrightly, without avoidance.
translations.idiomatic: When I err, he speaks frankly to my face; even what I least wish to hear, he states plainly, without evasion.

sentences.zh: 朕聞其過，而天下不知其諫，豈不忠乎！

translations.literal: I hear my faults, yet the realm does not know his remonstrance—is this not loyalty!
translations.idiomatic: I learn of my faults, yet the realm never knows he remonstrated—is that not true loyalty?

sentences.zh: 汝等在左右，曾不聞一正言，但伺朕喜時求官乞職。

translations.literal: You who are at my side have never once heard a single upright word, but only watch when I am pleased to seek office and beg rank.
translations.idiomatic: You at my side have never offered one honest word, but only wait until I am pleased to beg for offices and ranks.

sentences.zh: 汝等把弓刀侍朕左右，徒立勞耳，皆至公王。

translations.literal: You hold bow and blade attending at my left and right, merely standing in vain labor, yet all reach ducal and princely rank.
translations.idiomatic: You hold bow and blade at my side, standing idle in my service, yet all of you have risen to princely rank.

sentences.zh: 此人把筆匡我國家，不過作郎。

translations.literal: This man holds the brush and rectifies our state, yet rises no higher than Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: This man holds the brush and steadies the realm, yet rises no higher than Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 汝等不自愧乎？」

translations.literal: Are you not ashamed yourselves?"
translations.idiomatic: Are you not ashamed?

sentences.zh: 於是拜允中書令，著作如故。

translations.literal: Thereupon he appointed Yun Central Secretariat Director, his post as Compiler unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: With that he appointed Yun Director of the Central Secretariat, while retaining his post as Compiler.

sentences.zh: 司徒陸麗曰：「高允雖蒙寵待，而家貧布衣，妻子不立。」

translations.literal: Minister of Works Lu Li said: "Though Gao Yun enjoys favored treatment, his household is poor in plain cloth; wife and children have no standing."
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Lu Li said, "Though Gao Yun enjoys the emperor's favor, his household is poor—he wears plain cloth, and his wife and children have no proper home."

sentences.zh: 高宗怒曰：「何不先言！

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong angrily said: "Why did you not speak of this first!
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wencheng said angrily, "Why did you not tell me this sooner!

sentences.zh: 今見朕用之，方言其貧。」

translations.literal: Now that you see I employ him, you speak of his poverty."
translations.idiomatic: Only now that you see I have promoted him do you speak of his poverty."

sentences.zh: 是日幸允第，惟草屋數間，布被縕袍，厨中鹽菜而已。

translations.literal: That day he visited Yun's residence: only several thatched rooms, cloth quilt and worn robe, in the kitchen nothing but salt and vegetables.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he visited Yun's home and found only a few thatched rooms, a cloth quilt and worn robe, and in the kitchen nothing but salt and vegetables.

sentences.zh: 高宗歎息曰：「古人之清貧豈有此乎！」

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong sighed and said: "The pure poverty of the ancients—could it have been like this!"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wencheng sighed and said, "The austere poverty of the ancients—was it ever like this?

sentences.zh: 即賜帛五百匹、粟千斛，拜長子忱為綏遠將軍、長樂太守。

translations.literal: He immediately bestowed five hundred bolts of silk and a thousand hu of grain, and appointed his eldest son Chen General Who Pacifies the Distant and Administrator of Changle.
