translations.idiomatic: He at once bestowed five hundred bolts of silk and a thousand hu of grain, and appointed his eldest son Chen General Who Pacifies the Distant and Administrator of Changle.

sentences.zh: 允頻表固讓，高宗不許。

translations.literal: Yun repeatedly memorialized firmly declining; Emperor Gaozong did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Yun repeatedly memorialized to decline, but Emperor Wencheng would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 初與允同徵游雅等多至通官封侯，及允部下吏百數十人亦至刺史二千石，而允為郎二十七年不徙官。

translations.literal: At first those summoned with Yun, such as You Ya and many others, reached high office and enfeoffment as marquises; and of Yun's subordinate clerks, a hundred and several tens also reached regional inspector and two-thousand-dan rank, while Yun remained Gentleman for twenty-seven years without transfer.
translations.idiomatic: Those originally summoned with Yun, such as You Ya, mostly rose to high office and marquisates; a hundred or more of his former clerks became regional inspectors and two-thousand-dan officials, yet Yun remained a Gentleman for twenty-seven years without promotion.

sentences.zh: 時百官無祿，允常使諸子樵采自給。

translations.literal: At that time the hundred officials had no salary; Yun often had his sons gather firewood to support themselves.
translations.idiomatic: In those days officials received no salary; Yun often had his sons gather firewood to support the household.

sentences.zh: 初，尚書竇瑾坐事誅，瑾子遵亡在山澤，遵母焦沒入縣官。

translations.literal: At first, Director of the Imperial Secretariat Dou Jin was executed for his crime; Jin's son Zun fled to mountains and marshes; Zun's mother Jiao was confiscated to the district office.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Director of the Imperial Secretariat Dou Jin had been executed for his crime. Jin's son Zun fled to the wilds, and Zun's mother Jiao was seized by the authorities.

sentences.zh: 後焦以老得免，瑾之親故，莫有恤者。

translations.literal: Later Jiao was released on account of age; none of Jin's kin and old friends showed compassion.
translations.idiomatic: Later Jiao was released because of her age, yet none of Jin's kin or friends showed her any kindness.

sentences.zh: 允愍焦年老，保護在家。

translations.literal: Yun pitied Jiao's advanced years and sheltered her in his home.
translations.idiomatic: Yun pitied Jiao in her old age and sheltered her in his home.

sentences.zh: 積六年，遵始蒙赦。

translations.literal: After six years, Zun at last received amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: After six years Zun at last received amnesty.

sentences.zh: 其篤行如此。

translations.literal: His steadfast conduct was like this.
translations.idiomatic: His steadfast conduct was of this kind.

sentences.zh: 轉太常卿，本官如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Master of Ceremonies, his original post unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Grand Master of Ceremonies while retaining his original post.

sentences.zh: 允上代都賦，因以規諷，亦二京之流也。

translations.literal: Yun submitted his Rhapsody on the Former Capitals, using it thereby to admonish indirectly—it too belongs to the stream of the Two Capitals.
translations.idiomatic: Yun submitted his Rhapsody on the Former Capitals, using it to admonish indirectly—a work in the tradition of the Two Capitals rhapsodies.

sentences.zh: 文多不載。

translations.literal: The text is mostly not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the text is not preserved.

sentences.zh: 時中書博士索敞與侍郎傅默、梁祚論名字貴賤，著議紛紜。

translations.literal: At that time Erudite Suo Chang of the Central Secretariat and Attendants-in-Ordinary Fu Mo and Liang Zuo debated the noble and base of names, their treatises contentious.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Erudite Suo Chang of the Central Secretariat and Attendants-in-Ordinary Fu Mo and Liang Zuo debated the noble and base of personal names, their treatises contentious.

sentences.zh: 允遂著名字論以釋其惑，甚有典證。

translations.literal: Yun thereupon composed his Treatise on Names to resolve their confusion, with very canonical evidence.
translations.idiomatic: Yun thereupon composed his Treatise on Names to resolve their confusion, with strong canonical evidence.

sentences.zh: 復以本官領祕書監，解太常卿，進爵梁城侯，加左將軍。

translations.literal: He again held his original post as Director of the Palace Library, resigned as Grand Master of Ceremonies, was advanced in rank to Marquis of Liangcheng, and added as General of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: He again held his original post as Director of the Palace Library, resigned as Grand Master of Ceremonies, was ennobled as Marquis of Liangcheng, and was appointed General of the Left.

sentences.zh: 初，允與游雅及太原張偉同業相友，雅嘗論允曰：「夫喜怒者，有生所不能無也。

translations.literal: At first Yun studied together as friends with You Ya and Zhang Wei of Taiyuan; Ya once discussed Yun, saying: "Joy and anger are what the living cannot be without.
translations.idiomatic: Early on Yun studied with You Ya and Zhang Wei of Taiyuan as close friends. Ya once remarked of Yun, "Joy and anger are what no living person can be without.

sentences.zh: 而前史載卓公寬中，文饒洪量，褊心者或之弗信。

translations.literal: Yet former histories record Duke Zhuo's breadth at center and Wen Rao's vast measure; narrow-hearted men perhaps disbelieved.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the histories record Duke Zhuo's equanimity and Wen Rao's vast forbearance—men of narrow heart perhaps did not believe it.

sentences.zh: 余與高子遊處四十年矣，未嘗見其是非慍喜之色，不亦信哉。

translations.literal: I have associated with Master Gao for forty years and have never seen the color of his approval or anger at right and wrong—is it not believable?
translations.idiomatic: I have kept company with Master Gao for forty years and have never seen him show anger or pleasure at right and wrong—is that not believable?

sentences.zh: 高子內文明而外柔弱，其言吶吶不能出口，余常呼為『文子』。

translations.literal: Master Gao is inwardly enlightened yet outwardly yielding; his words are hesitant and cannot leave his mouth—I often call him "Master Wen."
translations.idiomatic: Master Gao is inwardly enlightened yet outwardly yielding; his words come haltingly and barely leave his lips—I often call him "Master Wen."

sentences.zh: 崔公謂余云：『高生豐才博學，一代佳士，所乏者矯矯風節耳。』

translations.literal: Master Cui told me: "Master Gao has abundant talent and broad learning, a man of excellence for his generation; what he lacks is stern moral bearing."
translations.idiomatic: Master Cui told me, "Master Gao has abundant talent and broad learning—a man of excellence for his age; what he lacks is stern moral bearing."

sentences.zh: 余亦然之。

translations.literal: I too thought so.
translations.idiomatic: I thought so as well.

sentences.zh: 司徒之譴，起於纖微，及於詔責，崔公聲嘶股戰不能言，宗欽已下伏地流汗，都無人色。

translations.literal: The Minister of Works' reprimand arose from a trifle and reached imperial edict and censure; Master Cui's voice grew hoarse and his legs trembled so he could not speak; Zong Qin and those below prostrated themselves sweating, all without complexion.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Works' reprimand began from a trifle and reached imperial edict and censure. Master Cui's voice grew hoarse and his legs trembled until he could not speak; Zong Qin and those below prostrated themselves streaming sweat, all pale with fear.

sentences.zh: 高子敷陳事理，申釋是非，辭義清辯，音韻高亮。

translations.literal: Master Gao laid out the principles of the matter and explained right and wrong; his argument was clear and his voice resonant.
translations.idiomatic: Master Gao laid out the principles of the matter and explained right and wrong; his argument was lucid and his voice resonant.

sentences.zh: 明主為之動容，聽者無不稱善。

translations.literal: The enlightened ruler was moved on his countenance; listeners all praised his excellence.
translations.idiomatic: The enlightened ruler was visibly moved; everyone who heard him praised his excellence.

sentences.zh: 仁及僚友，保茲元吉，向之所謂矯矯者，更在斯乎？

translations.literal: Benevolence reaching colleagues and friends, preserving this great good—was not what was called stern bearing found precisely here?
translations.idiomatic: Benevolence reaching colleagues and friends, preserving this great good—was not what we called stern bearing found precisely here?

sentences.zh: 宗愛之任勢也，威振四海。

translations.literal: When Zong Ai wielded power, his authority shook the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: When Zong Ai wielded power, his authority shook the four seas.

sentences.zh: 嘗召百司於都坐，王公以下，望庭畢拜，高子獨昇階長揖。

translations.literal: He once summoned the hundred offices to the capital seat; from princes and dukes down, all gazed at the courtyard and bowed completely—Master Gao alone ascended the steps with a long bow.
translations.idiomatic: He once summoned the hundred offices to the capital seat; from princes and dukes down, all gazed at the courtyard and bowed completely—Master Gao alone ascended the steps with a long bow.

sentences.zh: 由此觀之，汲長孺可臥見衞青，何抗禮之有！

translations.literal: From this one may observe: Ji Changru could lie down to see Wei Qing—what need was there to resist ritual!
translations.idiomatic: From this one may observe: Ji Changru could receive Wei Qing lying down—what need was there to resist ritual propriety!

sentences.zh: 向之所謂風節者，得不謂此乎？

translations.literal: What was called moral bearing—may it not be called this?
translations.idiomatic: What we called moral bearing—may it not be precisely this?

sentences.zh: 知人固不易，人亦不易知。

translations.literal: To know a person is indeed not easy; a person too is not easy to know.
translations.idiomatic: To know a person is indeed not easy; a person too is not easy to know.

sentences.zh: 吾既失之於心內，崔亦漏之於形外。

translations.literal: I lost it in my inner heart; Cui too leaked it in outward form.
translations.idiomatic: I missed it in my inner judgment; Cui too missed it in outward appearance.

sentences.zh: 鍾期止聽於伯牙，夷吾見明於鮑叔，良有以也。」

translations.literal: Zhong Qi ceased listening only to Bo Ya; Guan Zhong saw clarity in Bao Shu—there is truly reason for this."
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Qi heard only Bo Ya; Guan Zhong saw clarity in Bao Shu—there is truly reason for this.

sentences.zh: 其為人物所推如此。

translations.literal: He was thus commended by others in character.
translations.idiomatic: Thus was he esteemed by others in character.

sentences.zh: 高宗重允，常不名之，恒呼為「令公」。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong valued Yun and often did not call him by name, always addressing him as "Lord Director."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wencheng esteemed Yun and often did not call him by name, always addressing him as "Lord Director."

sentences.zh: 「令公」之號，播於四遠矣。

translations.literal: The title "Lord Director" spread to the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: The title "Lord Director" spread to the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 高宗崩，顯祖居諒闇，乙渾專擅朝命，謀危社稷。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong died, Emperor Xianzu dwelt in mourning garb; Yi Hun monopolized court commands and plotted to endanger the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wencheng died, Emperor Xianzu observed mourning; Yi Hun monopolized court commands and plotted to endanger the state.

sentences.zh: 文明太后誅之，引允禁中，參決大政。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wenming executed him, summoned Yun within the palace confines, and had him participate in deciding great affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenming executed him, summoned Yun within the palace, and had him participate in deciding great affairs.

sentences.zh: 又詔允曰：「自頃以來，庠序不建，為日久矣。

translations.literal: She also issued an edict to Yun: "In recent times, schools have not been established, and this has been so for long.
translations.idiomatic: She also issued an edict to Yun, "For some time now schools have not been established, and this has gone on for long.

sentences.zh: 道肆陵遲，學業遂廢，子衿之歎，復見于今。

translations.literal: The Way declines and learning is abandoned; the sigh of the collar-gem appears again today.
translations.idiomatic: The Way declines and learning is abandoned; the sigh of the collar-gem appears again today.

sentences.zh: 朕既篡統大業，八表晏寧，稽之舊典，欲置學官於郡國，使進修之業，有所津寄。

translations.literal: I have succeeded to the great enterprise; the eight regions are tranquil; consulting the old statutes, I wish to establish academic officers in commanderies and states so that advancing study may have a ford and resting place.
translations.idiomatic: I have succeeded to the great enterprise; the eight regions are tranquil. Consulting the old statutes, I wish to establish academic officers in commanderies and states so that advancing study may have a place to moor.

sentences.zh: 卿儒宗元老，朝望舊德，宜與中、祕二省參議以聞。」

translations.literal: You are an elder of the Confucian school, the court's hope and old virtue—you should join the Central Secretariat and Palace Library in deliberation and report."
translations.idiomatic: You are an elder of the Confucian school, the court's hope and old virtue—you should join the Central Secretariat and Palace Library in deliberation and report.

sentences.zh: 允表曰：「臣聞經綸大業，必以教養為先；

translations.literal: Yun memorialized: "Your servant has heard that to weave the great enterprise, one must take instruction and nurture as foremost;
translations.idiomatic: Yun memorialized, "Your servant has heard that to weave the great enterprise, one must take instruction and nurture as foremost;

sentences.zh: 咸秩九疇，亦由文德成務。

translations.literal: To complete the nine categories in order also depends on literary virtue accomplishing the task.
translations.idiomatic: To complete the nine categories in order also depends on literary virtue accomplishing the task.

sentences.zh: 故辟雍光於周詩，泮宮顯於魯頌。

translations.literal: Hence the Bright Hall shone in the Zhou odes, and the Pan Palace appeared in the Lu eulogies.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Bright Hall shone in the Zhou odes, and the Pan Palace appeared in the Lu eulogies.

sentences.zh: 自永嘉以來，舊章殄滅。

translations.literal: Since the Yongjia era, old statutes have perished.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Yongjia era, old statutes have perished.

sentences.zh: 鄉閭蕪沒雅頌之聲，京邑杜絕釋奠之禮。

translations.literal: In villages and hamlets the sounds of the Odes and Hymns were overgrown and lost; in the capital the rites of libation and sacrifice were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: In villages and hamlets the sounds of the Odes and Hymns were overgrown and lost; in the capital the rites of libation and sacrifice were cut off.

sentences.zh: 道業陵夷，百五十載。

translations.literal: The Way and its enterprise declined for a hundred and fifty years.
translations.idiomatic: The Way and learning had declined for a hundred and fifty years.

sentences.zh: 仰惟先朝每欲憲章昔典，經闡素風，方事尚殷，弗遑克復。

translations.literal: Looking up to the former court, it often wished to take the ancient statutes as model and expound the plain style, yet affairs were still pressing and there was no leisure to restore them.
translations.idiomatic: The former court often wished to take the ancient statutes as its model and revive the plain style of old, yet pressing affairs left no leisure to restore them.

sentences.zh: 陛下欽明文思，纂成洪烈，萬國咸寧，百揆時敍。

translations.literal: Your Majesty reveres bright culture and literary reflection, succeeding to the great enterprise; the myriad states are all tranquil, the hundred offices timely ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty reveres bright culture and literary reflection, succeeding to the great enterprise; the myriad states are tranquil and the hundred offices duly ordered.

sentences.zh: 申祖宗之遺志，興周禮之絕業，爰發德音，惟新文教。

translations.literal: Extending the ancestors' testamentary will, reviving the Zhou rites' severed enterprise, thereupon issuing virtuous proclamation, renewing cultural instruction.
translations.idiomatic: You extend the ancestors' testamentary will and revive the severed enterprise of the Zhou rites, issuing virtuous proclamation to renew cultural instruction.

sentences.zh: 搢紳黎獻，莫不幸甚。

translations.literal: Girdled sashes and black-haired folk all had no greater fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and common people alike rejoiced beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 臣承旨敕，並集二省，披覽史籍，備究典紀，靡不敦儒以勸其業，貴學以篤其道。

translations.literal: Your servant received the edict's command and together gathered the two secretariats, perused historical records, fully investigated canonical statutes—none did not esteem Confucianism to encourage their enterprise and value learning to deepen their Way.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant received the edict and together with the two secretariats perused historical records and fully investigated canonical statutes—every age esteemed Confucianism to encourage study and valued learning to deepen the Way.

sentences.zh: 伏思明詔，玄同古義。

translations.literal: Prostrating myself I reflect on the bright edict: it is darkly identical with ancient meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting on the bright edict, I find it darkly identical with ancient meaning.

sentences.zh: 宜如聖旨，崇建學校以厲風俗。

translations.literal: It should follow the sage edict: grandly establish schools to stimulate custom.
translations.idiomatic: It should follow the sage edict and grandly establish schools to stimulate custom.

sentences.zh: 使先王之道，光演於明時；

translations.literal: Let the former kings' Way brightly unfold in the enlightened age;
translations.idiomatic: Let the Way of the former kings brightly unfold in this enlightened age;

sentences.zh: 郁郁之音，流聞於四海。

translations.literal: the lush sounds flow and are heard within the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: may its lush sounds flow and be heard throughout the four seas.

sentences.zh: 請制大郡立博士二人、助教四人、學生一百人，次郡立博士二人、助教二人、學生八十人，中郡立博士一人、助教二人、學生六十人，下郡立博士一人、助教一人、學生四十人。

translations.literal: I request that great commanderies establish two Erudites, four Assistant Instructors, and a hundred students; secondary commanderies two Erudites, two Assistant Instructors, and eighty students; middle commanderies one Erudite, two Assistant Instructors, and sixty students; lower commanderies one Erudite, one Assistant Instructor, and forty students.
translations.idiomatic: I propose that great commanderies establish two Erudites, four Assistant Instructors, and a hundred students; secondary commanderies two Erudites, two Assistant Instructors, and eighty students; middle commanderies one Erudite, two Assistant Instructors, and sixty students; and lower commanderies one Erudite, one Assistant Instructor, and forty students.

sentences.zh: 其博士取博關經典、世履忠清、堪為人師者，年限四十以上。

translations.literal: The Erudites should be chosen from those broadly versed in the classics, whose conduct in the world is loyal and pure and who can serve as others' teachers, aged forty or above.
translations.idiomatic: Erudites should be chosen from those broadly versed in the classics, loyal and pure in conduct, fit to serve as teachers, and aged forty or above.

sentences.zh: 助教亦與博士同，年限三十以上。

translations.literal: Assistant Instructors are the same as Erudites, aged thirty or above.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Instructors should meet the same standards as Erudites, aged thirty or above.

sentences.zh: 若道業夙成，才任教授，不拘年齒。

translations.literal: If the Way's enterprise was early accomplished and talent suffices for instruction, age is not restricted.
translations.idiomatic: If the Way's enterprise was early accomplished and talent suffices for instruction, age should not restrict appointment.

sentences.zh: 學生取郡中清望，人行修謹，堪循名教者，先盡高門，次及中第。」

translations.literal: Students should be taken from the commandery's clear reputation—persons whose conduct is cultivated and careful and who can follow name and teaching; first exhaust the high gates, then reach the middle ranks."
translations.idiomatic: Students should be drawn from families of clear reputation in the commandery—persons of cultivated and careful conduct who can follow name and teaching—first from eminent households, then from middle ranks.

sentences.zh: 顯祖從之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzu followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzu approved this.

sentences.zh: 郡國立學，自此始也。

translations.literal: Commandery and state schools were established from this time.
translations.idiomatic: Commandery and state schools were established from this time onward.

sentences.zh: 後允以老疾，頻上表乞骸骨，詔不許。

translations.literal: Later Yun, because of old age and illness, repeatedly memorialized begging to retire with his bones; edicts did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Later, afflicted by old age and illness, Yun repeatedly memorialized begging to retire; the edicts did not permit it.

sentences.zh: 於是乃著告老詩。

translations.literal: Thereupon he composed his poem on announcing old age.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he composed his poem on announcing retirement.

sentences.zh: 又以昔歲同徵，零落將盡，感逝懷人，作徵士頌，蓋止於應命者，其有命而不至，則闕焉。

translations.literal: Also, because in that year's same summons his companions were nearly all gone, moved by the passing of time he cherished men and composed his Eulogy for Summoned Scholars—covering only those who answered the summons; those with summons who did not come are omitted.
translations.idiomatic: Also, because those summoned with him in that year were nearly all gone, moved by the passing of time he cherished his companions and composed his Eulogy for Summoned Scholars—covering only those who answered the summons; those summoned who did not come are omitted.

sentences.zh: 羣賢之行，舉其梗概矣。

translations.literal: The conduct of the assembled worthies—he set forth their outlines.
translations.idiomatic: He set forth the outlines of the assembled worthies' conduct.

sentences.zh: 今著之於左：

translations.literal: Now they are recorded at left:
translations.idiomatic: They are recorded below:

translations.idiomatic: Lü Jicai of Zhao Commandery, Administrator of Chenliu Commandery and Viscount of Gaoyi

sentences.zh: 夫百王之御士也，莫不資伏羣才，以隆治道。

translations.literal: Of the hundred kings' governing of scholars, none did not rely on and submit to the host of talents to elevate the governing Way.
translations.idiomatic: In governing scholars, none of the hundred kings failed to rely on the host of talents to elevate the governing Way.

sentences.zh: 故周文以多士克寧，漢武以得賢為盛。

translations.literal: Hence King Wen of Zhou with many scholars achieved tranquility; Emperor Wu of Han took obtaining the worthy as flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: Hence King Wen of Zhou with many scholars achieved tranquility, and Emperor Wu of Han took obtaining the worthy as his glory.

sentences.zh: 此載籍之所記，由來之常義。

translations.literal: This the records memorialize—the constant meaning from antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Such is what the records memorialize—the constant meaning handed down from antiquity.

sentences.zh: 魏自神䴥已後，宇內平定，誅赫連積世之僭，掃窮髮不羇之寇，南摧江楚，西盪涼域，殊方之外，慕義而至。

translations.literal: Wei from after Shenqi onward, within the realm was pacified; they executed the Herunian line's usurpation across generations and swept away the unrestrained barbarians of poor hair; south they crushed Jiang and Chu, west they shook the Liang domains—beyond strange regions, those who admired righteousness came.
translations.idiomatic: From Shenqi onward Wei pacified the realm, destroyed the Herunian usurpers across generations, and swept away unrestrained barbarians; south they crushed Jiang and Chu, west they shook the Liang domains—and beyond strange regions, those who admired righteousness came.

sentences.zh: 於是偃兵息甲，修立文學，登延儁造，酬諮政事。

translations.literal: Thereupon they stilled weapons and rested armor, established and raised literary learning, ascended and extended outstanding makers, and rewarded and consulted on government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon they stilled weapons and rested armor, established literary learning, promoted outstanding men, and consulted them on government affairs.

sentences.zh: 夢想賢哲，思遇其人，訪諸有司，以求名士。

translations.literal: Dreaming of the worthy and wise, they thought to encounter such persons; they inquired of the relevant offices to seek famous scholars.
translations.idiomatic: They dreamed of the worthy and wise and sought to encounter such persons, inquiring of the relevant offices to seek famous scholars.

sentences.zh: 咸稱范陽盧玄等四十二人，皆冠冕之冑，著問州邦，有羽儀之用。

translations.literal: All praised Lu Xuan of Fanyang and forty-two others—all caps and coronets' scions, renowned in their commanderies and states, with the usefulness of feathered banners.
translations.idiomatic: All praised Lu Xuan of Fanyang and forty-two others—all scions of eminent houses, renowned in their commanderies and states, fit to serve as exemplars.

sentences.zh: 親發明詔，以徵玄等。

translations.literal: The sovereign personally issued bright edicts to summon Xuan and the others.
translations.idiomatic: He personally issued bright edicts summoning Xuan and the others.

sentences.zh: 乃曠官以待之，懸爵以縻之。

translations.literal: They left offices vacant to await them and suspended ranks to tether them.
translations.idiomatic: They left offices vacant to await them and suspended ranks to retain them.

sentences.zh: 其就命三十五人，自餘依例州郡所遣者不可稱記。

translations.literal: Those who accepted the command were thirty-five men; the rest sent according to precedent by commanderies and states cannot be fully recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-five accepted the command; the rest sent according to precedent by commanderies and states cannot be fully recorded.

sentences.zh: 爾乃髦士盈朝，而濟濟之美興焉。

translations.literal: Then eminent scholars filled the court, and the beauty of abundance arose.
translations.idiomatic: Then eminent scholars filled the court, and the splendor of abundance flourished.

sentences.zh: 昔與之俱蒙斯舉，或從容廊廟，或游集私門，上談公務，下盡忻娛，以為千載一時，始於此矣。

translations.literal: Formerly those who together received this summons—some at ease in the hall and temple, some gathering in private gates—above discussed public affairs, below fully shared delight, thinking it a thousand-year moment, beginning from this.
translations.idiomatic: Those who together received this summons—some at ease in court, some gathering in private homes—above discussed public affairs, below fully shared delight, thinking it a moment once in a thousand years, beginning from this.

sentences.zh: 日月推移，吉凶代謝，同徵之人，凋殲殆盡。

translations.literal: Sun and moon shifted; fortune and misfortune succeeded one another; those summoned together were nearly all destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Sun and moon shifted; fortune and misfortune succeeded one another; those summoned together were nearly all gone.

sentences.zh: 在者數子，然復分張。

translations.literal: Of those who remain, a few men—yet again scattered apart.
translations.idiomatic: Of those who remain, only a few—and they too are scattered apart.

sentences.zh: 往昔之忻，變為悲戚。

translations.literal: Former delight changed into present sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Former delight has changed into present sorrow.

sentences.zh: 張仲業東臨營州，遲其還返，一敍于懷，齊衿于垂歿之年，寫情於桑榆之末。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhongye eastward governed Yingzhou; I delayed his return and once poured out my breast; together we grieved in the year of approaching death, writing feeling at mulberry and sunset's end.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhongye governed Yingzhou in the east; I longed for his return and once poured out my heart to him; together we grieved as death approached, writing our feelings at life's sunset.

sentences.zh: 其人不幸，復至殞歿。

translations.literal: That man was unfortunate and again came to perishing death.
translations.idiomatic: That man was unfortunate and again met death.

sentences.zh: 在朝者皆後進之士，居里者非疇昔之人，進涉無寄心之所，出入無解顏之地。

translations.literal: Those in court are all later-entering scholars; those in the neighborhood are not men of former days; advancing and wading has no place for the mind to rest; going out and entering has no place to unknit the countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Those in court are all later-entering scholars; those in the neighborhood are not men of former days; in advancing there is no place for the mind to rest, in going out and entering no face to unburden.

sentences.zh: 顧省形骸，所以永歎而不已。

translations.literal: Looking back at my bodily form, therefore I sigh unceasingly.
translations.idiomatic: Looking back at my bodily form, I therefore sigh unceasingly.

sentences.zh: 夫頌者美盛德之形容，亦可以長言寄意。

translations.literal: The eulogy is the portrayal of flourishing virtue's form and appearance; one may also use long words to lodge intent.
translations.idiomatic: The eulogy portrays flourishing virtue's form; one may also use extended words to lodge one's intent.

sentences.zh: 不為文二十年矣，然事切於心，豈可默乎？

translations.literal: I have not composed writing for twenty years, yet affairs cut to the heart—how can I be silent?
translations.idiomatic: I have not written for twenty years, yet affairs cut to the heart—how can I remain silent?

sentences.zh: 遂為之頌，詞曰：

translations.literal: Thereupon I made this eulogy for them; the words say:
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon I composed this eulogy; the words say:

sentences.zh: 紫氣干霄，羣雄亂夏，王龔徂征，戎車屢駕。

translations.literal: Purple vapor reached the heavens; many heroes disturbed Xia; King Gong set out on campaign; war chariots were repeatedly driven.
translations.idiomatic: Purple vapor reached the heavens; many heroes disturbed Xia; the king set out on campaign and war chariots rolled forth again and again.

sentences.zh: 掃盪遊氛，克剪妖霸，四海從風，八垠漸化。

translations.literal: Sweeping away roaming mists, he cut down demonic usurpers; the four seas followed the wind; the eight borders gradually transformed.
translations.idiomatic: He swept away roaming mists and cut down demonic usurpers; the four seas followed the wind and the eight borders gradually transformed.

sentences.zh: 政教無外，既寧且一，偃武櫜兵，唯文是恤。

translations.literal: Government and teaching had no outside; already tranquil and unified; he stilled martial arts and sheathed weapons, caring only for culture.
translations.idiomatic: Government and teaching knew no border; the realm was tranquil and unified; he stilled martial arts and sheathed weapons, caring only for culture.

sentences.zh: 帝乃旁求，搜賢舉逸，巖隱投竿，異人並出。

translations.literal: The emperor then sought widely, searching for the worthy and raising the reclusive; from cliffs and hidden places and those who cast aside fishing poles, unusual men all emerged.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then sought widely, searching for the worthy and raising the reclusive; from cliffs and hidden places men emerged, and those who had cast aside their fishing poles came forth together.

sentences.zh: 亹亹盧生，量遠思純，鑽道據德，遊藝依仁。

translations.literal: Assiduous, assiduous Master Lu; measure far-reaching, thought pure; drilling the Way, holding virtue, roaming in arts, relying on benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Assiduous Master Lu, far-reaching in measure and pure in thought; drilling the Way and holding virtue, roaming in the arts and relying on benevolence.

sentences.zh: 旌弓既招，釋褐投巾，攝齊升堂，嘉謀日陳。

translations.literal: The signal bow already summoned; he doffed coarse cloth for the towel; gathering his hem he ascended the hall; excellent plans daily presented.
translations.idiomatic: The signal bow summoned him; he doffed coarse cloth for office; gathering his hem he ascended the hall and excellent plans were daily presented.

sentences.zh: 自東徂南，躍馬馳輪，僭馮影附，[9]劉以和親。

translations.literal: From east to south he leaped horse and drove wheel; the usurper Feng's shadow attached;[9] Liu thereby harmonized through marriage.
translations.idiomatic: From east to south he leaped horse and drove wheel; the usurper Feng cast his shadow;[9] Liu was thereby harmonized through marriage.

sentences.zh: 茂祖煢單，夙離不造，克己勉躬，聿隆家道。

translations.literal: Maozu solitary and alone; early departed, not reared; restraining self and exerting body; thereby elevating the household Way.
translations.idiomatic: Maozu solitary and alone, early bereft and not reared; restraining himself and exerting his person, thereby elevating the household Way.

sentences.zh: 敦心六經，遊思文藻，終辭寵命，以之自保。

translations.literal: He devoted heart to the Six Classics, roamed thought in literary ornament; ultimately declined favored command, thereby preserving himself.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted his heart to the Six Classics and roamed in literary ornament; ultimately he declined favored command to preserve himself.

sentences.zh: 燕、常篤信，百行靡遺，位不苟進，任理栖遲。

translations.literal: Yan and Chang were sincere and faithful; the hundred conduct lines none left behind; rank he did not advance without cause; he dwelt in principle and tarried.
translations.idiomatic: Yan and Chang were sincere and faithful; in the hundred lines of conduct none was left behind; he would not advance in rank without cause but dwelt in principle and tarried.

sentences.zh: 居沖守約，好讓善推，思賢樂古，如渴如飢。

translations.literal: Dwelling in the center he guarded simplicity; he loved yielding and was good at deferring; thinking of the worthy and delighting in antiquity, like thirst, like hunger.
translations.idiomatic: He dwelt in modesty and guarded simplicity, loved yielding and excelled at deferring, and yearned for the worthy and delighted in antiquity as if thirsty or hungry.

sentences.zh: 子翼致遠，道賜悟深，相期以義，相和若琴。

translations.literal: Ziyi reached far; Daoci awakened deep; they expected one another by righteousness; they harmonized like the zither.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi reached far and Daoci awakened deep; they expected one another by righteousness and harmonized like the zither.

sentences.zh: 並參幕府，俱發德音，優遊卒歲，聊以寄心。

translations.literal: Together they joined the headquarters staff; together they issued virtuous sound; at ease they completed the year; briefly they lodged the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Together they joined the headquarters staff and together issued virtuous sound; at ease they completed the year and briefly lodged their hearts.

sentences.zh: 祖根運會，克光厥猷，仰緣朝恩，俯因德友。

translations.literal: Zugen's fortune met; he could brighten his plans; looking up he relied on court grace; looking down he relied on virtuous friends.
translations.idiomatic: Zugen's fortune met and he could brighten his plans; looking up he relied on court grace, looking down on virtuous friends.

sentences.zh: 功雖後建，祿實先受，班同舊臣，位並羣后。

translations.literal: Merit though later established, emolument in fact first received; rank equal to old ministers, position alongside the host of nobles.
translations.idiomatic: Though his merit was later established, emolument in fact came first; rank equal to old ministers, position alongside the host of nobles.

sentences.zh: 士衡孤立，內省靡疚，言不崇華，交不遺舊。

translations.literal: Shiheng stood alone; inward examination without fault; words he did not exalt with splendor; in association he did not abandon the old.
translations.idiomatic: Shiheng stood alone; inward examination found no fault; he did not exalt his words with splendor and in association did not abandon old friends.

sentences.zh: 以產則貧，論道則富，所謂伊人，實邦之秀。

translations.literal: By property he was poor; by the Way he was rich—what is called "that man" is truly the state's outstanding talent.
translations.idiomatic: Poor in worldly goods yet rich in the Way—such a man is truly the state's finest talent.

sentences.zh: 卓矣友規，禀茲淑亮，存彼大方，擯此細讓。

translations.literal: Outstanding was Yougui; he received this pure brightness; he preserved that great squareness and rejected this petty yielding.
translations.idiomatic: Outstanding was Yougui, who received this pure brightness; he preserved that great squareness and rejected petty yielding.

sentences.zh: 神與理冥，形隨流浪，雖屈王侯，莫廢其尚。

translations.literal: Spirit and principle were darkly united; form followed wandering waves; though he bent to princes and marquises, he never abandoned his elevation.
translations.idiomatic: His spirit merged with principle in obscurity; his form followed wandering waves; though he bowed to princes and marquises, he never abandoned his high purpose.

sentences.zh: 趙實名區，世多奇士，山岳所鍾，挺生三李。

translations.literal: Zhao was truly a famous region; the age had many marvelous scholars; what mountains and rivers keyed, three Lis were born upright.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was a region of true renown; the age produced many marvelous scholars, and where mountains and rivers converged, three men of the Li clan rose upright.

sentences.zh: 矯矯清風，抑抑容止，初九而潛，望雲而起。

translations.literal: Stern, stern the pure wind; restrained, restrained the bearing; at the first nine he was submerged; gazing at clouds he rose.
translations.idiomatic: Stern the pure wind, restrained the bearing; at the first nine he was submerged; gazing at clouds he rose.

sentences.zh: 詵尹西都，靈惟作傳，垂訓皇宮，載理雲霧。

translations.literal: Shen governed the western capital; Ling alone made the commentary; he handed down instruction to the imperial palace and bore reason through mist and cloud.
translations.idiomatic: Shen governed the western capital; Ling alone made the commentary; he handed down instruction to the imperial palace and bore governance through mist and cloud.

sentences.zh: 熙雖中夭，迹階郎署，餘塵可挹，終亦顯著。

translations.literal: Though Xi died in mid-course, his traces ascended the Gentleman's office; remaining dust could be scooped—ultimately he too was illustrious.
translations.idiomatic: Though Xi died young, his traces reached the Gentleman's office; what remained could still be gathered—ultimately he too won distinction.

sentences.zh: 仲業淵長，雅性清到，憲章古式，綢繆典誥。

translations.literal: Zhongye was deep and long; elegant nature clear and penetrating; he took the ancient style as statute and bound close the canonical edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongye was profound and far-reaching, of elegant and penetrating nature; he took ancient style as his statute and bound himself to canonical edicts.

sentences.zh: 時值險難，常一其操。

translations.literal: When the time met peril and hardship, he always kept one conduct.
translations.idiomatic: When times met peril and hardship, he always held to one course of conduct.

sentences.zh: 納眾以仁，訓下以孝，化被龍川，民歸其教。

translations.literal: Receiving the multitude by benevolence, instructing subordinates by filial piety—his transformation covered Longchuan and the people returned to his teaching.
translations.idiomatic: He received the multitude with benevolence and instructed subordinates with filial piety; his transformation covered Longchuan and the people returned to his teaching.

sentences.zh: 邁則英賢，侃亦稱選，聞達邦家，名行素顯。

translations.literal: Mai was then the outstanding worthy; Kan too was called selected; heard and reached the state and family; name and conduct always illustrious.
translations.idiomatic: Mai was an outstanding worthy and Kan too was acclaimed; their fame reached the state and family and their names and conduct were always illustrious.

sentences.zh: 志在兼濟，豈伊獨善，繩匠弗顧，功不獲展。

translations.literal: Their will lay in aiding all; how could it be self-good alone? The line-and-compass craftsman did not look—merit could not be displayed.
translations.idiomatic: Their will lay in aiding all—how could it be self-cultivation alone? The craftsman of governance did not heed them and their merit could not be displayed.

sentences.zh: 劉、許履忠，竭力致躬，出能騁說，入獻其功。

translations.literal: Liu and Xu trod loyalty; they exhausted strength to devote body; going out they could expound persuasion; entering they presented their merit.
translations.idiomatic: Liu and Xu trod the path of loyalty and exhausted themselves in service; going out they could expound persuasion and entering they presented their merit.

sentences.zh: 輶軒一舉，撓燕下崇，名彰魏世，享業亦隆。

translations.literal: Once the light carriage was raised, they bent Yan and lowered Chong; name shone in the Wei age; enjoyed enterprise also lofty.
translations.idiomatic: Once the envoy carriage was raised, they bent Yan and lowered Chong; their names shone in the Wei age and their enjoyed enterprise was lofty.

sentences.zh: 道茂夙成，弱冠播名，與朋以信，行物以誠。

translations.literal: Daomao early accomplished; at weak cap he spread name; with friends by trust; in conduct toward things by sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Daomao was early accomplished and at a young age spread his name; with friends he was trustworthy and in conduct toward things he was sincere.

sentences.zh: 怡怡昆弟，穆穆家庭，發響九臯，翰飛紫冥。

translations.literal: Harmonious, harmonious the brothers; reverent, reverent the household; issuing sound from the nine marshes, brush flying in purple obscurity.
translations.idiomatic: Harmonious were the brothers and reverent the household; he issued sound from the nine marshes and his brush flew in purple obscurity.

sentences.zh: 頻在省闥，亦司于京，刑以之中，政以之平。

translations.literal: Frequently in the provincial gates, he also served in the capital; punishment by the mean, government by the level.
translations.idiomatic: He frequently served in the provincial gates and also in the capital; punishment was measured by the mean and government by equity.

sentences.zh: 猗歟彥鑒，思參文雅，率性任真，器成非假。

translations.literal: How great Yanjian! Thought joined cultured elegance; by nature he followed truth; accomplishment formed without borrowing.
translations.idiomatic: How great Yanjian! His thought joined cultured elegance; by nature he followed truth and his accomplishment formed without artifice.

sentences.zh: 靡矜于高，莫耻于下，乃謝朱門，歸迹林野。

translations.literal: He did not pride himself on height nor was he shamed by lowliness; thereupon he thanked the vermilion gate and returned his traces to woods and fields.
translations.idiomatic: He did not pride himself on height nor was he shamed by lowliness; thereupon he left the vermilion gate and returned to woods and fields.

sentences.zh: 宗敬延譽，號為四儁，華藻雲飛，金聲夙振。

translations.literal: Zongjing extended reputation; he was called one of the four outstanding men; flowery ornament flew like clouds; golden sound early vibrated.
translations.idiomatic: Zongjing extended his reputation and was called one of the four outstanding men; his flowery ornament flew like clouds and his golden sound early vibrated.

sentences.zh: 中遇沈痾，賦詩以訊，忠顯于辭，理出于韻。

translations.literal: Midway he met deep illness; he composed poetry to inquire; loyalty displayed in words; principle issued from rhyme.
translations.idiomatic: Midway he met deep illness and composed poetry to inquire; loyalty displayed in his words and principle issued from his rhyme.

sentences.zh: 高滄朗達，默識淵通，領新悟異，發自心胸。

translations.literal: Gao was vast and penetrating; silent knowledge deep and penetrating; leading the new and comprehending the strange, issuing from heart and breast.
translations.idiomatic: Gao was vast and penetrating, with silent knowledge deep and penetrating; leading the new and comprehending the strange, he issued from heart and breast.

sentences.zh: 質侔和璧，文炳雕龍，燿姿天邑，衣錦舊邦。

translations.literal: Quality matched the harmonious jade; writing gleamed like carved dragon; radiant bearing in the heavenly city; brocade robes in the old domain.
translations.idiomatic: His quality matched the harmonious jade and his writing gleamed like a carved dragon; radiant bearing in the heavenly city and brocade robes in his old domain.

sentences.zh: 士元先覺，介焉不惑，振袂來庭，始賓王國。

translations.literal: Shiyuan first awakened; between them he was not confused; shaking his sleeves he came to court; first guest of the royal domain.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyuan first awakened and between extremes was not confused; shaking his sleeves he came to court and was first guest of the royal domain.

sentences.zh: 蹈方履正，好是繩墨，淑人君子，其儀不忒。

translations.literal: Treading the square and treading the upright; he loved the plumb line and ink; the good man and gentleman—his bearing without error.
translations.idiomatic: Treading the square and treading the upright, he loved the plumb line and ink; a good man and gentleman whose bearing was without error.

sentences.zh: 孔稱游夏，漢美淵雲，越哉伯度，出類踰羣。

translations.literal: Confucius praised You and Xia; Han praised Yuan and Yun; how surpassing Bodu! He exceeded his kind and surpassed the host.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius praised You and Xia; Han praised Yuan and Yun; how surpassing was Bodu! He exceeded his kind and surpassed the host.

sentences.zh: 司言祕閣，作牧河汾，移風易俗，理亂解紛。

translations.literal: He spoke for the secret archive; was governor of He and Fen; shifting wind and changing custom; ordering disorder and unraveling confusion.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke for the secret archive and was governor of He and Fen; shifting wind and changing custom, ordering disorder and unraveling confusion.

sentences.zh: 融彼滯義，渙此潛文，儒道以析，九流以分。

translations.literal: He melted that stagnant meaning and dispersed this hidden writing; Confucian Way thereby analyzed; nine streams thereby divided.
translations.idiomatic: He melted stagnant meaning and dispersed hidden writing; the Confucian Way was thereby analyzed and the nine streams divided.

sentences.zh: 崔、宋二賢，誕性英偉，擢穎閭閻，聞名象魏。

translations.literal: The two worthies Cui and Song—innate nature heroic and great; they plucked brilliance from the lane gate; name heard in the elephant and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The two worthies Cui and Song were heroic and great by nature; they plucked brilliance from the lane gate and their names were heard at court.

sentences.zh: 謇謇儀形，邈邈風氣，達而不矜，素而能賁。

translations.literal: Stern, stern their bearing form; remote, remote their wind and air; reaching yet not proud; plain yet able to adorn.
translations.idiomatic: Stern their bearing, remote their wind and air; reaching yet not proud, plain yet able to adorn.

sentences.zh: 潘符摽尚，杜熙好和，清不潔流，渾不同波。

translations.literal: Pan Fu held high esteem; Du Xi loved harmony; pure without defiling the current; muddy without sharing the wave.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Fu held high esteem and Du Xi loved harmony; pure without defiling the current, muddy without sharing the wave.

sentences.zh: 絕希龍津，止分常科，幽而逾顯，損而逾多。

translations.literal: He utterly hoped for the dragon ford; stopping at the common grade; obscure yet more illustrious; diminished yet more abundant.
translations.idiomatic: He utterly hoped for the dragon ford yet stopped at the common grade; obscure yet more illustrious, diminished yet more abundant.

sentences.zh: 張綱柔謙，叔術正直，道雅洽聞，弼為兼識。

translations.literal: Zhang Gang was yielding and modest; Shushu upright; Daoya well versed in hearing; Bi assisted as doubly knowing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gang was yielding and modest, Shushu upright; Daoya was well versed in hearing and Bi assisted as doubly knowing.

sentences.zh: 拔萃衡門，俱漸鴻翼，發憤忘餐，豈要斗食。

translations.literal: Pulling out from the balance gate, together they gradually gained swan wings; issuing indignation they forgot meals—how could they want a peck of grain?
translations.idiomatic: Pulling out from the balance gate, together they gradually rose like swans; so driven they forgot meals—how could they want a peck of grain?

sentences.zh: 率禮從仁，罔愆于式，失不繫心，得不形色。

translations.literal: Leading ritual and following benevolence, without fault in the pattern; loss did not bind the heart; gain did not show in form and color.
translations.idiomatic: Leading ritual and following benevolence without fault in the pattern; loss did not bind the heart and gain did not show in form and color.

sentences.zh: 郎苗始舉，用均已試，智足周身，言足為治。

translations.literal: Lang Miao at first was raised; Yong Jun already tested; wisdom sufficed for the whole body; words sufficed for governing.
translations.idiomatic: Lang Miao was at first raised and Yong Jun already tested; wisdom sufficed for the whole body and words sufficed for governing.

sentences.zh: 性協於時，情敏於事，與今而同，與古曷異。

translations.literal: Nature harmonized with the time; feeling keen in affairs; with today the same, with antiquity how different?
translations.idiomatic: His nature harmonized with the time and his feeling was keen in affairs; with today the same—with antiquity how different?

sentences.zh: 物以利移，人以酒昏，侯生潔己，唯義是敦。

translations.literal: Things shift by profit; people by wine grow dim; Hou Sheng cleansed himself—only righteousness he honored.
translations.idiomatic: Things shift by profit and people by wine grow dim; Hou Sheng cleansed himself and honored only righteousness.

sentences.zh: 日縱醇醪，逾敬逾溫，其在私室，如涉公門。

translations.literal: Daily he poured rich wine yet grew more reverent and warm; in private chambers it was like treading the public gate.
translations.idiomatic: Daily he poured rich wine yet grew ever more reverent and warm; even in private chambers he conducted himself as if treading the public gate.

sentences.zh: 季才之性，柔而執競，屆彼南秦，申威致命。

translations.literal: Jicai's nature was yielding yet he held to striving; arriving in southern Qin he extended authority and gave command.
translations.idiomatic: Jicai's nature was yielding yet he held to striving; arriving in southern Qin he extended authority and asserted command.

sentences.zh: 誘之以權，矯之以正，帝道用光，邊土納慶。

translations.literal: Enticing by authority, correcting by the upright—the imperial Way thereby shone and border lands received celebration.
translations.idiomatic: Enticing by authority and correcting by the upright—the imperial Way thereby shone and border lands received celebration.

sentences.zh: 羣賢遭世，顯名有代，志竭其忠，才盡其概。

translations.literal: The host of worthies met the age; illustrious names had their generations; will exhausted their loyalty; talent exhausted their outline.
translations.idiomatic: The host of worthies met the age and illustrious names had their generations; will exhausted loyalty and talent exhausted its outline.

sentences.zh: 體襲朱裳，腰紐雙佩，榮曜當時，風高千載。

translations.literal: Form inherited vermilion robes; waist girded with double pendants; glory shone in the age; wind high for a thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Form inherited vermilion robes and waist girded with double pendants; glory shone in the age and wind high for a thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 君臣相遇，理實難偕，昔因朝命，舉之克諧。

translations.literal: Ruler and minister met; principle and reality hard to join; formerly because of court command they were raised and could harmonize.
translations.idiomatic: Ruler and minister met yet principle and reality were hard to join; formerly because of court command they were raised and could harmonize.

sentences.zh: [10]披衿散想，解帶舒懷，此忻如昨，存亡奄乖。

translations.literal: [10] Opening the lapel and scattering thought, loosening the belt and easing the breast—this delight like yesterday; survival and death suddenly parted.
translations.idiomatic: Opening the lapel and scattering thought, loosening the belt and easing the breast—this delight like yesterday; survival and death suddenly parted.

sentences.zh: 靜言思之，中心九摧，揮毫頌德，漼爾增哀。

translations.literal: Quiet words thinking of it—the center ninefold crushed; wielding brush to eulogize virtue, tearfully thus increased sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Quietly thinking of it—the heart ninefold crushed; wielding the brush to eulogize virtue, tears thus increased sorrow.

sentences.zh: 皇興中，詔允兼太常，至兗州祭孔子廟，謂允曰：「此簡德而行，勿有辭也。」

translations.literal: In Huangxing, an edict made Yun concurrently Grand Master of Ceremonies; arriving at Yanzhou to sacrifice at Confucius' temple, he told Yun: "This is simple virtue in action—do not decline."
translations.idiomatic: In Huangxing, an edict made Yun concurrently Grand Master of Ceremonies; arriving at Yanzhou to sacrifice at Confucius' temple, the emperor told Yun, "This is simple virtue in action—do not decline."

sentences.zh: 後允從顯祖北伐，大捷而還，至武川鎮，上北伐頌，其詞曰：「皇矣上天，降鑒惟德，眷命有魏，照臨萬國。

translations.literal: Later Yun followed Emperor Xianzu on the northern campaign; great victory and return; arriving at Wuchuan garrison, he submitted a northern campaign eulogy; its words say: "August Heaven, descending inspection only by virtue, entrusting mandate to Wei, shining over the myriad states.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yun followed Emperor Xianzu on the northern campaign and returned in great victory; arriving at Wuchuan garrison he submitted a northern campaign eulogy whose words say, "August Heaven, descending inspection only by virtue, entrusting mandate to Wei, shining over the myriad states.

sentences.zh: 禮化丕融，王猷允塞，靜亂以威，穆民以則。

translations.literal: Ritual transformation greatly blended; royal plans truly filled; stilling disorder by might; making tranquil the people by rule.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual transformation greatly blended and royal plans truly filled; stilling disorder by might and making tranquil the people by rule.

sentences.zh: 北虜舊隸，禀政在蕃，往因時□，逃命北轅。

translations.literal: The northern barbarians of old were subordinate; receiving government lay in the domains; going because of the time□, fleeing life to the northern shafts.
translations.idiomatic: The northern barbarians of old were subordinate and receiving government lay in the domains; going because of the time□, they fled for their lives to the northern shafts.

sentences.zh: 世襲凶軌，背忠食言，招亡聚盜，醜類實繁。

translations.literal: Generation after generation inherited vicious tracks; turning back on loyalty and eating words; recruiting the perished and gathering robbers—the ugly sort truly numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Generation after generation they inherited vicious tracks, turned back on loyalty and broke their words, recruited the perished and gathered robbers—the ugly sort truly numerous.

sentences.zh: 敢率犬羊，圖縱猖蹶，乃詔訓師，興戈北伐。

translations.literal: Daring to lead dogs and sheep, they plotted wanton rampage; thereupon an edict instructed the army and raised spears for northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Daring to lead dogs and sheep they plotted wanton rampage; thereupon an edict instructed the army and raised spears for the northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 躍馬裹糧，星馳電發，撲討虔劉，肆陳斧鉞。

translations.literal: Leaping horse, wrapping grain, stars hurrying and lightning issuing; striking and attacking the reverent slaughter, broadly displaying axe and yue.
translations.idiomatic: Leaping horse and wrapping grain, stars hurrying and lightning issuing; striking and attacking the enemy, broadly displaying axe and yue.

sentences.zh: 斧鉞暫陳，馘翦厥旅，積骸填谷，流血成浦。

translations.literal: Axe and yue briefly displayed; ears cut and brigade trimmed; piled corpses filled valleys; flowing blood became a stream.
translations.idiomatic: Axe and yue briefly displayed, ears cut and brigades trimmed; piled corpses filled valleys and flowing blood became a stream.

sentences.zh: 元兇狐奔，假息窮墅，爪牙既摧，腹心亦阻。

translations.literal: The chief villain fox-fled; borrowing breath in a poor lodge; claws and teeth already destroyed; belly and heart also blocked.
translations.idiomatic: The chief villain fox-fled, borrowing breath in a poor lodge; claws and teeth already destroyed and belly and heart also blocked.

sentences.zh: 周之忠厚，存及行葦，翼翼聖明，有兼斯美。

translations.literal: Zhou's generous honesty preserved even traveling reeds; cautious, cautious the sage brightness—having both this beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou's generous honesty extended even to traveling reeds; cautious and bright was the sage ruler—he possessed both this beauty.

sentences.zh: 澤被京觀，垂此仁旨，封尸野獲，惠加生死。

translations.literal: Grace covered the Jingguan; hanging this benevolent edict; sealing corpses in the wild and obtaining captives; favor added to life and death.
translations.idiomatic: Grace covered the Jingguan and hung this benevolent edict; sealing corpses in the wild and obtaining captives, favor added to life and death.

sentences.zh: 生死蒙惠，人欣覆育，理貫幽冥，澤漸殊域。

translations.literal: Life and death received grace; people rejoiced in overturning nurture; principle penetrated dark obscurity; grace gradually reached strange domains.
translations.idiomatic: Life and death received grace and people rejoiced in overturning nurture; principle penetrated dark obscurity and grace gradually reached strange domains.

sentences.zh: 物歸其誠，神獻其福，遐邇斯懷，無思不服。

translations.literal: Things returned to their sincerity; spirits presented their blessing; far and near thereby cherished; none thought but submission.
translations.idiomatic: Things returned to their sincerity and spirits presented their blessing; far and near thereby cherished—none thought but submission.

sentences.zh: 古稱善兵，歷時始捷，今也用師，辰不及浹。

translations.literal: Antiquity called good at arms—across seasons then victory; now using arms, the chen did not reach moistening.
translations.idiomatic: Antiquity called those good at arms victorious only across seasons; now using arms, victory came before the chen had moistened.

sentences.zh: 六軍克合，萬邦以協，義著春秋，功銘玉牒，載興頌聲，播之來葉。」

translations.literal: The six armies harmoniously joined; the myriad states thereby accorded; righteousness displayed in Spring and Autumn; merit inscribed on jade tablets; raising eulogy sound, spreading to coming generations."
translations.idiomatic: The six armies harmoniously joined and the myriad states thereby accorded; righteousness displayed in Spring and Autumn and merit inscribed on jade tablets; raising eulogy sound and spreading it to coming generations."

sentences.zh: 顯祖覽而善之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzu perused it and approved.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzu perused it and approved.

sentences.zh: 又顯祖時有不豫，以高祖沖幼，欲立京兆王子推，集諸大臣以次召問。

translations.literal: Also when Emperor Xianzu was unwell, because Emperor Gaozu was young and tender, he wished to establish the son of the Prince of Jingzhao, Tui; he gathered the great ministers and summoned them in order to ask.
translations.idiomatic: Also when Emperor Xianzu was unwell, because Emperor Xiaowen was young and tender, he wished to establish the son of the Prince of Jingzhao, Tui; he gathered the great ministers and summoned them in order to ask.

sentences.zh: 允進跪上前，涕泣曰：「臣不敢多言，以勞神聽，願陛下上思宗廟託付之重，追念周公抱成王之事。」

translations.literal: Yun advanced, knelt before the sovereign, wept and said: "Your servant dares not speak much to weary the divine hearing; I wish Your Majesty above to think of the weight of entrustment to the ancestral temples, recalling Duke of Zhou's embracing of King Cheng."
translations.idiomatic: Yun advanced, knelt before the sovereign, wept and said, "Your servant dares not speak much to weary the divine hearing; I wish Your Majesty above to think of the weight of entrustment to the ancestral temples and recall Duke of Zhou embracing King Cheng."

sentences.zh: 顯祖於是傳位於高祖，賜帛千匹，以標忠亮。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzu thereupon transmitted the throne to Emperor Gaozu and bestowed a thousand bolts of silk to mark loyal brightness.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzu thereupon transmitted the throne to Emperor Xiaowen and bestowed a thousand bolts of silk to mark loyal brightness.

sentences.zh: 又遷中書監，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Director of the Central Secretariat and added as Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Director of the Central Secretariat and appointed Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 雖久典史事，然而不能專勤屬述，時與校書郎劉模有所緝綴，大較續崔浩故事，準春秋之體，而時有刊正。

translations.literal: Though long managing historical affairs, yet he could not exclusively and diligently attend to composition; at times with Proofreader Liu Mo there was some collation and binding—in the main continuing Cui Hao's precedent, taking Spring and Autumn as the body, yet at times having revision and correction.
translations.idiomatic: Though long managing historical affairs, he could not exclusively and diligently attend to composition; at times with Proofreader Liu Mo he collated and bound—in the main continuing Cui Hao's precedent on the model of Spring and Autumn, yet at times revising and correcting.

sentences.zh: 自高宗迄于顯祖，軍國書檄，多允文也。

translations.literal: From Emperor Gaozong through Emperor Xianzu, military and state documents and proclamations were mostly Yun's writing.
translations.idiomatic: From Emperor Wencheng through Emperor Xianzu, military and state documents and proclamations were mostly Yun's writing.

sentences.zh: 末年乃薦高閭以自代。

translations.literal: In his late years he then recommended Gao Lu to replace himself.
translations.idiomatic: In his final years he recommended Gao Lu to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 以定議之勳，進爵咸陽公，加鎮東將軍。

translations.literal: Because of the merit in fixing the succession, he was advanced in rank to Duke of Xianyang and added as General Who Pacifies the East.
translations.idiomatic: For merit in fixing the succession he was ennobled Duke of Xianyang and made General Who Pacifies the East.

sentences.zh: 尋授使持節、散騎常侍、征西將軍、懷州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, General Who Conquers the West, and Regional Inspector of Huaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, General Who Conquers the West, and Regional Inspector of Huaizhou.

sentences.zh: 允秋月巡境，問民疾苦。

translations.literal: In autumn of the eighth month Yun inspected the borders and inquired into the people's suffering.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn Yun toured the borders and asked after the people's hardships.

sentences.zh: 至邵縣，見邵公廟廢毀不立，乃曰：「邵公之德，闕而不禮，為善者何望。」

translations.literal: Arriving at Shao County, he saw Duke Shao's temple abandoned and destroyed, not established; he said: "Duke Shao's virtue—lacking yet not ritually honored—what hope for those who do good?"
translations.idiomatic: Arriving at Shao County, he saw Duke Shao's temple abandoned and not established; he said, "Duke Shao's virtue—lacking yet not ritually honored—what hope for those who do good?"

sentences.zh: 乃表聞修葺之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he memorialized and reported to repair it.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he memorialized and reported to repair it.

sentences.zh: 允於時年將九十矣，勸民學業，風化頗行。

translations.literal: Yun at that time was nearly ninety; he encouraged the people in learning and enterprise, and transformation and instruction were considerably practiced.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was then nearly ninety; he urged the people toward learning and custom was considerably reformed.

sentences.zh: 然儒者優遊，不以斷決為事。

translations.literal: Yet Confucian scholars were at ease and did not take deciding judgments as their affair.
translations.idiomatic: Yet as a Confucian scholar he was at ease and did not make deciding judgments his chief concern.

sentences.zh: 後正光中，中散大夫、中書舍人河內常景追思允，帥郡中故老，為允立祠於野王之南，樹碑紀德焉。

translations.literal: Later in Zhengguang, Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and Gentleman Attendant of the Central Secretariat Chang Jing of Henei recalled Yun; leading the commandery's old elders, he established a shrine for Yun south of Yewang and set up a stele recording virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Later in Zhengguang, Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and Gentleman Attendant of the Central Secretariat Chang Jing of Henei recalled Yun; leading the commandery's old elders, he established a shrine for Yun south of Yewang and set up a stele recording his virtue.

sentences.zh: 太和二年，又以老乞還鄉里，十餘章，上卒不聽許，遂以疾告歸。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taihe, again because of old age he begged to return to his native village; more than ten memorials—the sovereign ultimately did not listen and permit; thereupon because of illness he announced return.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taihe, again because of old age he begged to return to his native village in more than ten memorials—the sovereign ultimately did not listen and permit; thereupon because of illness he announced return.

sentences.zh: 其年，詔以安車徵允，敕州郡發遣。

translations.literal: That year, an edict used the comfort carriage to summon Yun; it ordered commanderies and states to send him forth.
translations.idiomatic: That year, an edict used the comfort carriage to summon Yun and ordered commanderies and states to send him forth.

sentences.zh: 至都，拜鎮軍大將軍，領中書監。

translations.literal: Arriving at the capital, he was appointed General Who Pacifies the Army and concurrently Director of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the capital he was appointed General Who Pacifies the Army and Director of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 固辭不許。

translations.literal: He firmly declined and was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined but was not allowed.

sentences.zh: 又扶引就內，改定皇誥。

translations.literal: Again he was supported and led within; the imperial edict was revised and fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Again he was supported and led within to revise and fix the imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 允上酒訓曰：

translations.literal: Yun submitted his Wine Admonition, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Yun submitted his Admonition on Wine, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣被敕論集往世酒之敗德，以為酒訓。

translations.literal: Your servant received the edict to discuss and gather the failures of virtue from wine in former ages, taking it as the Wine Admonition.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant was ordered to gather instances where wine ruined virtue in former ages and compose an admonition on wine.

sentences.zh: 臣以朽邁，人倫所棄，而殊恩過隆，錄臣於將歿之年，勗臣於已墜之地。

translations.literal: Your servant, with decayed old age, is abandoned by human relations, yet special grace was excessively lofty—recording your servant in the year of approaching death, encouraging your servant on already fallen ground.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant, with decayed old age, is abandoned by human relations, yet special grace was excessively lofty—recording me in the year of approaching death and encouraging me on already fallen ground.

sentences.zh: 奉命驚惶，喜懼兼甚，不知何事可以上答。

translations.literal: Receiving the command I was startled and fearful, joy and fear together extreme—I do not know by what affair I can respond above.
translations.idiomatic: Receiving the command I was startled and afraid, joy and fear both extreme—I do not know what I can offer in reply.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下以叡哲之姿，撫臨萬國，太皇太后以聖德之廣，濟育羣生。

translations.literal: Prostrating myself I reflect: Your Majesty with sagely wisdom's bearing presides over the myriad states; the Grand Empress Dowager with sagely virtue's breadth nourishes and rears the host of life.
translations.idiomatic: Prostrating myself I reflect: Your Majesty with sagely wisdom presides over the myriad states; the Grand Empress Dowager with sagely virtue nourishes and rears the host of life.

sentences.zh: 普天之下，罔不稱賴。

translations.literal: Under all Heaven, none did not call and rely.
translations.idiomatic: Under Heaven all relied on them.

sentences.zh: 然日昃憂勤，虛求不已，思監往事，以為警戒。

translations.literal: Yet daily you lean toward worry and diligence, empty seeking without cease, thinking to mirror past affairs to take as warning.
translations.idiomatic: Yet daily you lean toward worry and diligence, empty seeking without cease, thinking to mirror past affairs as warning.

sentences.zh: 此之至誠，悟通百靈，而況於百官士民。

translations.literal: This utmost sincerity penetrates the hundred spirits—how much more the hundred officials and scholar-commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Such utmost sincerity moves the hundred spirits—how much more the officials and common people.

sentences.zh: 不勝踴躍，謹竭其所見，作酒訓一篇。

translations.literal: Unable to contain my leaping, I respectfully exhaust what I have seen and compose one chapter of the Wine Admonition.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to contain my joy, I respectfully set forth what I have observed in one chapter of the Wine Admonition.

sentences.zh: 但臣愚短，加以荒廢，辭義鄙拙，不足觀採。

translations.literal: But your servant is foolish and short, added to wasteland and abandonment; words and meaning are base and crude—not sufficient for viewing and gathering.
translations.idiomatic: But I am foolish and brief of talent, added to age and decay; my words are crude and unworthy of notice.

sentences.zh: 伏願聖慈，體臣悾悾之情，恕臣狂瞽之意。

translations.literal: I prostrate my wish for holy compassion to embody your servant's sincere sincere feeling and forgive your servant's mad and blind intent.
translations.idiomatic: I prostrate my wish for holy compassion to embody my sincere feeling and forgive my mad and blind intent.

sentences.zh: 其詞曰：

translations.literal: Its words say:
translations.idiomatic: The text reads:

sentences.zh: 自古聖王，其為饗也，玄酒在堂而𨣧酒在下，所以崇本重原，降於滋味。

translations.literal: From antiquity the sage kings, in what they feasted, placed dark wine in the hall while fermented wine was below—thereby honoring the root and weighting the origin, lowering to flavor.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity sage kings at their feasts placed dark wine in the hall and fermented wine below, thereby honoring the root and subordinating flavor.

sentences.zh: 雖汎爵旅行，不及於亂。

translations.literal: Though cups were passed and travel practiced, it did not reach disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Though cups passed in procession, they did not reach disorder.

sentences.zh: 故能禮章而敬不虧，事畢而儀不忒。

translations.literal: Therefore ritual chapters and respect were not impaired; affairs completed and ceremony without error.
translations.idiomatic: Thus ritual was preserved and respect unimpaired; when the affair ended the ceremony was without flaw.

sentences.zh: 非由斯致，是失其道。

translations.literal: If not achieved by this, this is losing the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Without this one loses the Way.

sentences.zh: 將何以範時軌物，垂之於世？

translations.literal: How will one model the age and regulate things, handing down to the generations?
translations.idiomatic: How then can one model the age, regulate things, and hand them down to posterity?

sentences.zh: 歷觀往代成敗之效，吉凶由人，不在數也。

translations.literal: Passing through observation of former generations' success and failure effects—fortune and misfortune lie in people, not in numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through observation of former generations' success and failure—fortune and misfortune lie in people, not in numbers.

sentences.zh: 商辛耽酒，殷道以之亡；

translations.literal: Shang Xin indulged in wine; Yin Way thereby perished;
translations.idiomatic: Shang Xin indulged in wine and the Yin Way thereby perished;

sentences.zh: 公旦陳誥，周德以之昌。

translations.literal: Duke of Zhou presented the announcement; Zhou virtue thereby flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Zhou presented the announcement and Zhou virtue thereby flourished.

sentences.zh: 子反昏酣而致斃，穆生不飲而身光。

translations.literal: Zi Fan muddled and drunk thereby met death; Mu Sheng did not drink and his person shone.
translations.idiomatic: Zi Fan, muddled with drink, met his death; Mu Sheng, who did not drink, kept his person bright.

sentences.zh: 或長世而為戒，或百代而流芳。

translations.literal: Some long generations and became warning; some hundred generations and flowed fragrance.
translations.idiomatic: Some became warnings for long generations; some flowed fragrant for a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 酒之為狀，變惑情性，雖曰哲人，孰能自競。

translations.literal: Wine's form as state transforms and confuses nature and feeling; though called wise men, who can self-strive?
translations.idiomatic: Wine transforms and confuses nature and feeling; even the wise—who can contend with it?

sentences.zh: 在官者殆於政也，為下者慢於令也，聰達之士荒於聽也，柔順之倫興於諍也，久而不悛，致於病也。

translations.literal: Those in office nearly fail in government; those below are negligent in orders; intelligent and penetrating scholars are wasteland in hearing; yielding and compliant relations rise in strife; long without repentance, reaching to sickness.
translations.idiomatic: Officials neglect government, subordinates slight commands, the keen-eared grow dull in hearing, the yielding breed strife, and long indulgence leads to ruin.

sentences.zh: 豈止於病，乃損其命。

translations.literal: It does not stop at sickness—it even damages one's life.
translations.idiomatic: It does not stop at illness—it can cost a person his life.

sentences.zh: 諺亦有云：其益如毫，其損如刀。

translations.literal: The proverb also says: its benefit is like a hair, its harm is like a knife.
translations.idiomatic: As the proverb says: its benefit is like a hair, its harm like a knife.

sentences.zh: 言所益者止於一味之益，不亦寡乎。

translations.literal: What is said of benefit stops at the benefit of one flavor—is it not meager?
translations.idiomatic: The benefit spoken of extends only to the pleasure of taste—is that not meager?

sentences.zh: 言所損者夭年亂志，夭亂之損，不亦夥乎。

translations.literal: What is said of harm is shortened years and disordered will; the harm of shortened years and disorder—is it not abundant?
translations.idiomatic: The harm is shortened years and a disordered will; harm to life and order—is that not abundant?

sentences.zh: 無以酒荒而陷其身，無以酒狂而喪其倫。

translations.literal: Do not because of wine's excess ruin yourself; do not because of wine's madness lose your human relations.
translations.idiomatic: Do not ruin yourself in wine's excess, nor lose your human relations in wine's madness.

sentences.zh: 迷邦失道，流浪漂津。

translations.literal: Confusing the state and losing the Way, drifting on the ford.
translations.idiomatic: You will confuse the state, lose the Way, and drift on the current.

sentences.zh: 不師不遵，反將何因。

translations.literal: Not taking teachers, not following rules—on what basis then?
translations.idiomatic: Without teachers and without following rules—on what basis will you act?

sentences.zh: 詩不言乎，「如切如瑳，如琢如磨」，朋友之義也。

translations.literal: Does the Poetry not say, "As you cut and file, as you carve and polish"—the meaning of friendship?
translations.idiomatic: Does the Poetry not say, "As you cut and file, as you carve and polish"—that is the meaning of friendship.

sentences.zh: 作官以箴之，申謨以禁之，君臣之道也。

translations.literal: Making office to admonish, extending counsels to forbid—this is the Way of ruler and minister.
translations.idiomatic: Officials admonish and counsels forbid—such is the Way of ruler and minister.

sentences.zh: 其言也善，則三覆而佩之；

translations.literal: If the words are good, then thrice review and wear them on the belt;
translations.idiomatic: If the words are good, review them thrice and wear them at your belt;

sentences.zh: 言之不善，則哀矜而貸之。

translations.literal: if the words are not good, then pity and pardon them.
translations.idiomatic: if the words are not good, pity them and grant pardon.

sentences.zh: 此實先王納規之意。

translations.literal: This is truly the meaning of the former kings' receiving remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: This is truly how the former kings received remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 往者有晉，士多失度，肆散誕以為不羇，縱長酣以為高達，調酒之頌，[11]以相眩曜。

translations.literal: Formerly in Jin, scholars mostly lost measure; they spread dissipation and called it unbound, indulged long drunkenness and called it lofty attainment, and songs praising wine[11] to dazzle one another.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly in Jin scholars mostly lost measure; they spread dissipation and called it freedom, indulged long drunkenness and called it lofty attainment, and songs praising wine[11] to dazzle one another.

sentences.zh: 稱堯舜有千鍾百觚之飲，著非法之言，引大聖為譬，以則天之明，豈其然乎？

translations.literal: They claimed Yao and Shun had drinks of a thousand bells and hundred cups, set forth unlawful words, cited the great sage as comparison, and took Heaven's clarity as norm—is it really so?
translations.idiomatic: They claimed Yao and Shun drank a thousand bells and hundred cups, set forth unlawful words, cited the great sage as example, and took Heaven's clarity as their norm—is it really so?

sentences.zh: 且子思有云，夫子之飲，不能一升。

translations.literal: Moreover Zisi said that the Master's drinking could not reach one sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Zisi said the Master's drinking could not reach one sheng.

sentences.zh: 以此推之，千鍾百觚皆為妄也。

translations.literal: Pushing from this, a thousand bells and hundred cups are all false.
translations.idiomatic: By this reasoning, a thousand bells and hundred cups are all false.

sentences.zh: 今大魏應圖，重明御世，化之所暨，無思不服，仁風敦洽於四海。

translations.literal: Now Great Wei responds to the chart, doubly bright governing the age; where transformation reaches, none fails to submit; benevolent wind thickly harmonizes within the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: Now Great Wei responds to the chart and governs with redoubled brilliance; where transformation reaches none fails to submit, and benevolent wind thickly harmonizes the four seas.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后以至德之隆，誨而不倦，憂勤備於皇情，誥訓行於無外。

translations.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager with utmost virtue's loftiness instructs without weariness; worry and diligence complete in the imperial feeling; edicts and instructions proceed without.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Empress Dowager with utmost virtue instructs without weariness; worry and diligence fill the imperial heart; edicts and instructions proceed everywhere.

sentences.zh: 故能道協兩儀，功同覆載。

translations.literal: Therefore the Way harmonizes the two principles; merit equals covering and bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the Way harmonizes the two principles and merit equals that of heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 仁恩下逮，罔有不遵，普天率土，靡不蒙賴。

translations.literal: Benevolent grace reaches below; none do not follow; all under Heaven and the leading earth—none do not receive reliance.
translations.idiomatic: Benevolent grace reaches below and none fail to follow; all under Heaven and the leading earth receive its reliance.

sentences.zh: 在朝之士，有志之人，宜克己從善，履正存貞。

translations.literal: Scholars in court with aspiring will should restrain themselves and follow goodness, tread the upright and preserve constancy.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars in court with aspiring will should restrain themselves and follow goodness, tread the upright path and preserve constancy.

sentences.zh: 節酒以為度，順德以為經。

translations.literal: Moderate wine to make a measure; follow virtue to make a warp.
translations.idiomatic: Take moderation in wine as your measure and following virtue as your warp.

sentences.zh: 悟昏飲之美疾，審敬慎之彌榮。

translations.literal: Comprehend the beautiful illness of muddled drinking; examine how respect and caution grow ever more glorious.
translations.idiomatic: Comprehend the grave harm of muddled drinking and see how respect and caution grow ever more glorious.

sentences.zh: 遵孝道以致養，顯父母而揚名。

translations.literal: Follow filial Way to achieve nurture; display parents and spread name.
translations.idiomatic: Follow the filial Way to nurture your parents and spread their name.

sentences.zh: 蹈閔曾之前軌，遺仁風於後生。

translations.literal: Tread the former tracks of Min and Zeng; leave benevolent wind for later generations.
translations.idiomatic: Tread the former tracks of Min and Zeng and leave benevolent wind for later generations.

sentences.zh: 仰以答所授，俯以保其成。

translations.literal: Looking up to answer what was entrusted; looking down to preserve what was accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Look up to answer what was entrusted; look down to preserve what was accomplished.

sentences.zh: 可不勉歟！

translations.literal: Can you not exert yourselves!
translations.idiomatic: You must exert yourselves!

sentences.zh: 可不勉歟！

translations.literal: Can you not exert yourselves!
translations.idiomatic: Surely you must exert yourselves!

sentences.zh: 高祖悅之，常置左右。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu was pleased with it and often placed it at his left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen was pleased with it and often kept it at his side.

sentences.zh: 詔允乘車入殿，朝賀不拜。

translations.literal: An edict allowed Yun to ride a carriage into the hall; at court congratulations he did not bow.
translations.idiomatic: An edict permitted Yun to ride a carriage into the hall and exempted him from bowing at court congratulations.

sentences.zh: 明年，詔允議定律令。

translations.literal: The next year, an edict ordered Yun to deliberate on drafting laws and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: The following year an edict ordered Yun to deliberate on drafting laws and ordinances.

sentences.zh: 雖年漸期頤，而志識無損，猶心存舊職，披考史書。

translations.literal: Though his years gradually reached the term of centenarian, his will and knowledge were undiminished; he still bore the old office in mind and perused and examined historical records.
