translations.idiomatic: Though his years gradually reached a centenarian term, his will and knowledge were undiminished; he still bore his old duties in mind and perused historical records.

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「允年涉危境，而家貧養薄。

translations.literal: Another edict said: "Yun's years touch the perilous border, yet his household is poor and nurture thin.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict said, "Yun's years touch the perilous border, yet his household is poor and his nurture thin.

sentences.zh: 可令樂部絲竹十人，五日一詣允，以娛其志。」

translations.literal: Let the Music Bureau provide ten string and bamboo players; every five days let them visit Yun to please his will."
translations.idiomatic: Let the Music Bureau provide ten musicians; every five days they were to visit Yun to please his spirit.

sentences.zh: 特賜允蜀牛一頭，四望蜀車一乘，素几杖各一，蜀刀一口。

translations.literal: He specially bestowed Yun one Shu ox, one four-canopied Shu carriage, one plain table and cane each, and one Shu knife.
translations.idiomatic: He specially bestowed Yun one Shu ox, one four-canopied Shu carriage, one plain table and cane each, and one Shu knife.

sentences.zh: 又賜珍味，每春秋常致之。

translations.literal: He also bestowed delicacies; each spring and autumn he regularly sent them.
translations.idiomatic: He also bestowed delicacies, sent regularly each spring and autumn.

sentences.zh: 尋詔朝晡給膳，朔望致牛酒，衣服綿絹，每月送給。

translations.literal: Soon an edict provided morning and evening meals, on the first and fifteenth of the month sent ox and wine, and clothes of cotton silk supplied and sent each month.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict provided morning and evening meals, on the first and fifteenth sent ox and wine, and cotton silk clothes supplied monthly.

sentences.zh: 允皆分之親故。

translations.literal: Yun all divided them among kin and old friends.
translations.idiomatic: Yun divided them all among kin and old friends.

sentences.zh: 是時貴臣之門，皆羅列顯官，而允子弟皆無官爵。

translations.literal: At that time the gates of noble ministers all arrayed illustrious officials, yet Yun's sons and younger brothers all had no office or rank.
translations.idiomatic: At that time noble ministers' gates all arrayed illustrious officials, yet none of Yun's sons or younger brothers held office or rank.

sentences.zh: 其廉退若此。

translations.literal: His integrity and withdrawal were like this.
translations.idiomatic: His integrity and withdrawal were of this kind.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書、散騎常侍，時延入，備几杖，問以政治。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry; at times he was summoned in, provided with table and cane, and asked about government.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry; at times he was summoned in, provided with table and cane, and questioned on government.

sentences.zh: 十年，加光祿大夫、金章紫綬。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was added Grand Master of the Palace and golden seal with purple cord.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was made Grand Master of the Palace with golden seal and purple cord.

sentences.zh: 朝之大議，皆咨訪焉。

translations.literal: Great deliberations of the court all consulted and inquired of him.
translations.idiomatic: The court's great deliberations all consulted him.

sentences.zh: 魏初法嚴，朝士多見杖罰。

translations.literal: In early Wei the law was strict; court scholars were often seen beaten and punished.
translations.idiomatic: In early Wei the law was strict and court scholars were often beaten and punished.

sentences.zh: 允歷事五帝，出入三省，五十餘年，初無譴咎。

translations.literal: Yun served through five emperors, entering and leaving the three secretariats for more than fifty years, at first without reprimand or fault.
translations.idiomatic: Yun served through five emperors, entering and leaving the three secretariats for more than fifty years, without a single reprimand or fault.

sentences.zh: 初，真君中以獄訟留滯，始令中書以經義斷諸疑事。

translations.literal: At first, in the Zhenjun era because litigation was detained and delayed, it was first ordered that the Central Secretariat use canonical meaning to decide doubtful matters.
translations.idiomatic: At first, in the Zhenjun era because litigation was detained and delayed, the Central Secretariat was first ordered to use canonical meaning to decide doubtful matters.

sentences.zh: 允據律評刑，三十餘載，內外稱平。

translations.literal: Yun according to statute evaluated punishments for more than thirty years; inner and outer called it even.
translations.idiomatic: Yun judged punishments according to statute for more than thirty years; inner and outer circles called it even-handed.

sentences.zh: 允以獄者民之命也，常歎曰：「臯陶至德也，其後英蓼先亡，劉項之際，英布黥而王。

translations.literal: Yun because litigation is the people's life, often sighed and said: "Gao Yao had utmost virtue; afterward Ying and Liao perished first; at the Liu and Xiang transition, Ying Bu was tattooed and became king.
translations.idiomatic: Yun, because litigation is the people's life, often sighed and said, "Gao Yao had utmost virtue, yet afterward Ying and Liao perished first; at the Liu and Xiang transition Ying Bu was tattooed and made king.

sentences.zh: 經世雖久，猶有刑之餘釁。

translations.literal: Though the age since has been long, there are still remaining stigmas of punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Though ages have passed since, there remain stigmas of punishment.

sentences.zh: 況凡人能無咎乎？」

translations.literal: How much more can ordinary men be without fault?"
translations.idiomatic: How much less can ordinary men be without fault?

sentences.zh: 其年四月，有事西郊，詔以御馬車迎允就郊所板殿觀矚。

translations.literal: That year in the fourth month there was business at the western suburb; an edict used the imperial carriage to welcome Yun to the suburban lodge's plank hall to observe.
translations.idiomatic: That year in the fourth month there was a rite at the western suburb; an edict used the imperial carriage to bring Yun to the suburban plank hall to observe.

sentences.zh: 馬忽驚奔，車覆，傷眉三處。

translations.literal: The horse suddenly startled and ran; the carriage overturned; three places on his brow were injured.
translations.idiomatic: The horse suddenly startled and ran; the carriage overturned and his brow was injured in three places.

sentences.zh: 高祖、文明太后遣醫藥護治，存問相望。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu and Empress Dowager Wenming sent medicine to nurse and treat him; inquiries and visits followed one another.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen and Empress Dowager Wenming sent medicine to nurse him; inquiries and visits followed one another.

sentences.zh: 司駕將處重坐，允啟陳無恙，乞免其罪。

translations.literal: The Director of Imperial Transport was to impose heavy punishment; Yun memorialized stating he was unharmed and begged to exempt their crime.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Imperial Transport was to impose heavy punishment; Yun memorialized that he was unharmed and begged to exempt their crime.

sentences.zh: 先是，命中黃門蘇興壽扶持允，曾雪中遇犬驚倒，扶者大懼。

translations.literal: Before this, he had ordered the inner yellow gate Su Xingshou to support Yun; once in snow they met a dog that startled and knocked him down; the supporter was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Before this he had ordered the inner yellow gate Su Xingshou to support Yun; once in snow they met a dog that startled and knocked him down, and the supporter was greatly afraid.

sentences.zh: 允慰勉之，不令聞徹。

translations.literal: Yun comforted and encouraged him, not letting it be heard throughout.
translations.idiomatic: Yun comforted and encouraged him, not letting the matter be reported.

sentences.zh: 興壽稱共允接事三年，未嘗見其忿色。

translations.literal: Xingshou said that together with Yun he attended to affairs for three years and had never seen the color of his anger.
translations.idiomatic: Xingshou said that together with Yun he attended to affairs for three years and had never seen him show anger.

sentences.zh: 恂恂善誘，誨人不倦。

translations.literal: Assiduous and assiduous, good at guiding; he instructed people without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Assiduous and good at guiding, he instructed people without weariness.

sentences.zh: 晝夜手常執書，吟詠尋覽。

translations.literal: Day and night his hand constantly held books; he chanted and sought through them.
translations.idiomatic: Day and night his hand constantly held books; he chanted and browsed through them.

sentences.zh: 篤親念故，虛己存納。

translations.literal: He was devoted to kin and mindful of old ties; empty of self he received and admitted.
translations.idiomatic: He was devoted to kin and mindful of old ties; empty of self he received others.

sentences.zh: 雖處貴重，志同貧素。

translations.literal: Though he occupied honored and weighty position, his will was the same as poverty and plainness.
translations.idiomatic: Though he occupied honored and weighty position, his will matched poverty and plainness.

sentences.zh: 性好音樂，每至伶人弦歌鼓舞，常擊節稱善。

translations.literal: His nature loved music; whenever actors strummed, sang, drummed, and danced, he often beat time and praised their excellence.
translations.idiomatic: His nature loved music; whenever actors strummed, sang, drummed, and danced, he often beat time and praised them.

sentences.zh: 又雅信佛道，時設齋講，好生惡殺。

translations.literal: He also elegantly believed the Buddhist Way; at times he set up fasts and lectures; he loved life and hated killing.
translations.idiomatic: He also devoutly believed the Buddhist Way; at times he set up fasts and lectures; he loved life and hated killing.

sentences.zh: 性又簡至，不妄交遊。

translations.literal: His nature was also simple and direct; he did not rashly associate and travel.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was also simple and direct; he did not associate rashly.

sentences.zh: 顯祖平青齊，徙其族望於代。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzu pacified Qing and Qi and moved their clan prominence to Dai.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzu pacified Qing and Qi he moved their clan prominence to Dai.

sentences.zh: 時諸士人流移遠至，率皆飢寒。

translations.literal: At that time the various scholars who flowed and moved from afar mostly all suffered hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: At that time scholars who flowed in from afar mostly suffered hunger and cold.

sentences.zh: 徙人之中，多允姻媾，皆徒步造門。

translations.literal: Among the relocated people many were Yun's affines by marriage; all came on foot to his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Among the relocated many were Yun's affines by marriage; all came on foot to his gate.

sentences.zh: 允散財竭產，以相贍賑，慰問周至。

translations.literal: Yun scattered wealth and exhausted property to relieve and aid them; his inquiries and comfort were thorough.
translations.idiomatic: Yun scattered wealth and exhausted his property to relieve them; his inquiries and comfort were thorough.

sentences.zh: 無不感其仁厚。

translations.literal: None did not feel his benevolence and generosity.
translations.idiomatic: None failed to feel his benevolence and generosity.

sentences.zh: 收其才能，表奏申用。

translations.literal: He gathered their talent and ability and memorialized to report and employ them.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered their talents and memorialized to have them employed.

sentences.zh: 時議者皆以新附致異，允謂取材任能，無宜抑屈。

translations.literal: At that time discussants all took newly attached as causing difference; Yun said to take material and assign ability—there should be no suppressing and bending.
translations.idiomatic: At that time discussants all took newly attached men as causing difference; Yun said to take material and assign ability and not suppress them.

sentences.zh: 先是，允被召在方山作頌，志氣猶不多損，談說舊事，了無所遺。

translations.literal: Before this, when Yun was summoned at Fangshan to compose an eulogy, his vital energy was still not much diminished; discussing old affairs, nothing was left out.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, when Yun was summoned at Fangshan to compose an eulogy, his vital energy was still not much diminished; discussing old affairs, he forgot nothing.

sentences.zh: 十一年正月卒，年九十八。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, first month, he died, aged ninety-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, first month, he died at the age of ninety-eight.

sentences.zh: 初，允每謂人曰：「吾在中書時有陰德，濟救民命。

translations.literal: At first Yun often told people: "When I was in the Central Secretariat I had hidden virtue and rescued the people's lives.
translations.idiomatic: At first Yun often told people, "When I was in the Central Secretariat I had hidden virtue and rescued people's lives.

sentences.zh: 若陽報不差，吾壽應享百年矣。」

translations.literal: If yang recompense is not in error, my years ought to enjoy a hundred."
translations.idiomatic: If yang recompense is not in error, my years ought to reach a hundred."

sentences.zh: 先卒旬外，微有不適。

translations.literal: More than ten days before he died he had slight discomfort.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten days before he died he had slight discomfort.

sentences.zh: 猶不寢臥，呼醫請藥，出入行止，吟詠如常。

translations.literal: He still did not lie down to sleep; he called doctors and requested medicine; going out and coming in, chanting and singing as usual.
translations.idiomatic: He still did not lie down to sleep; he called doctors and requested medicine; going out and coming in, he chanted and sang as usual.

sentences.zh: 高祖、文明太后聞而遣醫李脩往脉視之，告以無恙。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu and Empress Dowager Wenming heard and sent the physician Li Xiu to go feel his pulse and look at him, reporting that there was no harm.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen and Empress Dowager Wenming heard and sent the physician Li Xiu to feel his pulse, reporting that there was no harm.

sentences.zh: 脩入，密陳允榮衞有異，懼其不久。

translations.literal: Xiu entered and secretly stated that Yun's glory and guard had strangeness; he feared he would not last long.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu entered and secretly stated that Yun's glory and guard showed strangeness; he feared Yun would not last long.

sentences.zh: 於是遣使備賜御膳珍羞，自酒米至於鹽醢百有餘品，皆盡時味，及牀帳、衣服、茵被、几杖，羅列於庭。

translations.literal: Thereupon envoys were sent prepared with imperial meals and delicacies—from wine and grain to salt and pickles more than a hundred kinds, all the season's flavors, and bed curtains, clothes, mats, cushions, tables, and canes, arrayed in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon envoys were sent with imperial meals and delicacies—from wine and grain to salt and pickles more than a hundred kinds, all the season's flavors, and bed curtains, clothes, mats, cushions, tables, and canes arrayed in the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 王官往還，慰問相屬。

translations.literal: Royal officials came and went; condolences and inquiries followed one another.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials came and went and condolences followed in succession.

sentences.zh: 允喜形於色，語人曰：「天恩以我篤老，大有所賚，得以贍客矣。」

translations.literal: Yun's joy showed in his form; he told people: "Heaven's grace, because I am sincerely old, greatly bestows on me; I can thereby entertain guests."
translations.idiomatic: Yun's joy showed in his form; he told people, "Heaven's grace, because I am sincerely old, greatly bestows on me—I can thereby entertain guests."

sentences.zh: 表謝而已，不有他慮。

translations.literal: He memorialized thanks only, without other concern.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized thanks only and had no other concern.

sentences.zh: 如是數日，夜中卒，家人莫覺。

translations.literal: Thus for several days; in the middle of the night he died; his household did not notice.
translations.idiomatic: Thus for several days; in the middle of the night he died and his household did not notice.

sentences.zh: 詔給絹一千匹、布二千匹、綿五百斤、錦五十匹、雜綵百匹、穀千斛以周喪用。

translations.literal: An edict bestowed a thousand bolts of silk, two thousand bolts of cloth, five hundred jin of cotton, fifty bolts of brocade, a hundred bolts of mixed silks, and a thousand hu of grain for funeral use.
translations.idiomatic: An edict bestowed a thousand bolts of silk, two thousand bolts of cloth, five hundred jin of cotton, fifty bolts of brocade, a hundred bolts of mixed silks, and a thousand hu of grain for funeral expenses.

sentences.zh: 魏初以來，存亡蒙賚者莫及焉，朝庭榮之。

translations.literal: From early Wei onward, none who survived or perished received grace like this; the court honored it.
translations.idiomatic: From early Wei onward none who survived or perished received grace like this; the court honored it.

sentences.zh: 將葬，贈侍中、司空公、冀州刺史，將軍、公如故，諡曰文，賜命服一襲。

translations.literal: When about to bury, he was posthumously given Attendant-in-Ordinary, Duke of the Ministry of Works, Regional Inspector of Jizhou; general and duke as before; posthumous name Wen; one set of command robes bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: When about to bury he was posthumously given Attendant-in-Ordinary, Duke of the Ministry of Works, Regional Inspector of Jizhou; general and duke as before; posthumous name Wen; one set of command robes bestowed.

sentences.zh: 允所製詩賦誄頌箴論表讚，左氏、公羊釋，毛詩拾遺，論雜解，[12]議何鄭膏肓事，凡百餘篇，別有集行於世。

translations.literal: What Yun composed—poems, rhapsodies, dirges, eulogies, admonitions, discourses, memorials, praises, Zuo's and Gongyang's explanations, Mao's Odes gleanings, miscellaneous explanations,[12] discussion of He and Zheng's incurable cases—in all more than a hundred chapters; separately there is a collected work circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: What Yun composed—poems, rhapsodies, dirges, eulogies, admonitions, discourses, memorials, praises, Zuo's and Gongyang's explanations, Mao's Odes gleanings, miscellaneous explanations,[12] discussion of He and Zheng's incurable cases—in all more than a hundred chapters; separately a collected work circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 允明算法，為算術三卷。

translations.literal: Yun understood calculation methods and made three chapters on arithmetic.
translations.idiomatic: Yun understood calculation methods and composed three chapters on arithmetic.

sentences.zh: 子忱襲。

translations.literal: His son Chen inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chen succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 忱，字士和。

translations.literal: Chen, styled Shihe.
translations.idiomatic: Chen, whose courtesy name was Shihe.

sentences.zh: 以父任除綏遠將軍、長樂太守。

translations.literal: Because of his father he was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distant and Administrator of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: Through his father's privilege he was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distant and Administrator of Changle.

sentences.zh: 為政寬惠，民庶安之。

translations.literal: In governing he was lenient and generous; the people were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: In governing he was lenient and generous and the people were at peace.

sentences.zh: 後例降爵為侯。

translations.literal: Later by precedent his rank was reduced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Later, by precedent, his noble rank was reduced to marquis.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon he died.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died.

sentences.zh: 孫貴賓，襲。

translations.literal: Grandson Binke inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Binke succeeded.

sentences.zh: 除州治中，卒官。

translations.literal: He was appointed Chief Clerk of the province and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Chief Clerk of the province and died in that office.

sentences.zh: 忱弟懷，字士仁。

translations.literal: Chen's younger brother Huai, styled Shiren.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's younger brother was Huai, styled Shiren.

sentences.zh: 任城王雲郎中令、大將軍從事中郎，授中散。

translations.literal: Director of Retainers for Prince Yun of Rencheng, Attendant-in-Ordinary to the Grand General; appointed Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Director of Retainers to Prince Yun of Rencheng and Attendant-in-Ordinary to the Grand General, then was appointed Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 恬淡退靜，不競世利，在散輩十八年不易官。

translations.literal: Tranquil and retiring, quiet and still, he did not compete for worldly profit; among the scattered ranks for eighteen years he did not change office.
translations.idiomatic: Tranquil and retiring, he did not compete for worldly profit; among the scattered ranks for eighteen years he did not change office.

sentences.zh: 太和中，除太尉東陽王諮議參軍而卒。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era he was appointed Consultant and Adjutant to the Grand Marshal, Prince Dongyang of the Ministry of Works, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taihe era he was appointed Consultant to Prince Dongyang, Grand Marshal of the Ministry of Works, and died in that post.

sentences.zh: 子綽，字僧裕。

translations.literal: His son Chuo, styled Sengyu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chuo, whose courtesy name was Sengyu.

sentences.zh: 少孤，恭敏自立。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he was respectful and keen and established himself.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he was respectful, keen, and self-reliant.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺，腰帶十圍，沉雅有度量，博涉經史。

translations.literal: His body was eight chi tall, his waist girdle ten wei around; he was deep and elegant with measure, broadly versed in the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: He stood eight chi tall with a ten-wei waist; deep, elegant, and measured, he was broadly versed in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 太和十五年拜奉朝請、太尉法曹行參軍，尋兼尚書祠部郎。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Taihe he was appointed Court Gentleman for the Imperial Audience and Acting Adjutant in the Law Section of the Grand Marshal; soon he was concurrently Gentleman of the Imperial Ancestral Temples Section of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe year fifteen he was appointed Court Gentleman and Acting Adjutant in the Grand Marshal's Law Section; soon he was also Gentleman of the Ancestral Temples Section.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去職。

translations.literal: Because of his mother's mourning he left office.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 久之，除治書侍御史，轉洛陽令。

translations.literal: After long time he was appointed Attending Secretary and transferred to Magistrate of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was appointed Attending Secretary and became Magistrate of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 綽為政強直，不避豪貴，邑人憚之。

translations.literal: Chuo in governing was forceful and upright, not avoiding the powerful and noble; the district people feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo governed with forceful uprightness and did not avoid the powerful; the people of the district feared him.

sentences.zh: 又詔參議律令。

translations.literal: Another edict ordered him to deliberate on laws and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: He was also ordered to deliberate on laws and ordinances.

sentences.zh: 遷長兼國子博士，行潁川郡事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Senior Erudite of the Imperial University concurrently and acted as Administrator of Yingchuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Senior Erudite of the Imperial University and acted as Administrator of Yingchuan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 詔假節，行涇州刺史。

translations.literal: An edict granted him the staff of authority and he acted as Regional Inspector of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted him the staff of authority and he served as Acting Regional Inspector of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 延昌初，遷尚書右丞，參議壬子曆。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yanchang he was transferred to Right Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat and deliberated on the Renzi calendar.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yanchang he became Right Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat and joined deliberation on the Renzi calendar.

sentences.zh: 肅宗初，司徒清河王懌司馬、冠軍，又隨懌遷太尉司馬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Suzong's reign he was Marshal to Prince Yi of Qinghe, Minister of Works, and Champion; again following Yi he was transferred to Marshal of the Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Suzong's reign he was Marshal to Prince Yi of Qinghe and Champion, then followed Yi as Marshal of the Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 其年秋，大乘賊起於冀州，都督元遙率眾討之，詔綽兼散騎常侍，持節，以白虎幡軍前招慰。

translations.literal: That autumn the Mahayana bandits rose in Jizhou; Commander-in-Chief Yuan Yao led troops to attack them; an edict made Chuo concurrently Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, Bearer of the Staff, to precede the army with the white-tiger banner to summon and comfort.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Mahayana rebels rose in Jizhou; Commander Yuan Yao led troops against them; Chuo was made Regular Attendant with the staff to precede the army with the white-tiger banner and summon surrender.

sentences.zh: 綽信著州里，降者相尋。

translations.literal: Chuo's trust was renowned in the commandery and district; those who surrendered followed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo's trust was renowned in the region and surrenderers came in succession.

sentences.zh: 軍還，除汲郡太守，固辭不拜。

translations.literal: When the army returned he was appointed Administrator of Ji Commandery but firmly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned he was appointed Administrator of Ji Commandery but firmly declined the post.

sentences.zh: 御史中尉元匡奏高聰及綽等朋附高肇，詔並原罪。

translations.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Yuan Kuang memorialized that Gao Cong and Chuo and others cliqued with Gao Zhao; an edict pardoned all their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Director Yuan Kuang memorialized that Gao Cong, Chuo, and others had cliqued with Gao Zhao; an edict pardoned them all.

sentences.zh: 俄行滎陽郡事，以本將軍出除豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he acted as Administrator of Xingyang Commandery; with his original rank as general he went out and was appointed Regional Inspector of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he administered Xingyang Commandery, then left office as Regional Inspector of Yuzhou with his original general's rank.

sentences.zh: 為政清平，抑強扶弱，百姓愛之，流民歸附者二千餘戶。

translations.literal: In governing he was clear and level, suppressing the strong and supporting the weak; the people loved him, and more than two thousand households of displaced persons attached themselves.
translations.idiomatic: His government was clear and level; he suppressed the strong and aided the weak; the people loved him and more than two thousand displaced households attached themselves.

sentences.zh: 遷後將軍、并州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Rear and Regional Inspector of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: This man was transferred to General of the Rear and Regional Inspector of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 正光三年冬，暴疾卒，年四十八。

translations.literal: In winter of the third year of Zhengguang he died suddenly of illness, aged forty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In winter of Zhengguang year three he died suddenly of illness at forty-eight.

sentences.zh: 四年九月，詔贈安東將軍、冀州刺史，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fourth year an edict posthumously gave General Who Pacifies the East and Regional Inspector of Jizhou; posthumous name Jian.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the fourth year an edict posthumously made him General Who Pacifies the East and Regional Inspector of Jizhou with posthumous name Jian.

sentences.zh: 子炳，字仲彰。

translations.literal: His son Bing, styled Zhongzhang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bing, whose courtesy name was Zhongzhang.

sentences.zh: 太尉行參軍，稍遷征虜將軍、開府掾。

translations.literal: Acting Adjutant to the Grand Marshal; gradually transferred to General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Staff Officer of the Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Acting Adjutant to the Grand Marshal, then rose to General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Staff Officer of the Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 早卒。

translations.literal: He died young.
translations.idiomatic: He died in youth.

sentences.zh: 允弟推，字仲讓，小名檀越，早有名譽。

translations.literal: Yun's younger brother Tui, styled Zhongrang, childhood name Tan'yue, early had fame and reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Yun's younger brother Tui, styled Zhongrang, childhood name Tan'yue, was early famed.

sentences.zh: 太延中，以前後南使不稱，妙簡行人。

translations.literal: In the Taiyan era, because successive southern envoys were unsatisfactory, envoys were superbly selected.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taiyan era, because successive southern envoys had proved unsatisfactory, envoys were carefully selected.

sentences.zh: 游雅薦推應選。

translations.literal: You Ya recommended Tui as fit for selection.
translations.idiomatic: You Ya recommended Tui as qualified.

sentences.zh: 詔兼散騎常侍使劉義隆，南人稱其才辯。

translations.literal: An edict made him concurrently Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and envoy to Liu Yilong; the southerners praised his talent and eloquence.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made him Regular Attendant and envoy to Liu Yilong; southerners praised his talent and eloquence.

sentences.zh: 遇疾卒於建業。

translations.literal: He met illness and died at Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill and died at Jianye.

sentences.zh: 朝廷悼惜之。

translations.literal: The court mourned and regretted him.
translations.idiomatic: The court mourned and regretted his loss.

sentences.zh: 喪還，贈輔國將軍、臨邑子，諡曰恭，賜命服衣冠。

translations.literal: When the coffin returned he was posthumously given General Who Assists the State and Viscount of Linyi; posthumous name Gong; command robes and cap were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: When his coffin returned he was posthumously made General Who Assists the State and Viscount of Linyi, posthumous name Gong, with command robes bestowed.

sentences.zh: 允為之作誄。

translations.literal: Yun composed a dirge for him.
translations.idiomatic: Yun wrote a dirge for him.

sentences.zh: 推弟燮，字季和，小字淳于，亦有文才。

translations.literal: Tui's younger brother Xie, styled Jihe, childhood name Chunyu, also had literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: Tui's younger brother Xie, courtesy name Jihe, childhood name Chunyu, likewise possessed literary talent.

sentences.zh: 世祖每詔徵，辭疾不應。

translations.literal: Each time Emperor Shizu issued an edict to summon him, he declined on grounds of illness and did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Emperor Shizu summoned him he pleaded illness and did not respond.

sentences.zh: 恒譏笑允屈折久宦，栖泊京邑。

translations.literal: He constantly mocked Yun for bending and long serving in office, dwelling and mooring in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He constantly mocked Yun for bending himself in long service and dwelling in the capital.

sentences.zh: 常從容於家。

translations.literal: He was always at ease at home.
translations.idiomatic: He lived at ease in his own home.

sentences.zh: 州辟主簿。

translations.literal: The province summoned him as Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: The province recruited him as Chief Clerk.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He passed away.

sentences.zh: 孫市賓，奉朝請、冀州京兆王愉城局參軍。

translations.literal: Grandson Shibin, Court Gentleman for the Imperial Audience and Adjutant in the City Bureau of Prince Yu of Jingzhao in Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Grandson Shibin, Court Gentleman and Adjutant in the City Bureau of Prince Yu of Jingzhao in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 愉構逆，市賓逃歸京。

translations.literal: Yu plotted rebellion; Shibin fled back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu plotted rebellion Shibin fled back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 後除青州安南府司馬。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Military Administrator of the Pacify-the-South Headquarters in Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Military Administrator of the Pacify-the-South Headquarters in Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 永熙中，冠軍將軍、開府從事中郎。

translations.literal: In the Yongxi era, General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Attendant-in-Ordinary to the Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongxi era he was General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Attendant-in-Ordinary to the Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 始神䴥中，允與從叔濟、族兄毗及同郡李金俱被徵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenqi, Yun together with his paternal uncle Ji, his clan elder cousin Pi, and Li Jin of the same commandery were all summoned.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Shenqi, Yun together with his paternal uncle Ji, clan cousin Pi, and Li Jin of the same commandery were all summoned.

sentences.zh: 濟，字叔民。

translations.literal: Ji, styled Shumin.
translations.idiomatic: Ji, whose courtesy name was Shumin.

sentences.zh: 初補中書博士，又為楚王傅。

translations.literal: At first he was appointed Erudite of the Central Secretariat; he was also Tutor to the Prince of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: At first he was Erudite of the Central Secretariat and Tutor to the Prince of Chu.

sentences.zh: 真君中，假員外常侍，賜爵浮陽子，使於劉義隆。

translations.literal: In the Zhenjun era he was Acting Regular Attendant Outside the Body, ennobled Viscount of Fuyang, and sent as envoy to Liu Yilong.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenjun era he was Acting Regular Attendant, ennobled Viscount of Fuyang, and envoy to Liu Yilong.

sentences.zh: 世祖臨江，於行所除盱眙太守，後超授游擊將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu crossed the Yangzi, at the marching camp he was appointed Administrator of Xuyi; later he was exceptionally appointed General Who Roams in Attack.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu crossed the Yangzi he was appointed Administrator of Xuyi at the marching camp; later he was exceptionally made General Who Roams in Attack.

sentences.zh: 尋出除滄水太守。

translations.literal: Soon he went out and was appointed Administrator of Cangshui.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Administrator of Cangshui.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十七。

translations.literal: He died, aged sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 贈鎮遠將軍、冀州刺史，諡曰宣。

translations.literal: Posthumously given General Who Pacifies the Distant and Regional Inspector of Jizhou; posthumous name Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the Distant and Regional Inspector of Jizhou with posthumous name Xuan.

sentences.zh: 子矯，襲。

translations.literal: His son Jiao inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jiao succeeded.

sentences.zh: 卒，子師襲。

translations.literal: He died; his son Shi inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He died and his son Shi succeeded.

sentences.zh: 師，字孝則，有學識。

translations.literal: Shi, styled Xiaozi, had learning and knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: Shi, whose courtesy name was Xiaozi, possessed learning and discernment.

sentences.zh: 歷詹事丞、太子舍人、尚書主客郎。

translations.literal: He served as Assistant in the Household of the Heir Apparent, Gentleman Attendant of the Heir Apparent, and Gentleman of the Hosts Section of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Assistant in the Heir Apparent's Household, Gentleman Attendant of the Heir Apparent, and Gentleman of the Hosts Section.

sentences.zh: 轉通直散騎侍郎、從事正員郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Regular Attendant of Direct Communication and Attending Regular Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: This man was transferred to Regular Attendant of Direct Communication and Attending Regular Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 累遷光祿少卿，行涇州事。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Palace Masters and acted as Administrator of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Director of the Palace Masters and administered Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈龍驤將軍、河州刺史。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously given General of the Dragon Cavalry and Regional Inspector of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made General of the Dragon Cavalry and Regional Inspector of Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 子和仁，字德舒，襲。

translations.literal: His son Heren, styled Deshu, inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Heren, styled Deshu, succeeded.

sentences.zh: 釋褐員外散騎侍郎，領殿中御史。

translations.literal: On first appointment he was Outside-the-Body Gentleman of Scattered Cavalry and concurrently Director of the Palace Censors.
translations.idiomatic: On entering service he was Outside-the-Body Gentleman of Scattered Cavalry and concurrently Director of the Palace Censors.

sentences.zh: 少清簡，有文才，曾為五言詩贈太尉屬盧仲宣，仲宣甚歎重之。

translations.literal: Young he was pure and simple, with literary talent; he once composed a five-character poem presented to Lu Zhongxuan, Attendant of the Grand Marshal, and Zhongxuan greatly praised and valued him.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was pure and simple with literary talent; he once presented a five-character poem to Lu Zhongxuan of the Grand Marshal's staff, who greatly prized it.

sentences.zh: 常有高尚之志。

translations.literal: He constantly had elevated aspirations.
translations.idiomatic: He constantly cherished elevated aspirations.

sentences.zh: 後為洛州錄事參軍，不赴，服餌於汲郡白鹿山。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Recorder of Luozhou but did not take up the post; he took elixirs on White Deer Mountain in Ji Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later appointed Recorder of Luozhou he did not take up the post but took elixirs on White Deer Mountain in Ji Commandery.

sentences.zh: 未幾卒，時人悼惜之。

translations.literal: Before long he died; people of the time mourned and regretted him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died, to the regret of his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 和仁弟德偉，武定末，東宮齋帥。

translations.literal: Heren's younger brother Dewei, at the end of Wuding, was Director of Provisions in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Heren's younger brother Dewei served at the end of Wuding as Director of Provisions in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 矯弟遵，自有傳。

translations.literal: Jiao's younger brother Zun has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao's younger brother Zun is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 毗，字子翼，鄉邑稱為長者。

translations.literal: Pi, styled Ziyi, was called an elder by his village and district.
translations.idiomatic: Pi, styled Ziyi, was called an elder in his home district.

sentences.zh: 官至從事中郎。

translations.literal: He reached the office of Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 孫當，尚書郎。

translations.literal: Grandson Dang, Gentleman of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Dang was Gentleman of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈樂陵太守，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously given Administrator of Leling; posthumous name Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Administrator of Leling with posthumous name Gong.

sentences.zh: 初，允所引劉模者，長樂信都人也。

translations.literal: At first, Liu Mo whom Yun introduced was a man of Xindu in Changle.
translations.idiomatic: At first Liu Mo, whom Yun introduced, was from Xindu in Changle.

sentences.zh: 少時竊遊河表，遂至河南，尋復潛歸。

translations.literal: In youth he secretly traveled beyond the River and reached Henan; soon he secretly returned.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he secretly traveled south of the River to Henan, then secretly returned.

sentences.zh: 頗涉經籍，微有注疏之用。

translations.literal: He was fairly versed in the classics and had slight use for commentary and gloss.
translations.idiomatic: He was fairly versed in the classics and useful for commentary and gloss.

sentences.zh: 允領祕書、典著作，選為校書郎。

translations.literal: Yun headed the Palace Library and directed compilation; Mo was chosen as Proofreader.
translations.idiomatic: When Yun headed the Palace Library and directed compilation, Mo was chosen Proofreader.

sentences.zh: 允修撰國記，與俱緝著。

translations.literal: Yun compiled the National Record and together with him collated and composed.
translations.idiomatic: Yun compiled the National Record and Mo collated and composed with him.

sentences.zh: 常令模持管籥，每日同入史閣，接膝對筵，屬述時事。

translations.literal: He often had Mo hold the brush and keys; daily they entered the History Pavilion together, knees touching, mats facing, composing current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He often had Mo hold brush and keys; daily they entered the History Pavilion together, knee to knee, composing current affairs.

sentences.zh: 允年已九十，[13]目手稍衰，多遣模執筆而指授裁斷之。

translations.literal: Yun's years already reached ninety,[13] eyes and hands gradually declined; he mostly sent Mo to hold the brush while he directed and judged.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was already ninety,[13] his eyes and hands gradually failing; he mostly had Mo hold the brush while he directed and judged.

sentences.zh: 如此者五六歲。

translations.literal: Thus for five or six years.
translations.idiomatic: This continued for five or six years.

sentences.zh: 允所成篇卷，著論上下，模預有功焉。

translations.literal: Of the chapters and scrolls Yun completed, discourses upper and lower, Mo shared in the merit.
translations.idiomatic: Of the chapters Yun completed and his discourses upper and lower, Mo had a share in the merit.

sentences.zh: 太和初，模遷中書博士，與李彪為僚友，並相愛好。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe, Mo was transferred to Erudite of the Central Secretariat; with Li Biao he was a colleague and friend, and both loved one another.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taihe Mo was transferred to Erudite of the Central Secretariat; he and Li Biao were colleagues and close friends.

sentences.zh: 至於訓導國冑，甄明風範，遠不及彪也。

translations.literal: As for instructing and guiding the imperial scions and discerning and clarifying models of conduct, he was far inferior to Biao.
translations.idiomatic: In instructing imperial scions and clarifying models of conduct he was far inferior to Biao.

sentences.zh: 出除潁州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out and was appointed Regional Inspector of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He left office as Regional Inspector of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: [14]王肅之歸闕，路經懸瓠，羇旅窮悴，時人莫識。

translations.literal: [14]When Wang Su returned to the court, his route passed Xuan'e; he was a traveler in poverty and emaciation; people of the time did not recognize him.
translations.idiomatic: [14]When Wang Su returned to court his route passed Xuan'e; a traveler in poverty and emaciation, he was unrecognized.

sentences.zh: 模獨給所須，弔待以禮。

translations.literal: Mo alone supplied what was needed and condoled and received him with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Mo alone supplied his needs and received him with proper ritual.

sentences.zh: 肅深感其意。

translations.literal: Su deeply felt his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Su was deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 及肅臨豫州，模猶在郡，微報復之，由是為新蔡太守。

translations.literal: When Su took charge of Yuzhou, Mo was still in the commandery; he slightly repaid the favor and thereby became Administrator of Xincai.
translations.idiomatic: When Su governed Yuzhou Mo was still in the commandery; Su repaid the favor and had him made Administrator of Xincai.

sentences.zh: 在二郡積十年，寬猛相濟，頗有治稱。

translations.literal: In the two commanderies for accumulated ten years, lenience and severity complemented each other; he had considerable reputation in governing.
translations.idiomatic: In two commanderies over ten years he balanced lenience and severity and won a considerable reputation for governance.

sentences.zh: 正始元年，復出為陳留太守。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengshi he again went out as Administrator of Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengshi year one he again went out as Administrator of Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 時年七十餘矣，而飾老隱年，昧禁自效。

translations.literal: He was already more than seventy, yet he adorned old age and concealed his years, dimly violating the prohibition and taking effect on his own.
translations.idiomatic: Though already over seventy he concealed his age and took office in violation of the prohibition.

sentences.zh: 遂家於南潁川，不復歸其舊鄉矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon he made his home in southern Yingchuan and did not return to his old village.
translations.idiomatic: He then made his home in southern Yingchuan and never returned to his old village.

sentences.zh: 子懷恕，聰率多□。

translations.literal: His son Huaishu was intelligent and quick, with many□.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huaishu was clever and quick, with many talents□.

sentences.zh: 甚收潁川情和。

translations.literal: He greatly won the affection and harmony of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: This man greatly won the affection and harmony of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 至襄威將軍、本州冠軍府功曹參軍。

translations.literal: He reached General Who Displays Might and Merit Officer in the Champion Headquarters of his native province.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to General Who Displays Might and Merit Officer in his province's Champion Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 懷恕弟懷遜，頗解醫術。

translations.literal: Huaishu's younger brother Huaiyun was fairly skilled in medical arts.
translations.idiomatic: Huaishu's younger brother Huaiyun was fairly skilled in medicine.

sentences.zh: 歷位給事中。

translations.literal: He served as Attendant Within.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Attendant Within.

sentences.zh: 卒於左軍將軍、鎮遠將軍。

translations.literal: He died holding the offices of General of the Left Army and General Who Pacifies the Distant.
translations.idiomatic: He died holding the posts of General of the Left Army and General Who Pacifies the Distant.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：依仁遊藝，執義守哲，其司空高允乎？

translations.literal: The historian says: Relying on benevolence and roaming in the arts, holding righteousness and guarding wisdom—is this not Director of Works Gao Yun?
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: By benevolence and the arts, by righteousness and wisdom—was this not Gao Yun, Director of Works?

sentences.zh: 蹈危禍之機，抗雷電之氣，處死夷然，忘身濟物，卒悟明主，保己全身。

translations.literal: He trod the mechanism of peril and calamity, resisted the qi of thunder and lightning; facing death he was level, forgot self to aid things; ultimately he awakened the enlightened ruler and preserved himself whole.
translations.idiomatic: He trod peril and calamity, resisted thunder and lightning; facing death he was level, forgot self to aid others, and ultimately awakened the enlightened ruler and preserved himself whole.

sentences.zh: 自非體隣知命，鑒照窮達，亦何能以若此？

translations.literal: Unless his person neighbored knowledge of fate and his mirror illumined extremity and attainment, how could he have been like this?
translations.idiomatic: Unless one neighbored knowledge of fate and mirrored extremity and attainment, how could one be like this?

sentences.zh: 宜其光寵四世，終享百齡，有魏以來，斯人而已。

translations.literal: It was fitting that glory and favor extended through four generations and he ultimately enjoyed a hundred years; since Wei began, only this man.
translations.idiomatic: It was fitting that glory extended through four generations and he enjoyed a hundred years; since Wei began, only this man.

sentences.zh: 僧裕學治有聞，聿修之義也。

translations.literal: Sengyu's learning and governance had reputation; this is the meaning of continuing the line.
translations.idiomatic: Sengyu's learning and governance won renown—the meaning of continuing the family line.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation Notes
translations.idiomatic: Textual Collation Notes

sentences.zh: 冬十月日在尾箕 北史卷三一高允傳「日」下有「旦」字。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the sun was in Tail and Winnowing Basket. Book of Northern Wei, juan 31, Biography of Gao Yun: below "sun" is the character "dawn."
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the sun was in Tail and Winnowing Basket. Northern Wei History, juan 31, Biography of Gao Yun: below "sun" is the character "dawn."

sentences.zh: 按下云「昏沒於申南」，則這裏當有「旦」字。

translations.literal: Pressing down it says "at dusk it set south of Shen," so here there ought to be the character "dawn."
translations.idiomatic: Since below it says "at dusk it set south of Shen," the character "dawn" should appear here.

sentences.zh: 李虛 北史卷三一「虛」作「靈」。

translations.literal: Li Xu. Book of Northern Wei, juan 31: "Xu" is written "Ling."
translations.idiomatic: Li Xu. Northern Wei History, juan 31: "Xu" is written "Ling."

sentences.zh: 按卷四九李靈傳不載此事。

translations.literal: Pressing the Biography of Li Ling in juan 49, this matter is not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: The Biography of Li Ling in juan 49 does not record this matter.

sentences.zh: 卷五二胡方回傳、卷五四游雅傳、卷一一一刑罰志都不載李靈或李虛參加這次律令的修定。

translations.literal: Biographies of Hu Fanghui in juan 52, You Ya in juan 54, and the Punishments Monograph in juan 111 none record Li Ling or Li Xu participating in this drafting of laws.
translations.idiomatic: The biographies of Hu Fanghui, You Ya, and the Punishments Monograph do not record Li Ling or Li Xu participating in this legal drafting.

sentences.zh: 但李靈這時是中書侍郎，同時未見有侍郎「李虛」其人，疑「虛」是「靈」之訛。

translations.literal: But Li Ling at this time was Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Central Secretariat, and at the same time no Attendant-in-Ordinary "Li Xu" is seen; I suspect "Xu" is an error for "Ling."
translations.idiomatic: Li Ling was then Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Central Secretariat, and no "Li Xu" is attested; "Xu" is likely an error for "Ling."

sentences.zh: 若勤之則畝益三斗不勤則畝損三斗 諸本及北史「斗」並作「升」，御覽卷四五四

translations.literal: If diligent then per mu three dou more gain; if not diligent then per mu three dou less—All editions and Northern Wei History juan 31 read "sheng" for "dou"; Imperial Readings juan 454
translations.idiomatic: If diligent, three dou more per mu; if not, three dou less—all editions and Northern Wei History juan 31 read "sheng" for "dou"; Imperial Readings juan 454

sentences.zh: 〈二０八七頁〉

translations.literal: 〈page 2087〉

sentences.zh: 作「斗」。

translations.literal: reads "dou."
translations.idiomatic: has "dou."

sentences.zh: 按漢書卷二四食貨志引李悝說「畝益三升」，臣瓚和顏師古都說「升」當作「斗」。

translations.literal: Pressing the Treatise on Food and Money in Hanshu juan 24 citing Li Kui: "per mu three sheng more," both Chen Zan and Yan Shigu say "sheng" should be "dou."
translations.idiomatic: Hanshu, Treatise on Food and Money, citing Li Kui's "three sheng more per mu": Chen Zan and Yan Shigu both say "sheng" should be "dou."

sentences.zh: 這裏稱「百里則田三萬七千頃」，又說「方百里損益之率為粟二百二十二萬斛」。

translations.literal: Here it says "a hundred li then fields thirty-seven thousand qing," and also "for a hundred li square the rate of gain and loss is 2,220,000 hu of grain."
translations.idiomatic: Here it says "within a hundred li, fields total thirty-seven thousand qing," and "for a hundred-li square the gain-and-loss rate is 2,220,000 hu of grain."

sentences.zh: 每畝損益共六斗，三萬七千頃正得二百二十二萬斛。

translations.literal: Per mu six dou total gain and loss; thirty-seven thousand qing exactly yields 2,220,000 hu.
translations.idiomatic: Six dou gain and loss per mu; thirty-seven thousand qing yields exactly 2,220,000 hu.

sentences.zh: 知作「斗」是，今據御覽改。

translations.literal: Knowing "dou" is correct; now altered according to Imperial Readings.
translations.idiomatic: Since "dou" is correct, the text is now altered according to Imperial Readings.

sentences.zh: 又俳優鄙藝 北史卷三一「藝」作「䙝」。

translations.literal: Moreover actors' vulgar arts. Book of Northern Wei, juan 31: "arts" is written "the cited text."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover actors' vulgar arts. Northern Wei History, juan 31: "arts" is written "the cited text."

sentences.zh: 「藝」字當是形訛，但也可通，今不改。

translations.literal: The character "arts" is likely a graphic error, but it can also pass; not altered now.
translations.idiomatic: The character "arts" is likely a graphic error but can pass; it is not altered here.

sentences.zh: 征南大將軍從事中郎勃海李欽道賜 北史卷三一「欽」作「金」。

translations.literal: Attendant-in-Ordinary to the General Who Conquers the South Li Qin styled Daoci of Bohai. Book of Northern Wei, juan 31: "Qin" is written "Jin."
translations.idiomatic: Li Qin of Bohai, styled Daoci, Attendant-in-Ordinary to the General Who Conquers the South. Northern Wei History juan 31: "Qin" is written "Jin."

sentences.zh: 按下文說允與「同郡李金同被徵，卷七二李叔虎傳也說「從祖金，世祖神䴥中與高允俱被徵」，疑作「金」是。

translations.literal: Pressing below it says Yun with "Li Jin of the same commandery was summoned together," and Biography of Li Shuhu in juan 72 says "his collateral ancestor Jin, in Emperor Shizu's Shenqi together with Gao Yun was summoned"—I suspect "Jin" is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Below it says Li Jin of the same commandery was summoned with Yun; Biography of Li Shuhu, juan 72, says collateral ancestor Jin was summoned with Gao Yun in Shenqi—"Jin" is likely correct.

sentences.zh: 中書郎中即丘子趙郡李遐仲熙 張森楷云：「李順傳

translations.literal: Gentleman within the Central Secretariat, Viscount of Qiqiu, Li Xia styled Zhongxi of Zhao Commandery. Zhang Senkai says: "Biography of Li Shun
translations.idiomatic: Gentleman of the Central Secretariat, Viscount of Qiqiu, Li Xia of Zhao Commandery, styled Zhongxi. Zhang Senkai remarks in the Biography of Li Shun

sentences.zh: 〈卷三六〉

translations.literal: 〈juan 36〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈juan 36〉

sentences.zh: 有族弟熙，字仲熙，神䴥中，與高允同被徵，拜中書博士，轉侍郎，封元氏子。

translations.literal: has a clan younger brother Xi, styled Zhongxi; in Shenqi together with Gao Yun was summoned, appointed Erudite of the Central Secretariat, transferred to Attendant-in-Ordinary, enfeoffed Viscount of Yuanshi.
translations.idiomatic: has a clan younger brother Xi, styled Zhongxi; summoned with Gao Yun in Shenqi, appointed Erudite of the Central Secretariat, transferred to Attendant-in-Ordinary, enfeoffed Viscount of Yuanshi.

sentences.zh: 與此不同。

translations.literal: This differs from this.
translations.idiomatic: This differs from the present text.

sentences.zh: 以下文徵士頌稱『熙雖中夭』觀之，則『熙』是而『遐』非。」

translations.literal: Viewing the Eulogy for Summoned Scholars below that says "Though Xi died young," then "Xi" is correct and "Xia" is not."
translations.idiomatic: The Eulogy for Summoned Scholars says "Though Xi died young"—"Xi" is correct and "Xia" is not.

sentences.zh: 按「中書郎中」下「中」字當是衍文。

translations.literal: Below "Gentleman within the Central Secretariat" the character "within" is likely superfluous.
translations.idiomatic: Below "Gentleman within the Central Secretariat" the character "within" is likely superfluous.

sentences.zh: 中書郎武恒子河間邢穎宗敬 張森楷北史校勘記云：「邢巒傳

translations.literal: Gentleman of the Central Secretariat, Viscount of Wuheng, Xing Ying styled Zongjing of Hejian. Zhang Senkai's Collation Notes for Northern Wei History say: "Biography of Xing Luan
translations.idiomatic: Gentleman of the Central Secretariat, Viscount of Wuheng, Xing Ying styled Zongjing of Hejian. Zhang Senkai's Collation Notes for Northern Wei History: "Biography of Xing Luan

sentences.zh: 〈卷六五〉

translations.literal: 〈juan 65〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈juan 65〉

sentences.zh: 稱穎假平城子使宋，不云封『武恒子』，且地志亦無武恒縣，或『武垣』誤也。」

translations.literal: says Ying was Acting Viscount of Pingcheng and envoy to Song, and does not say enfeoffed "Viscount of Wuheng," and the Treatise on Geography also has no Wuheng County—or "Wuheng" is an error for "Wuyuan."
translations.idiomatic: says Ying was Acting Viscount of Pingcheng and envoy to Song, not enfeoffed "Viscount of Wuheng," and the geography has no Wuheng County—or "Wuheng" is an error for "Wuyuan."

sentences.zh: 太平太守平原子雁門李熙士元 北史卷三一「平原」作「原平」。

translations.literal: Administrator of Taiping, Viscount of Pingyuan, Li Xi styled Shiyuan of Yanmen. Book of Northern Wei, juan 31: "Pingyuan" is written "Yuanping."
translations.idiomatic: Li Xi of Yanmen, styled Shiyuan, Administrator of Taiping and Viscount of Pingyuan. Northern Wei History juan 31: "Pingyuan" is written "Yuanping."

sentences.zh: 按當時封邑，往往取本郡地名，雁門有原平縣，疑作「原平」是。

translations.literal: Pressing enfeoffments of the time often took the native commandery's place-name; Yanmen had Yuanping County—I suspect "Yuanping" is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Enfeoffments often took local place-names; Yanmen had Yuanping County—"Yuanping" is likely correct.

sentences.zh: 僭馮影附 諸本「馮」作「憑」，北史卷三一作「馮」。

translations.literal: The usurper Feng's shadow attached. All editions read "Feng" as "Ping"; Book of Northern Wei, juan 31, reads "Feng."
translations.idiomatic: The usurper Feng cast his shadow. All editions read "Feng" as "Ping"; Northern Wei History juan 31 reads "Feng."

sentences.zh: 按這幾句是說玄出使事。

translations.literal: Pressing: these lines speak of Xuan's mission.
translations.idiomatic: These lines concern Xuan's diplomatic missions.

sentences.zh: 玄出使劉宋，見本書卷四七、北史卷三０盧玄傳，又曾出使北燕馮弘，則魏書不載，只見北史盧玄傳。

translations.literal: Xuan went as envoy to Liu Song—see this book juan 47 and Northern Wei History juan 30, Biography of Lu Xuan; he also went to Northern Yan's Feng Hong, which Wei Shu does not record, seen only in Northern Wei History, Biography of Lu Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan went as envoy to Liu Song (see juan 47 and Northern Wei History juan 30); he also went to Feng Hong of Northern Yan, unrecorded in Wei Shu but in Northern Wei History.

sentences.zh: 「僭馮」指馮弘，與下「劉以和親」句相對。

translations.literal: "Usurper Feng" refers to Feng Hong, paired with the line below "Liu thereby harmonized through marriage."
translations.idiomatic: "Usurper Feng" refers to Feng Hong, paired with "Liu thereby harmonized through marriage" below.

sentences.zh: 「憑」字訛，今據北史改。

translations.literal: The character "Ping" is erroneous; now altered according to Northern Wei History.
translations.idiomatic: The character "Ping" is erroneous; altered according to Northern Wei History.

sentences.zh: 舉之克諧 諸本及北史「舉」作「與」，獨百衲本作「舉」。

translations.literal: They were raised and could harmonize. All editions and Northern Wei History read "raise" as "with"; only the Baona edition reads "raise."
translations.idiomatic: They were raised and could harmonize. All editions and Northern Wei History read "raise" as "with"; only the Baona edition reads "raise."

sentences.zh: 按李慈銘云：「『與』，宋本作『舉』。」

translations.literal: Pressing Li Ciming says: "'With,' the Song edition reads 'raise.'"
translations.idiomatic: Li Ciming says: "'With'—the Song edition reads 'raise.'"

sentences.zh: 則李所見宋本同百衲本。

translations.literal: Then the Song edition Li saw agrees with the Baona edition.
translations.idiomatic: The Song edition Li saw agrees with the Baona edition.

sentences.zh: 這句上文云「君臣相遇，理實難偕」，接以「昔因朝命，舉之克諧」，「舉」即指徵舉，不誤。

translations.literal: Above it says "Ruler and minister met, principle and reality hard to join," followed by "Formerly because of court command, they were raised and could harmonize"—"raise" refers to the summons and is not wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Above: "Ruler and minister met, principle and reality hard to join"; then "Formerly by court command they were raised and harmonized"—"raise" means the summons and is correct.

sentences.zh: 今從百衲本。

translations.literal: Now following the Baona edition.
translations.idiomatic: The text now follows the Baona edition.

sentences.zh: 調酒之頌 冊府卷五二三

translations.literal: Songs praising wine. Imperial Digest juan 523
translations.idiomatic: Songs praising wine, per the Imperial Digest, juan 523

sentences.zh: 〈六二四七頁〉

translations.literal: 〈page 6247〉

sentences.zh: 「調」作「諷」，「酒」下有「德」字。

translations.literal: "Tune" is written "satire," and below "wine" has the character "virtue."
translations.idiomatic: The text reads "tune" as "satire," and after "wine" adds the character "virtue."

sentences.zh: 疑是。

translations.literal: I suspect this is correct.
translations.idiomatic: This is likely correct.

sentences.zh: 論雜解 按「論雜解」不可解，北史卷三一無「論」字，當連上文作「毛詩拾遺雜解」。

translations.literal: Miscellaneous explanations. Pressing: "Miscellaneous explanations" is not intelligible; Book of Northern Wei, juan 31, lacks "discourse," which should join the above as "Mao's Odes Gleanings, miscellaneous explanations."
translations.idiomatic: "Miscellaneous explanations" is unclear; Northern Wei History juan 31 lacks "discourse," which should join above as "Mao's Odes Gleanings, miscellaneous explanations."

sentences.zh: 但也可能「論」下脫「語」字。

translations.literal: But it is also possible the character "discourse" below is missing "language."
translations.idiomatic: It is also possible "discourse" is missing the character "language" below.

sentences.zh: 允年已九十 張森楷云：「允以太和十一年卒，年九十八。

translations.literal: Yun's years already ninety. Zhang Senkai says: "Yun died in the eleventh year of Taihe, aged ninety-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Yun's years already ninety. Zhang Senkai says: "Yun died Taihe year eleven, aged ninety-eight.

sentences.zh: 此敍在太和前，則未及九十也。

translations.literal: This narrative is before Taihe, so he had not yet reached ninety.
translations.idiomatic: This passage is set before Taihe, so he had not yet reached ninety.

sentences.zh: 疑『九』當為『八』，或『已』是『近』之誤。」

translations.literal: I suspect 'nine' should be 'eight,' or 'already' is an error for 'nearly.'"
translations.idiomatic: He suspects "nine" should be "eight," or "already" is an error for "nearly."

sentences.zh: 按傳稱允自中書監出任懷州刺史時，「年將九十」。

translations.literal: Pressing the biography says when Yun left office as Director of the Central Secretariat to become Regional Inspector of Huaizhou, "years nearly ninety."
translations.idiomatic: The biography says when Yun became Regional Inspector of Huaizhou, "years nearly ninety."

sentences.zh: 他典史事在官中書監時，下文又說「如此者五六歲」。

translations.literal: He managed historical affairs while Director of the Central Secretariat; below it also says "thus for five or six years."
translations.idiomatic: He managed historical affairs as Director of the Central Secretariat; below it says "thus for five or six years."

sentences.zh: 若允出任懷州時「年將九十」，則遷中書監時，必不及九十。

translations.literal: If at leaving for Huaizhou "years nearly ninety," then at transfer to Director of the Central Secretariat he must have been under ninety.
translations.idiomatic: If "nearly ninety" at Huaizhou, he must have been under ninety as Director of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 「九」疑是「八」之訛。

translations.literal: 'Nine' is suspected to be an error for 'eight.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Nine' is likely an error for 'eight.'

sentences.zh: 出除潁州刺史 汲本「州」作「川」，北史卷三一「潁州刺史」作「南潁川太守」。

translations.literal: He went out and was appointed Regional Inspector of Yingzhou. Jibu edition "zhou" is written "chuan"; Book of Northern Wei, juan 31: "Regional Inspector of Yingzhou" is written "Administrator of Southern Yingchuan."
translations.idiomatic: He went out as Regional Inspector of Yingzhou. Jibu edition: "zhou" written "chuan"; Northern Wei History juan 31: "Regional Inspector of Yingzhou" written "Administrator of Southern Yingchuan."

sentences.zh: 李慈銘、張森楷都以為當作「潁川太守」。

translations.literal: Li Ciming and Zhang Senkai both hold it should be "Administrator of Yingchuan."
translations.idiomatic: Li Ciming and Zhang Senkai both hold it should read "Administrator of Yingchuan."

sentences.zh: 按下文說王肅「臨豫州，模猶在郡」，又說：「由是為新蔡太守。

translations.literal: Pressing below it says when Wang Su "took charge of Yuzhou, Mo was still in the commandery," and also: "thereby became Administrator of Xincai.
translations.idiomatic: Below: when Wang Su "governed Yuzhou, Mo was still in the commandery," and "thereby became Administrator of Xincai.

sentences.zh: 在二郡，積十年。」

translations.literal: In the two commanderies, accumulated ten years."
translations.idiomatic: In two commanderies, ten years accumulated."

sentences.zh: 二郡即指新蔡和潁川或南潁川，分明是官潁川或南潁川太守，不是刺史。

translations.literal: The two commanderies refer to Xincai and Yingchuan or Southern Yingchuan—clearly he was Administrator of Yingchuan or Southern Yingchuan, not Regional Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: The two commanderies are Xincai and Yingchuan or Southern Yingchuan—clearly administrator, not regional inspector.

sentences.zh: 又潁川、新蔡屬豫州

translations.literal: Also Yingchuan and Xincai belonged to Yuzhou
translations.idiomatic: Yingchuan and Xincai both belonged to Yuzhou

sentences.zh: 〈卷一０六中地形志中〉

translations.literal: 〈Treatise on Geography, juan 106 middle〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Geography Treatise, juan 106, middle scroll〉

sentences.zh: 王肅是豫州刺史，才和劉模相關，若模作潁州刺史，王肅又如何能要他當新蔡太守。

translations.literal: Wang Su was Regional Inspector of Yuzhou, which is why he was connected with Liu Mo; if Mo were Regional Inspector of Ying, how could Wang Su make him Administrator of Xincai?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su was Regional Inspector of Yuzhou, hence connected with Mo; if Mo were Regional Inspector of Ying, how could Wang Su appoint him Administrator of Xincai?

sentences.zh: 而且潁州於天平初置，武定七年改鄭州

translations.literal: Moreover Yingzhou was established at the beginning of Tianping, changed to Zhengzhou in the seventh year of Wuding
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhou was established at Tianping's beginning, changed to Zhengzhou in Wuding year seven

sentences.zh: 〈見地形志中〉，

translations.literal: 〈see Treatise on Geography, middle〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈see Geography Treatise, middle scroll〉

sentences.zh: 太和年間地屬司州，根本沒有潁州。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era the territory belonged to Sizhou; fundamentally there was no Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taihe era the territory belonged to Sizhou; there was no Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 這裏汲本作「潁川」是，「刺史」也當作「太守」。

translations.literal: Here the Jibu edition's "Yingchuan" is correct; "Regional Inspector" should also be "Administrator."
translations.idiomatic: The Jibu edition's "Yingchuan" is correct; "Regional Inspector" should read "Administrator."

sentences.zh: 又當時司州也有潁川，是漢魏舊郡，豫州的潁川後置，相對於司州的潁川，故也稱「南潁川」。

translations.literal: Also Sizhou then had Yingchuan, the old Han-Wei commandery; Yuzhou's Yingchuan was later established, relative to Sizhou's Yingchuan, hence also called "Southern Yingchuan."
translations.idiomatic: Sizhou also had Yingchuan, the old Han-Wei commandery; Yuzhou's Yingchuan was later established, hence also "Southern Yingchuan" relative to Sizhou's.
